before.title: Port engine: bring a non-AXF app onto AmberX AXF (bake or rebuild)
before.detail:
Runs the ports that claude-project parks (pending items port-<name>, manifest x.port, plan in the project at _claude/memory/docs/port-to-axf.md). Brett chose: ask each time between the two ways.

- bake: keep the codebase, run axf init into it (react-ts / next-ts / android-compose), then move its look and chrome into asset@1 assets step by step (colour/style themes, menus, toolbars, nav, dialogs, layout with region slots); UI reads engine tokens only (THEMING.md). Old styles go as each piece moves.
- rebuild: new AXF app from the closest boilerplate (axf boilerplates), old code kept alongside as reference, rebuilt feature by feature on assets/libraries/plugins.

Deliver: axf port <dir> --mode bake|rebuild (analysis report: what maps to which asset types, libraries, plugins; then staged codemods like ui-port.mjs does for UI kits), console + MCP drivers, manifest relation none -> built-on when it starts, fixtures/tests. First real targets: xGallery (MossesX/xGallery, React 19 + Express + SQLite) and whatever claude-project parks.

notes.text: Merged from build profile "main-framework" into "all" (one profile for everything).

origin.said: ask each time between the two ways.

steps.text: Spec first: `_claude/memory/docs/port-engine.md` — the two modes (bake / rebuild), the analysis report shape (`port-report@1`: stack, UI kit found, screens, chrome pieces → asset types, styles → tokens, libraries/plugins suggested, risk list), the staged codemod plan, and what `axf port` refuses (no manifest, dirty git tree). Read `framework/cli/ui-port.mjs` and `claude-project.mjs` first.

CLI entry: `framework/cli/port.mjs` + `axf port <dir> --mode bake|rebuild [--report-only] [--stage N]` in `axf.mjs`; `requireProject` gate; refuses without `--yes` when git is dirty; writes `port-report.json` next to the manifest. `--report-only` works on an empty folder (empty report).

Stack detection: reuse `claude-project.mjs` detection (react/next/android/python…), add UI-kit detection (MUI, Chakra, shadcn, Material3, Compose, Tailwind) by package.json / gradle deps; unit test with fixture folders under `framework/spec/fixtures/port/`.

Analysis, screens + chrome: scan routes/screens (React Router / Next pages / Compose NavHost) and chrome components (app bar, drawer, bottom nav, menus, toolbars, dialogs) → candidate asset list with target type and confidence. Report section `pieces`.

Analysis, styles → tokens: run `portSource` from `ui-port.mjs` in dry mode over the codebase to count colour/size literals and role usages; map to the token list from the theme engine; report `tokens` with unmapped literals. Cap files scanned (size + count) and skip node_modules/build.

Bake, stage 1: `axf init` into the existing project (template by stack) without overwriting app files (`src/axf/` + assets + manifest relation `built-on`), `axf.lock.json`; app still builds (the template guard allows an existing codebase). Checked with a fixture react app.

Bake, stage 2: themes — generate `color-theme` + `style-theme` assets from the detected palette (nearest tokens), apply the literal → `var(--fx-*)` codemod (`ui-port.mjs portSource`) to CSS/TSX/Kotlin files in place with a `.port-backup/`; `--stage 2` only; report lists every file changed.

Bake, stage 3: chrome — generate nav-menu / app-menu / toolbar / dialog assets from the detected pieces and swap the components for the framework ones (`AppShell` / Compose `AppShell`), old components kept under `legacy/` until removed; `--stage 3`.

Rebuild mode: pick the closest boilerplate (`framework/boilerplates/index.json` tags vs detected features), `axf init --boilerplate` into `<dir>-axf` beside the old code, write `PORT-PLAN.md` with screen-by-screen mapping and the old file for each; report `rebuild.plan`.

Drivers: engine-rpc `port` / `port-report`, console `POST /api/port` + `GET /api/port/report?dir=`, MCP `app_port(dir, mode, stage)` (write, needs the console token); manifest `framework.relation` none → built-on when stage 1 runs (`project.mjs` validates).

Console view: Plugins → **Port** (or Wizards view section): pick a folder from allowed roots (project-wizard's `AXF_WIZARD_ROOTS` rule), run the report, show pieces/tokens tables, run stages one at a time with the file list and a diff count; rebuild plan rendered as a checklist.

Pending items hook: `port-<name>` items (parked by claude-project) get a "Run port" button in Pending rows (slot `pending.item`) that opens the console view on that project; `claude-project` writes `x.port.engine: "axf port"` into the manifest.
First real target, xGallery (MossesX/xGallery, React 19 + Express + SQLite): BRETT attaches the repo; run `--report-only`, review the report together, record the mode choice. No codemod yet.
xGallery bake stage 1–2 on a branch in that repo (init + themes), app builds; note unmapped literals; push branch `axf-port` for Brett to look at on the phone.
Tests: `framework/spec/check-port.mjs` over the fixture folders (detection, report shape, stage 1 idempotent, stage 2 backup + dry run, refusals: no manifest, dirty tree, symlinks); CI line.
Close: report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/app-port-engine.md`, LOG.md, CLAUDE.md Status + `axf port` in Build/run/test, pending complete; decisions.md note on bake vs rebuild defaults.

before.title: lib-clone: any AXF app clones its own install with current data
before.detail:
Turn xGallery's New project wizard (MossesX/xGallery: server/src/routes/newproject.ts, src/pages/dev/newproject/NewProjectWizard.tsx, kit/new-project.mjs) into an AXF library so every app built on AXF can clone its install into a new project. Brett: keep the xGallery wizard as is and make it a library for AXF.

before.title: Plugin conflict alarm + tracked AI patches + installed add-ons list
before.detail:
Brett, Oct 18 2026 (parked as unsafe: AI patching and cascading uninstalls need design and review before anyone builds it):

1. When a plugin could potentially conflict with another plugin, raise a developer alarm (alerts library, source conflicts) shown as an expandable row grid like the Systems check grid: same kinds of details per row, fix instructions and external links.
2. Each conflict row has 3 badges/actions: (a) uninstall a plugin - choose which one; (b) ignore; (c) use AI to patch the conflict. The patch must NOT alter any plugin source.
3. Patches are tracked and listed in an Installed add-ons list that covers plugins, add-ons, modules, libraries and patches. Installing a patch is tracked and the patch can be removed.
4. Removing a patch uninstalls every conflicting plugin it patched; those plugins must then be reinstalled.

Builds on: alerts library (conflicts source, diagnostics: same asset id / setting key / settings tab from two named modules; plugins:dup ids on the server), plugin-lifecycle@1 (install/uninstall scripts, backups), plugin-manager (Fable, pending), agent manager add-ons (agent-addon@1 install/uninstall tracking), axf.llm@1 for the AI patch.
Open questions for Brett at build time: what counts as a potential conflict beyond the runtime diagnostics (routes, capability services, settings keys, assets, nav ids, CSS prefixes, data dirs?); where patches live (an overlay layer the console applies at load, never the plugin folder); whether removing a patch should back up the plugins first and offer one-tap reinstall.

notes.text: Oct 22 2026: patches-plugins (Opus) adds Patches-owned plugin lists per hosted app and an auto install of missing plugins; check for overlap when this is designed.
Merged from build profile "main-framework" into "all" (one profile for everything).

origin.said: AI patching and cascading uninstalls need design and review before anyone builds it):

steps.text: Design note, part 1 (no code): `_claude/memory/docs/plugin-conflicts.md` — what counts as a potential conflict beyond runtime diagnostics: routes (`/api/plugins/<f>/`), capability services (two providers of one `axf.x@1`), settings keys, asset ids, nav ids, CSS prefixes (`axp-*`), data dirs, Python module names. For each: how it is detected from `plugin.json` + the bundle + `plugin-inventory@1` facts, severity, false-positive risk.

Design note, part 2: patches. Proposal: a patch is an **overlay** (`.axf-console/patches/<id>/patch.json`, `plugin-patch@1`: target plugins, kind rename-route / remap-setting / alias-asset / disable-contribution, applied by the console at load, never touching a plugin folder); AI only proposes a patch document, a person approves it (change-batch card); removal backs up + offers one-tap reinstall. Risks and what is refused.

BRETT reviews both notes and answers the three open questions (conflict kinds in scope, overlay approach yes/no, backup + reinstall on patch removal). Status stays `unsafe` until he says the design is approved; then `pending`. Record in decisions.md.

Conflict engine (pure): extend `framework/core/engines/plugins.ts` (`plugin-inventory@1`) with `potentialConflicts(records)` for the approved kinds, severity + fix hints; Kotlin `PluginInventoryEngine` + Python `plugin-manager/server/engine.py` mirror it; fixture cases in `spec/fixtures/plugin-inventory.json` → `conflicts` (`check-plugin-inventory.mts`, `test.py`, `PluginInventoryConformanceTest`).

Alerts source `conflicts`: `apps/console-web/server/alerts.py` raises one alert per conflict key (`conflict:<kind>:<a>:<b>`, warn, resolved when it disappears) from the engine output every poll; rule default: bell on. Test in `server/test_alerts.py`.

Conflict grid UI: plugin `apps/console-web/plugins/plugin-conflicts` (from `_template`) with a dialog `plugin-conflicts.grid` built on the Systems check grid component pattern (expandable rows: details, fix instructions, links); opened from the alert's link and from Plugin Manager rows. Read-only this step.

Row actions (a) Uninstall — pick which plugin, confirm by typing its folder, runs `plugin-lifecycle.mjs uninstall --all` through the existing `/api/plugin-lifecycle/<folder>/uninstall`; (b) Ignore — stored per conflict key in the plugin dataDir, hides the row and resolves the alert; both admin-only.

Patch overlay runtime: `server/patches.py` loads `plugin-patch@1` files, validates them against the schema (`framework/schemas/plugin-patch.json`), applies approved kinds at plugin load (route prefix rename, settings key remap, asset alias, contribution disable) in the loader, never writes into plugin folders; `GET /api/plugins/plugin-conflicts/patches`.

(c) AI patch: "Patch with AI" asks Mosses through `axf.llm@1` for a patch document for this conflict (prompt includes the engine facts), validates it, shows it on a change-batch-style approval card; Apply writes the file and reloads plugins; refused when the assistant is off (409 with what is missing).

Installed add-ons list: dialog + Settings → Plugins → Add-ons listing plugins, libraries (`plugin-inventory`), modules, agent add-ons (`agent-addon@1` from `axf.agents@1` when present) and patches, each with installed date, what it touches, Remove. Patches show which plugins they patch.

Patch removal: Remove patch → backup (`.axf-console/plugin-backups/`) → uninstall every plugin it patched (lifecycle) → list them with one-tap Reinstall from the catalog (`plugin-catalog.mjs install`) when the step-3 decision says so. Audit line per action.
Tests: plugin `test.py` (grid data, ignore, patch validation + refusals, removal cascade with fake lifecycle), engine fixtures, lifecycle check, CI lines.
Close: report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/plugin-conflicts.md`, LOG.md, web screenshots, CLAUDE.md Status, rules line about patches never touching plugin folders, pending complete.

before.detail: Permanent framework asset types: banner (thin bar above the layout, logo, hosts attached assets on left/center/right, plugins attach at run time), badge and clock (attachable, never rolled or picked as slots). steps.text: Read first (Build-Pilot repo must be attached): `src/pilot/contract.ts`, `stacks.ts`, `tests/contract.test.ts`, the five Android/all-stack plugins, `server/assembly.py`. Types: rewrite `pilot-plugin@1` manifest + `PilotStep`, `BuildPatch`, `ComposeResult`, `PilotProject` (`pilot-project@1`) as a pure, port-neutral module `src/pilot/contract/types.ts` with no DOM/React imports; JSON Schema generated for both documents (`schemas/`). before.title: Agents + assistant sessions hosted on axHub (one host for every app)
before.detail:
Brett, Oct 20 2026: agents (Build Pilot's pilot-assembler, Mosses and every agent-definition@1 agent) and AI assistant live sessions should run on axHub, not inside each app. Build Pilot, the Dev Console and the phone apps become clients.

- axHub gets an agent + session host: runs turns, owns live-session@1 event logs (sessions survive app restarts and browser closes), per-agent memory, provider keys in axHub's vault, hub permissions for who may use which agent.
- Apps plug in through what the Fable rebuilds left open: the live-session host registry (`axf.live-host@1` / `register_host`, today a typed `axhub` placeholder in the console and Build Pilot), Build Pilot's assembly backend (BP_AGENT=local|console|off → add `axhub`), and the kernel placeholders `axf.agents`, `axhub.agent`.
- axHub never depends on AXF (decision): the host speaks the contracts over its API (AXPP), with an AXF adapter on the AXF side (lib-hub).
- The assembly gate (pilot-assembly@1) stays in Build Pilot: axHub only proposes ops; Build Pilot checks and builds. Manual mode unaffected.
- Needs the axHub repo (MossesX/axHub) attached.

Until then: Build Pilot runs its agent locally (Fable rebuild Oct 20 2026), the console's assistant hosts its own sessions.

notes.text: Nov 3 2026: s12 (Build Pilot backend) skipped, Build Pilot is retired.
Merged from build profile "main-framework" into "all" (one profile for everything).

origin.said: agents (Build Pilot's pilot-assembler, Mosses and every agent-definition@1 agent) and AI assistant live sessions should run on axHub, not inside each app. Build Pilot, the Dev Console and the phone apps become clients.

steps.text: BRETT attaches MossesX/axHub. Read its session/worker layout, decisions #70–#87 and the AXPP protocol doc; write `_claude/memory/docs/axhub-agent-host.md` design: host API (sessions, turns, events, agents, memory, permissions), where provider keys live (vault, write-only), what the AXF adapter translates. No code.

Protocol contract (AXF side, pure): `framework/core/live-session.ts` gains the wire shape for a remote host (`RemoteHostDescriptor`, event envelope with seq, resume cursor), fixtures in `spec/fixtures/live-session.json` → `remote`; Kotlin `ai.amberx.axf.kernel.live` + Python mirror replay them.

axHub, session store: `sessions` table/collection (id, owner, agent, created, closed, cursor) + append-only event log keyed by seq (file or db per axHub's storage), with replay from a cursor; unit tests.

axHub, turn runner: a worker that runs one turn for a session (provider call through axHub's existing LLM client or a new one using vault keys), streams events into the log, survives the browser going away; one running turn per session; stop/cancel.

axHub, agents: `agent-definition@1` validator ported from `framework/core/agents.ts` (fixture `agents.json` replayed), agent registry per project in `/projects/<name>/_data/agents/`, per-agent memory using the memory engine rules from the contract.

axHub, permissions: who may use which agent / open sessions / write mode, as hub user permissions (`agents.use.<id>`, `sessions.open`, `agents.write`) on the users page, enforced on every host route; admin bypass as elsewhere on the hub.

axHub, host API: `/agents`, `/sessions`, `/sessions/{id}/turns` (POST = run), `/sessions/{id}/events?since=` (SSE + replay), `/sessions/{id}/stop|close`; approvals for destructive tool calls through the hub's approval screen (one-tap link rule). OpenAPI snippet in the design doc.

axHub, provider keys: turns use keys from the vault by name (`llm.<provider>`), never returned; `vault.set` from the console's Keys needed flow already exists — add the names to the systems-check key list on the AXF side later (step 15).

AXF adapter, web: `framework/libs/hub` (lib-hub, first slice exists) gets `AxhubLiveHost implements SessionHost` over the host API with the hub session cookie / token provider; registers through `axf.live-sessions@1.register_host()`; the console's AI assistant picks it when Settings → Assistant → Host = axHub.

AXF adapter, Android: `lib-hub` Kotlin `AxhubLiveHost` over axf-network (SSE reader from `lib-mcp`'s parser), registered in the kernel's live-session host registry; placeholder `axhub.agent` becomes real; written without a compiler, CI unit test with MockWebServer.

Console assistant on the hub host: `ai-assistant` plugin `server/sessions.py` host `axhub` stops being a `PlaceholderHost`: a thin proxy host that forwards to the hub API with the signed-in user's identity; reconnect/replay through the existing `watchReply` fold; `test.py` cases with a fake hub.

Build Pilot: `BP_AGENT=axhub` backend in `server/assembly.py` calling the hub host for the `pilot-assembler` agent; the assembly gate (`pilot-assembly@1`) still checks every op locally; manual mode untouched; `test_server.py` with a fake hub.
Phone apps: the AXHub Android app gets a Sessions tab (list, attach to a live reply, stop) on `lib-hub`'s host client; the Android console's assistant screen (when it exists) uses the same.

Migration: console sessions stored locally can be exported/imported into the hub (`POST /sessions/import` with the event log); one-time "Move my sessions to axHub" button in the assistant settings; no data loss on failure (import is additive).
Systems check: new checks `axhub-agent-host` (host reachable, caller allowed) and the vault key names for providers in the Keys needed list; Auto fix opens the right pages.
Alerts + activity: hub sessions appear in the Activity banner source list (`axf.activity@1`), failed turns raise an alert via the hub → console alerts source `axhub`.
Tests, AXF side: `check-live-session` fixture cases for the remote shape, lib-hub web unit tests (fake SSE), Android unit test, plugin `test.py` additions; CI lines in `android.yml`.
Tests, axHub side: host API tests (permissions, replay from cursor, one turn per session, stop), agent validator fixture replay, vault key never returned.

Deploy: axHub redeploy on Coolify with the worker enabled (env for worker count), console `install-console.sh` passes `AXF_ASSISTANT_HOST=axhub` once the hub answers; BRETT approves the deploy and runs one turn from his phone.
Close: differences report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/axhub-agent-host.md`, LOG.md, decisions.md (#88+ on the hub side), CLAUDE.md Status in both repos, pending complete.

before.detail: Brett chose the wrapper over a native rewrite (Nov 7 2026): the web Dev Console (console.amberxai.com) runs inside an Android app shell (Capacitor, like AmberX), so every console change shows on the phone at once. Reuse AmberX's Android shell/bridge pieces (apps/amberx-droid) rather than writing new ones.

1. Android app shell loading the console (console.amberxai.com), with sign-in kept, back button/navigation, pull-to-refresh, offline screen.
2. Native bridges where needed: push notifications (build start/finish/fail/land alerts), mic for voice, background wake, file share/download (APKs), deep links that open a console screen.
3. Console UI stays asset-driven; phone layouts come from the existing three-layouts/phone assets, no hard-coded styling.

steps.text: Shell app scaffold: apps/console-droid (Capacitor shell, server.url console.amberxai.com, allowNavigation console + hub, project manifest, package ai.amberx.console.droid)
Shell behaviour: sign-in kept (cookie flush), back button through web history, pull-to-refresh (guarded by the page's scroll state), offline screen from tokens
Native bridge ConsoleShell plugin: downloads (APKs via DownloadManager with the session cookie, own hosts only), share sheet, deep links (axfconsole:// + https App Links → console route)
Alerts: background wake (WorkManager periodic check of /api/alerts, reusing AmberX HubRules.consoleAlerts/mutedTypes), notifications channel, quiet when AmberX is installed; mic permission for voice
Console web side: shell detection + bridge client (framework-free plugin-free module in console-web), pull-to-refresh guard, notification mode setting
CI: console-droid job (APK console-droid-debug.apk next to amberx-debug.apk, unit tests), ci-scope output, app bundle → Apps catalog
UI Review: three shell-chrome options as assets (--choices), tests, Shipped features, docs, THREADS + report

step.text: 4a. `AxfWebTab` web view composable, locked down: allowed hosts only (own domains from manifest/settings), refuse other links with a toast (never the outside browser), JavaScript on, file access off, popups off, geolocation off, mixed content blocked; unit test of the allow rule (pure function `hostAllowed`).

4b. `AxfWebTab` state: one WebView per tab, lazily created, retained across recompositions (`remember` + `AndroidView` holder keyed by tab id), `FLAG_SECURE` honoured from the activity; manual check on the emulator that switching tabs keeps scroll position.

5a. Hub session cookies: `CookieManager` scoped to the app, `android:allowBackup` rules + `dataExtractionRules` exclude the WebView data; sign-in happens on the hub's own login page inside the tab (no JS injection, no off-hub navigation).

5b. Sign-out: a "Sign out of hub" setting clears cookies for every tab and reloads them; the console tab's own token stays in the SecureStore (untouched); unit test that sign-out does not clear SecureStore keys.
6. Downloads: only axHub Apps page APK links, handed to `DownloadManager` with the hub cookie (as `apps/axhub-android` does); everything else refused with a toast; unit test of the link rule.
7a. Cover slot: active non-console tab fills `app.frame.cover` below the bar; back button goes back inside the web view first, then returns to the Console tab (`BackHandler`).
7b. Loading + errors: pull-to-refresh, a "Loading…" bar, a plain error card (offline, 4xx/5xx, refused frame) with Retry, all from theme tokens; emulator check.
8a. Settings → Plugins → App tabs: pick tabs (switch per built-in), order (up/down), reset; `SettingsGroup`/`SettingSpec` with parent = Plugins.
8b. Custom tabs: add name + https address on an allowed host (validated with `hostAllowed`), remove; stored in `app-tabs.custom` with the web plugin's JSON shape.

10a. Tests: `lib-apptabs` unit tests (allowed-host, link rule, settings parity, tab list from manifests) + Compose UI test for bar + cover; CI job line in `android.yml`.

10b. Report: rebuild log line, differences report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/console-android-app-tabs.md`, push branch `fable/console-android-app-tabs` so `rebuild-shots.yml` captures Android before/after; pending complete.

steps.text: 1a. Pilot contract on Kotlin, types: `axf-pilot-core` pure-Kotlin module (`framework/android/axf-pilot-core`) with `PilotPluginManifest`, `PilotStep`, `BuildPatch`, `BuildRequest` (incl. `hidden`/`assets`) data classes mirroring Build-Pilot's `src/pilot/contract.ts` after its Fable rebuild (`build-pilot-contract`).
1b. Manifest checks + `servesStack`/`pluginsFor` in Kotlin, replaying `spec/fixtures/pilot-contract.json` (copied from Build-Pilot's generated fixture into `framework/spec/fixtures/`).
1c. `compose` merge + conflict rules in Kotlin, same fixture section; `PilotContractConformanceTest` in CI (`:axf-pilot-core:test`).

1d. Fixture sharing: a script in Build-Pilot (`npm run fixtures:export`) writes the fixture; AmberX-AXF CI fails if the copied fixture's hash differs from the one Build-Pilot publishes in its README (manual sync, documented).

2a. Pilot API client, models: Kotlin data classes for `/api/projects`, `/api/catalog`, `/assemble`, `/build`, `/apk`, `/metering/me` responses mirroring `server/main.py`; kotlinx.serialization, lenient unknown keys.
2b. Pilot API client, transport: `PilotClient` over axf-network with the token from SecureStore and the hub-admin sign-in reused (cookie provider), timeouts, no redirects, typed errors.
2c. Pilot API client, tests: MockWebServer test per route (happy path, 401, 5xx, malformed JSON), token never logged; CI job line.

3a. Android plugin face: define the `android/` part of `pilot-plugin@1` (a Compose `steps` composable entry + the same `contribute`/`check` shape) as Kotlin interfaces in `axf-pilot-core`; manifest field `android: { module }`.

3b. Loader: reads bundled plugin manifests from assets, instantiates Android parts by registered factory (open registry), lists web-only plugins separately; unit test with two fake plugins (one Android, one web-only).
4a. Pilot Home screen: stacks + projects list from `PilotClient`, New project button, error/empty states from theme tokens.
4b. Designer shell: steps from the loaded plugins in order, step navigation, autosave through the API (debounced), unsaved marker.
4c. Build step, part 1: review (composed request summary) + assemble with the agent (calls `/assemble`, shows ops, approve/deny).
4d. Build step, part 2: build + validate (`/build`, `/validate`), history list, retry; generic UI only.
5a. `android-app` plugin Android part: App setup form (name, id, package) with validation parity to the web plugin.
5b. `android-app` boilerplate browser: list from the catalog with screenshots (`GET /api/boilerplates/<id>/screenshots/<file>` through the console), pick one.
5c. `look` plugin Android part: slot picks per type from `framework-assets` (engine-rpc through the console), preview chips.
5d. `build-options` plugin Android part: switches from `GET /api/build-options`, defaults off, descriptions.
5e. `feature-manager` Android part, 1: FeatureList rows (catalog features, grouped), search, selected set.
5f. `feature-manager` Android part, 2: Chrome section (banner/toolbar entries) + Customize/Build now actions wired to the designers (step 6) and the Build step.
5g. `custom-features` Android part: metered Claude request form, usage from `/metering/me`, result list; refused when no key with a clear note.

6a. Banner designer on Android: builds the same asset@1 `banner` document as `src/pilot/designers.tsx` (surface, logo, divider, attach list); widget picker from the engine's app defaults (`typeLabels`/`typeIcons` via the console API).
6b. Toolbar designer on Android: items + widgets start/end + density/surface/collapsible, same asset@1 output; unit test that both designers emit documents that pass the Kotlin validator.

7a. Live preview, frame: a floating phone-frame composable (window via `windows/` engine) rendering the composed request's theme through the Kotlin theme engine; shrink to a pill, drag (same as the web `ScreenMock` behaviour).
7b. Live preview, content: nav/toolbar/banner from the picked assets, screens as placeholders with the boilerplate's screen kinds; updates on every designer change (debounced).
8. APK builds from the phone: Build APK → poll `/apk` → download via `DownloadManager` → install prompt; progress widget bound to a counter (`counter`/`progress` widget kinds).
9a. axHub admin client, models: Kotlin data classes for the hub's step-4 admin API (services, jobs, approvals, audit, users, projects) from its OpenAPI/JSON shapes; lenient parsing.
9b. axHub admin client, transport + tests: `HubAdminClient` over axf-network sharing the AXHub app's session (cookie jar), CSRF header handling, no redirects; MockWebServer tests per route.
9c. Approvals list screen native (replaces the web view the AXHub app uses today): list, filters, pull to refresh.
9d. Single approval screen: details, Approve/Deny through the API with the hub's CSRF rules, PIN prompt when the hub asks, result toast; one-tap link rule honoured from notifications.
10a. Services: list/describe/call with a JSON args editor, destructive confirm card (same rule as lib-mcp's gate).
10b. Jobs: list, detail with progress, cancel.
10c. Audit log viewer: paged list, filter by user/tool, detail sheet.
10d. Vault names: list of names only, set/rotate (write-only; values never shown).
10e. Users + permissions: list, per-user permission switches (`console.*`, `agents.*`, `apps.download`), add user (temporary password flow as the hub does).
10f. Projects tree browser over `axhub.memory_*` (read + edit text files with approval), Apps page (download APKs through `DownloadManager`).
11a. Native tab bar in slot `app.frame.top` (from `console-android-app-tabs` step 1) switching Console / Pilot (native) / axHub (native), each with its own back stack (`NavHost` per tab).
11b. Tab choice shared with the web console through the `app-tabs.*` settings keys (settings-from-axHub when it lands); unit test of the mapping.
12a. Tests: fake-server tests for both clients, Compose tests per screen group (Home/Designer/Build, plugin parts, designers, approvals, services), CI job lines.

12b. Report: rebuild log line, differences report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/console-android-native-tabs.md`, push `fable/console-android-native-tabs` for `rebuild-shots.yml` screenshots; pending complete.

steps.text: 1a. Framework embed@1 (web reference): `core/engines/embed.ts` — the marker a host app puts on the pages it embeds (query `?axf-embed=<host>[&axf-embed-hide=…]`, user agent `AXF-Embed/<host>[/<types>]`), host id rules, hidden-chrome cleaning (hideable types only, default banner, `none`), host helpers `userAgentSuffix` / `embedUrl`; fixture `spec/fixtures/embed.json`.

1b. Hide engine forced layer + runtime (web): `hiddenSlots(overrides, defaults, forced)`; `AxfRuntime.embedded` (detected from the page or passed), `embedHiddenSlots`, `slotHiddenByHost`, `setSlotHidden` refuses host-shown chrome with a toast and never writes an override; `AppShell` marks `.fx-frame[data-axf-embed]`; lib-settings greys the slot picker out ("Shown by <host>"); `spec/check-embed.mts` in CI.

1c. Kotlin twins: `EmbedEngine` (same fixture), `HideEngine.hiddenSlots(…, forced)`, `AxfRuntime(embedded = …)` + `slotHiddenByHost`, Compose settings chips greyed; `EmbedConformanceTest` + the hide fixture's forced cases in `ConformanceTest`.

2. Dev Console: remove the App tabs plugin cleanly (`uninstall.mjs --all`, lifecycle check clean), strip its doc lines, keep the `app.frame.top` / `app.frame.cover` slots for other plugins; the console stands alone with its own banner.

3a. Patches app scaffold: `axf init apps/patches` (android-compose, developer app: look + settings from axHub, hub library), app id `patches`, package `ai.amberx.axf.patches`, project manifest (repo `MossesX/patches` reserved), own layout asset `patches-tabs` (top tabs, no menubar/toolbar/status, full width), nav asset `patches-tabs` with the three tabs, manifest hides toolbar/app-menu.

3b. lib-hub `WebAppView`: a full web-app WebView (JavaScript + DOM storage on, cache allowed, origin allowlist with the hub origin for the sign-in wall, no file/content access, no mixed content, downloads to the hub app catalog handler), user agent suffix from `EmbedEngine.userAgentSuffix("patches")`, `WebAppHolder` that keeps one WebView per tab alive across tab switches (reparented, never destroyed until the activity goes), back button = page history.

3c. Patches views: three routes (console / pilot / axhub) each rendering the holder's WebView for that tab; the Patches banner (logo, day/night switch, clock, settings button) is the one banner; hub sign-in via the developer-app waiting screen (shared cookie store = one session for every tab); Settings → Patches group: hub address, each tab's URL, reload tab, open in the phone's browser.

4. Wiring: CI (`android.yml` builds every app `app-bundle.mjs list --android` finds → `patches-debug.apk` + app catalog entry), `project.manifest.json` validated (`axf project validate --all`), `framework/catalog` + tracker, CLAUDE.md status, rules note (Android hold exception for Patches), PORTING.md, decisions.md.

5. Proof: web checks (`check-embed`, `check-widgets`, `check-appearance`, `check-app-menu`, `check-hub`, `axf validate --framework`, console typecheck), before/after web screenshots (console with and without the tab group; console embedded = no banner), push `fable/patches-wrapper` (Android shots by `rebuild-shots.yml`), differences report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/patches-wrapper.md`, LOG.md line, change-log result.

before.title: Patches manages the plugins of the apps it hosts (Opus)
before.detail: Brett, Oct 22 2026: when Patches loads developer apps in tabs, Patches owns all plugins. New embed@1 take `plugins`: inside such a host an app loads only the plugins Patches has installed and enabled for it (its own on/off switches don't apply), and its plugin hooks (Settings → Plugins, Plugin Manager, plugin switches, plugin menu entries) are greyed out with "Plugins are managed in Patches". The app reports the plugins it has (`plugins` message); Patches compares with its own list, tries to install the missing ones by itself, and shows a Systems check entry with Auto fix while any are missing. Web first (patches-web + console); Patches Android and Kotlin twin deferred.

# Build: x.engine.dev

## Brett said (verbatim)
> 

## What to build
Continue build "Live reload (axf dev) + device hot reload" (x.engine.dev) [Build engine] — Phase 1, model Opus.
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 30 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.
Steps in this phase (4 left, ~2 h):
[ ] s1 (~30 min) Web hot reload: `framework/react` `useDevServer(url)` long-polls `/events` from `dev-server.mjs` and re-registers changed assets (`registry.register` + `rt.refreshFromSaved`); `axf dev` prints the URL; demo app opts in with `?axfDev=`.
[ ] s2 (~30 min) Android end to end on the emulator (CI): `rebuild-shots.yml`-style job step that starts `axf dev --framework` on the runner, points the emulator at `10.0.2.2:7070` (setting `axf.devServer`, flag `axf.hotReload`), edits a theme file, screenshots before/after and asserts the pixel diff > 0.
[ ] s3 (~30 min) Robustness: dev server validates every changed file before announcing it (invalid → `/events` carries `error` and the device shows a terminal line), ignores editor temp files, handles rename/delete; `check-dev-server.mjs` test with a temp folder.
[ ] s4 (~30 min) Docs + status: README section "Live reload on a phone" (PC IP, same Wi-Fi), plan warning cleared, status.json + tracker, `build_step complete`.
Tick each step: node apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/orchestrator.mjs act step x.engine.dev <stepId> done — it reaches main at once (builds-live). Link your branch / PR: node framework/cli/builds-live.mjs link x.engine.dev --branch <b> --pr <n>.
Watch live: when you start on a screen, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "…"` so the live preview follows you.
Screenshots that are not for approval (checking a screen, live captures, before/after): axf shot <file> --name "…" --app … --screen … --group "<build name>" (UI Review → Screenshots; ui-review-item@1), never the review queue.

## Pipeline
This session was started by the orchestrator's dispatcher on Claude account mossesx-max- for the Opus phase. Tick every step as you finish it (orchestrator.mjs act step x.engine.dev <stepId> done). When this phase's steps are done, stop: the dispatcher starts the next phase on the right account. If you must stop early with steps left, say why in a build note (orchestrator.mjs act note x.engine.dev "…"); the build goes back to Pending for Brett.

Android end to end on the emulator (CI): `rebuild-shots.yml`-style job step that starts `axf dev --framework` on the runner, points the emulator at `10.0.2.2:7070` (setting `axf.devServer`, flag `axf.hotReload`), edits a theme file, screenshots before/after and asserts the pixel diff > 0.

before.title: Plugin runtime (deliver features after install)
before.detail: plugin@1 manifest, scopes, action macros and a PluginLoader contract exist; loading plugins at runtime is a placeholder.

notes.text: Merged from build profile "main-framework" into "all" (one profile for everything).

steps.text: Design check (no code): read `contract/Plugin.kt` (PACK/MODULE/SCRIPT, scopes, `PluginLoader`), `framework/schemas/asset-pack.json` if asset-browser made it, and the plugin-catalog format; write `_claude/memory/docs/plugin-runtime.md`: what a PACK may carry (assets, action macros, string packs), install sources (file, URL, QR, console catalog), grants UI, and what stays placeholder (MODULE code loading, SCRIPT).

Pack format on every port: `framework/schemas/plugin-pack.json` (`pack@1`: manifest plugin@1 + files list + hashes) validated by TS (`core/plugins-pack.ts`), Kotlin (`PluginManifest` + pack reader) and Python (catalog engine); fixture `spec/fixtures/plugin-pack.json` (good pack, over-scope pack refused, bad hash).

Android loader, PACK only: `axf-platform-android` `PackLoader implements PluginLoader` — stage from file/URL (OkHttp, no redirects, size cap), verify hashes, keep under `filesDir/plugins/<id>/`, states STAGED→DISABLED→ENABLED; `axf.plugins` placeholder replaced for PACK, MODULE/SCRIPT still answer NotImplemented.

Android apply: an enabled pack registers its assets into `AssetRegistry` (origin = plugin id, conflicts reported as diagnostics) and its macros into `ExtensionPoints.MACROS`; disable/uninstall removes exactly those; unit test with a fixture pack.

Grants: scopes requested vs granted stored in KV; a pack asking beyond `PACK_MAX` is BLOCKED; Settings → Plugins (lib-settings) shows each pack with its scopes and an Enable switch; `PluginManagerModule` lists packs via `PluginInventoryHost`.

Sources: `ExtensionPoints.PLUGIN_SOURCES` gets two contributions — local file picker and console catalog (`GET /api/plugin-catalog?kind=pack` through the console client in lib-hub or a plain URL setting); QR stays placeholder.

Web loader: `framework/libs/plugins` (web `PackLoader`: fetch pack JSON, validate, register assets/macros into `rt`, enable/disable persisted in settings); the console installs it; Settings → Plugins lists packs beside libraries.

Catalog publish for packs: `plugin-catalog.mjs` kind `pack` (files = asset JSON only, validated by `validateAsset`), console Plugin Manager → Install view lists packs; `check-plugin-catalog.mjs` cases.
Tests + CI: Kotlin `PackLoaderTest` (fixture pack, hash refusal, scope block, remove leaves nothing), web unit via `check-plugin-pack.mts`, CI lines; written without a compiler for the Kotlin part.

Docs + status: PORTING.md "Plugins after install", plan android placeholder → built (PACK), web → built, status.json + tracker, `build_step complete`; MODULE/SCRIPT remain placeholders (named in the tracker).

before.title: Background work scheduler
before.detail: WorkSpec / Worker / WorkRegistry contracts and a placeholder scheduler. Real implementation is WorkManager on Android.

notes.text: Merged from build profile "main-framework" into "all" (one profile for everything).
Audit: done — work@1 engine (TS + Kotlin) and lib-work on main: commit 78a12bc07; framework/core/engines/work.ts, framework/spec/fixtures/work.json, framework/spec/check-work.mts

steps.text: Web contract: `framework/core/work.ts` = Kotlin `contract/Work.kt` (`WorkSpec`, `WorkConstraints`, policies, states, `WorkRegistry` of workers by id); fixture `spec/fixtures/work.json` (unique + KEEP/REPLACE/APPEND rules, backoff computation, constraint evaluation with explicit inputs).

Android scheduler: `axf-platform-android` `WorkManagerScheduler` mapping `WorkSpec` → WorkManager requests (constraints, backoff, unique work policy), `WorkRegistry` dispatch inside one `AxfWorker`; capability `axf.work` real; periodic + one-shot; progress through `WorkState` flow. Written without a compiler.

Web scheduler: `framework/libs/work` with a `setTimeout`/visibility-aware scheduler (one-shot + periodic while the page lives, persisted queue in settings so a reload re-enqueues), constraints evaluated with `navigator.connection`/battery where available, else ignored with a terminal note.

Workers registry: `ExtensionPoints.WORKERS` typed (`WorkerContribution {id, run}`) on Kotlin + web; the alerts library's 3-minute poll becomes the first web worker; Android console showcase registers a demo periodic worker (logs a line).
Tests: Kotlin `WorkConformanceTest` (fixture) + `WorkManagerSchedulerTest` with `WorkManagerTestInitHelper`; web `check-work.mts`; CI lines.
Docs + status: PORTING.md "Background work", plan android placeholder → built, web → built, features `k.scheduler`/`dv.bg` built, tracker, `build_step complete`.

before.title: Console in its own private repo
before.detail: Split apps/console-web into a private repo that depends on a tagged framework version.

notes.text: Merged from build profile "main-framework" into "all" (one profile for everything).

steps.text: BRETT says go (rule: not until he does) and picks the dependency style: tagged framework version via git tag + `npm pack`-style tarball, or a git submodule. Record in decisions.md.

Framework packaging: `framework/cli/axf.mjs pack-framework <tag>` producing `axf-framework-<tag>.tgz` (core, react, ui, schemas, libs, plan cores) + a GitHub release asset on tag push (`release.yml`).

Repo split: create `MossesX/axf-console` (exists on GitHub first), move `apps/console-web` with history (`git subtree split`), manifest `location` + `repo.exists: true`, `_claude/` + CLAUDE.md via `claude-project`; CI there re-bakes from the tagged tarball instead of `../../framework`.

This repo: `apps/console-web` becomes a thin pointer (README + manifest `location` pointing at the new repo), `install-console.sh` clones the console repo; `deploy/` scripts and `android.yml` console job updated.
Verify: console builds in its repo against the tag, deploy on the VPS from the new clone, `/api/health` + `/mcp` ok; status + `build_step complete`.

steps.text: Design the one builds dataset in plan.json: queue order/steps/rework, parked model + notes + sub prompts, orchestrator phases/approvals, hidden/archived; status mapping pending ↔ plan; spec framework/spec/BUILDS.md
builds-core.mjs (pure): every view (plan, tracker, queue, pending, orchestrator) is a filter/sort over one list, with nested info per row (steps, notes, deps, linked features, phases)
Shims: pending-core, build-queue-core and orchestrator-core read/write through builds-core (same APIs); tracker.json generated from it; fixture spec/fixtures/builds.json + checker
Migration: pending.json (9 planId items attach, 91 become entries), build-queue.json, orchestrator.json → plan.json; dry-run report; persist + manifest data.shared updated
Run the migration (repo + hub _data), keep the old files as read-only exports for one release
GET/POST /api/builds, engine-rpc and MCP; pending_list/pending_change, build-queue and orchestrator routes keep working through the shims
Builds page: one nav entry, view toolbar (Plan · Tracker · Queue · Pending · Orchestrator), shared filters, ?view= in the URL; old pages redirect to their view
Table look (framework DataGrid) as every view's default, rows expand to the Pending card; Orchestrator view = same table with phases and steps nested
Nested info per view: tracker → group + suggested features; queue → linked features, deps, rework; plan → acceptance, ports, deps; pending → steps, notes
Grid columns (summary, date added, time, cost), toolbar Archive/Delete/Hide/Unhide/Open in, double-click multi-select (pending-grid-view s1-s6)
View switching everywhere: app menu Builds ▸ View, context menu Open in view…, shortcuts 1–5, banners open a filtered view, axf://builds?view=…, search provider
claude.ai Pending page maps to the new data; Build manager merge simplified (no de-dup needed)

Every build entry carries hidden date/time fields: createdAt (set once) and updatedAt (any change: status, step tick, note, sub prompt, model, edit) on the feature build block and every step/note (at/doneAt). builds-core stamps them in apply(); the migration backfills missing ones from pending/queue/orchestrator/history dates (never blank). Kept in plan.json and every export (pending.json, build-queue.json, orchestrator.json, tracker.json, hub _data) and in the claude.ai Pending page data. Hidden: not shown as columns, only in row details / tooltip.
steps.why: Brett Oct 27 18:15: date and time in hidden fields of all entries everywhere data is stored

steps.text: Newest first, always: every view (Plan, Tracker, Queue, Pending, Orchestrator, Remaining/Live/Built/Sessions, banners, Build manager, claude.ai Pending page) sorts by updatedAt descending regardless of filters, chips or search; the old order/status/left sorts become a secondary key or an explicit per-click column sort that resets to newest-first on reload. Steps inside a build keep their own order.
steps.why: Brett Oct 27 18:15: regardless of filter always sort by recent at top (picked last updated)
checks: test: a step tick moves its build to the top in every view

before.title: Tools plugin: the Tools section as its own plugin, with a Tools tab in Patches web
before.detail:
Brett, Oct 22 2026: the Tools section is a plugin of its own, and Claude handoff depends on it.

- New plugin `tools` (plugin@1 + lifecycle): it owns the Tools nav section and the top-level `tools` application menu that tool plugins add to; it provides a capability service (e.g. `axf.tools@1`) that tool plugins require.
- Claude handoff (and any later tool plugin) declares it as a dependency (`requires`) and adds its entries through it instead of creating the section itself.
- For Patches: the Tools plugin adds a **Tools** tab to Patches web's app tab group (next to Console / Pilot / axHub). Patches itself runs the Tools page; it is not the console page in a frame.
- Patches web only for now (Android later).

before.title: AmberX: hands-free listening on screen + in background, ActiveX-style detection overlay (level graph, dB, quick settings)
before.detail: Brett, Oct 27 2026 (claude.ai): 'It only detects words when I press speak' in AmberX (apps/amberx-droid). Cause: the native wake listener runs only while 'Watch axHub in the background' is on (default off) and pauses while the app is on screen. Fix: hands-free listening is its own setting (default on), works on screen and in the background, independent of axHub monitoring; optional always-armed (no wake phrase). Plus a detection overlay like ActiveX: floating draggable window over other apps with a moving audio-level line graph, decibel number, what was heard, and quick settings (listening on/off, always armed, hide). Colours from the app's theme tokens. Profile refactor, Opus (Brett's pick). Android exception: AmberX shell is allowed (rule Oct 25).

before.title: Fix: switches and tab buttons dead inside interface tabs
before.detail: Brett Oct 27 2026: Appearance switches in console settings and the layout (interface) buttons at the top do nothing. Cause: AxfRuntime.scoped() gives a scope settings = Object.create(base.settings), so set()/clear()/reload() assign this.values on the scoped object and the shared settings never change (Main tab cannot be reached again from GizmoX Night / AmberX Signature). Fix: scoped settings forward every member except get to the shared registry.

before.title: Approval history with costs: every approval recorded with details + cost, browsable in Console + axHub
before.detail:
Brett Oct 28 2026 (claude.ai): 'Add cost of approval every time something is approved and display costs, as well as all details and history of past approvals browsing. Can you alert when needing approval without stopping and restarting.' Context: he asked whether sending an approval and waiting costs tokens. Answer given: waiting is free, but each retry check re-reads the conversation (mostly cached). The 15 s x10 then 1 min rule costs about 10-15 checks per 5 minutes. HELD: queued, not started. Picks (cards): profile Refactor, held; history in the Console AND on axHub's approvals page.

Scope:
1) Cost per approval: every approval records the session's token/cost spent while it waited (number of checks, tokens in/out, cached vs not, USD from framework/schemas/model-pricing.json), plus the time it waited and who/what asked (session, surface, machine, build ref, reason title/description, exact call, result).
2) History browser: every past approval with all details and its cost; filter/sort/search, totals per day/build/session. Console = History view in the approvals-banner plugin (framework DataGrid, expanding rows). axHub = same list on its approvals page. Approve stays on the first screen.
3) Alert without stopping/restarting: a hub-side wait (axhub tool, e.g. approvals.wait / long-poll on the confirmation id, up to ~10 min per call) so a session makes ONE call that returns the moment Brett approves. No retry loop and no session restart. The AmberX app push (already shipped, amberx-push) fires when the approval is created. Then update the shared retry rule (15 s x10, then 1 min) to 'one wait call, re-issued only if it times out' — Brett to confirm that rule change at build time.
Work spans MossesX/axHub (wait tool, cost fields, approvals page history) and AXF (approvals-banner History view, cost capture via codebase-changes hooks / session transcript).

before.title: Feature Matrix plugin: a skip/keep feature matrix for every build, one dataset, hooks in every builds grid, Apply updates status everywhere
before.detail:
Brett Oct 28 2026 (claude.ai, windows-terminal chat): "Make a plugin to build a feature matrix just like this [the windows-terminal scope list: https://claude.ai/artifact/CwBGQof4NBe4F3dPTczBvS] for every build and put hooks to them in every builds grid in orchestrator, pending, queued, build manager, etc. I need to be able to access its associated matrix from any entry in any grid. All matrix are compiled into 1 dataset that lists each one in expandable rows that open to display its matrix. The grid has column with date added and time cost to build generated by the matrix. When matrix changes an apply button lights up that updates the status across all tables. Nothing is ever removed only set for skip when time comes to build. They can be added removed whenever they never leave the matrix."

Rules from the ask: every build has a matrix (feature items grouped, each with minutes, model Fable/Opus, why); tick = keep, untick = skip; items can be added at any time and are NEVER deleted ("removed" = skip; skipped items stay in the matrix and are skipped when the build runs). One dataset of all matrices, shown as a grid of expandable rows (row = build; columns include date added and the time cost computed from the kept items); a row opens to its matrix. Editing a matrix lights an Apply button; Apply pushes the new totals/skips/status to every table (orchestrator, pending, build queue, build manager, plan…). Every builds grid gets a hook (row button + right-click) that opens that entry's matrix.

Brett's picks: Refactor profile; standalone plugin (builds-one-page removed); built in its own chat thread. Seed: the windows-terminal scope list (23 items, its db doc scope/selection) becomes the first matrix. Overlaps: share-search s1 (grid-attach@1: grid registry) — the hook seam here should be the same registry or forward-compatible with it; basic-filter (running, PR #155) attaches to datasets too.

before.title: Run unless blocked: 2-min countdown → urgent alarm (red banner + loud AmberX ring) → 1-min grace → runs; Block anytime; zero session tokens
before.detail:
Brett Oct 28 2026 (claude.ai): 'Can you send notification that a command is about to be ran and I can intercept it from the banner and block it before axhub tries sending it.' HELD: queued, not started. Picks (cards): profile Refactor, held; countdown 2 minutes.

Design: a third tool policy next to allow / confirm, e.g. 'veto' (run unless blocked). A session's call returns a job id at once; axHub holds the call for the countdown (default 2 min, per-tool override possible later) and immediately pushes through the AmberX app (rule: all axHub pushes come from AmberX) and shows it in the console's banner (approvals banner or its own) with the reason title, the exact call, a live countdown, Block and Run now. No action = runs at zero. Block = cancelled, never runs, the session sees 'blocked' when it next looks at the job. Sessions never poll during the countdown: they carry on and read the job result once at the end only if they need it, which saves the re-read cost of approval checks. Approvals (confirm) stay for risky calls: deletes and free-form root shell. Brett picks which tools move to veto (proposal: merge-pr, redeploys, container restarts). Every veto call is logged with its outcome (ran / blocked / ran early) in the approvals history (approval-costs build). Related: approval-costs (history, wait call, resume), axhub-github-write.

before.detail: Brett Oct 28 2026 14:18-14:20 (claude.ai): send the command to axHub; axHub waits for approval and runs it or not; the session does not wait. Today a confirm call returns confirmation_required and drops the call, so the session must re-send it with the confirmation_id after approval, which is why sessions poll (each check re-reads the whole chat). Change: axHub stores the full call on create; Approve = the hub runs it itself and keeps the result; Reject/expire = dropped. The session gets an approval id at once and moves on; it reads the result once later only if needed. Replaces the polling rule (15 s x10 then 1 min). HELD: queued in Refactor; Brett says go.

origin.said: send the command to axHub; axHub waits for approval and runs it or not; the session does not wait. Today a confirm call returns confirmation_required and drops the call, so the session must re-send it with the confirmation_id after approval, which is why sessions poll (each check re-reads the whole chat). Change: axHub stores the full call on create; Approve = the hub runs it itself and keeps the result; Reject/expire = dropped. The session gets an approval id at once and moves on; it reads the result once later only if needed. Replaces the polling rule (15 s x10 then 1 min). HELD: queued in Refactor; Brett says go.

before.title: Console Home cards: card@1 asset plugins carry, Home detects/shows/hides every card (always rendered), card layouts, cards for every data plugin
before.detail:
Brett, Oct 29 2026: "Design a bunch more cards for the console home screen. If plugins with data or dynamic content don't have a card, design one for them from scratch (you decide what to display and how). Plugins can now carry cards that can be designed in the future SDK and attached to the plugin as assets. Console Home detects all card assets attached to plugins and shows or hides them, but always rendered. The card layout can show or hide all cards detected."

Decisions (cards): profile Angel (new, this is its first build; nothing built in the asking session); Fable contract first, then Opus.
Card designs: one per plugin with data/dynamic content (31 plugins + 5 existing Home cards). No card: _template, basic-filter, plugin-switches, plugins-menu (tools with no data of their own).
Clash check Oct 29: no open build touches Home or cards (refactor profile all complete; main-framework pending items unrelated).

notes.text: Reconciler: branch angel/home-cards-queue (PR #171); PR #171; PR #171 merged

Replaced by urgent build home-cards-live (Nov 3 2026, Brett: "I shouldn't need to build cards. I should draw dynamic data."). No hand-built card per plugin; one card engine draws any plugin read command.
Merged from build profile "angel" into "all" (one profile for everything).
Shipped manifest sm-home-cards rev 1 sent to Shipped features (backfill): landed b2351e130, 10 file(s), 0 test line(s), 18 open.

origin.said: Design a bunch more cards for the console home screen. If plugins with data or dynamic content don't have a card, design one for them from scratch (you decide what to display and how). Plugins can now carry cards that can be designed in the future SDK and attached to the plugin as assets. Console Home detects all card assets attached to plugins and shows or hides them, but always rendered. The card layout can show or hide all cards detected.

steps.text: card@1 asset type in framework/schemas/asset-types.json (+ axf schemas): id, owner (plugin id or "console"), title, icon, kind (stat | list | meter | chart | feed | status | actions | custom), size (s | m | l | wide | tall), data {service (plugin_services capability), path, refreshSec, live:boolean}, slots (headline, value, sub, rows, sparkline, actions), emptyState, actions (ids run through the action engine), level (Simple/Basic/Developer/Administrator), minRole (UAC), defaultVisible, order, category. Open registry: unknown kinds render the custom slot, never fail.

plugin@1 gets `cards: ["cards/<id>.json", …]` (card assets ship inside the plugin folder, so plugin-lifecycle@1 removes them on uninstall); plugin-inventory@1 engine lists each plugin's cards (framework/core/engines/plugins.ts + server/engine.py twin) so anything can detect them; future card SDK attaches cards to a plugin by writing this list.

home-cards@1 engine (TS reference, framework/core/engines/cards.ts): collects every card from enabled plugins + console-owned cards, applies saved visibility/order/size, level and role; hidden cards stay in the output with `hidden: true` so Home ALWAYS renders (mounts) every card and only hides it (instant show, data kept warm). Fixture spec/fixtures/home-cards.json; Kotlin twin recorded as a deferred gap in PORTING.md (Android on hold).

card-layout@1 asset type: columns per window class (compact/medium/expanded), gap + density tokens, grouping (none | plugin | category), "show all / hide all" default, sort (manual | category | plugin). 3 starter layouts: grid-auto, two-column-dashboard, compact-list. Hot-swap via runtime.swap('card-layout', id); tokens only (THEMING.md).

Placeholders for the future card SDK: `axf.cards@1` capability service (list/register/unregister cards at runtime), extension point `home.cards`, typed NotImplemented card designer entry, so a designer plugin can later author card assets and attach them to any plugin without kernel changes.

Home renders from the home-cards engine. The 5 cards already there become console-owned card assets: Plan summary, Build summary, Coverage, Project, Recent installs & imports. Same look at the default theme.

Card layout toolbar on Home (hideable): Show all · Hide all · layout picker (card-layout assets) · group by · a Cards checklist popover with one switch per detected card. Right-click a card: Hide card · Card size · Open plugin · Plugin settings. Drag to reorder. Saved per user in settings (synced through axHub like the rest).
Settings → Home cards tab (with the level toolbar rule): every detected card grouped by plugin, switch + size + order, layout default; a card whose plugin is disabled shows greyed "plugin off".

Cards — Build orchestrator: next step + model chip, approvals waiting (one-tap), phase progress bar per open build. Build manager: remaining work split Fable/Opus, hours + cost left, top 3 builds. Build profiles: active profile chip + pending/queue/orchestrator counts for each profile, switch button.

Cards — Feature matrix: kept vs skipped minutes per build, matrices with unapplied changes (Apply button). Fable rebuilds: parked count, Fable hours left, next rebuild. Changes & features grid: latest 5 changes/features with state dots.

Cards — Codebase changes: live/running entries with heartbeat age and current step. Activity: running/queued CI runs and deploys as a feed. Push banner: branches not on main per repo with PR CI dots. Main build status: last main CI result + sparkline of the last 10 runs.

Cards — Approvals: calls waiting with title + one-tap Approve/Deny, veto countdowns. Systems check: pass/warn/fail meter + top 3 issues with Auto fix. Alerts bell: unread by source (CI, deploys, builds, crashes). Claude badge: AI connection state, active model, last check time.

Cards — AI assistant: live sessions + last message, Open chat. Agent manager: agents (Mosses, Vinny, Molly…) with running/idle state. Molly guide: recent walkthroughs + Ask Molly. AI keys: active key per kind (masked) and how many saved.

Cards — Todo manager: overdue / due today / open by list, quick add. Voice notes: listener state + latest 3 notes. Session check-in: active Claude sessions with machine and repo. Snapshot manager: latest snapshots with one-tap Restore.

Cards — Plugin Manager: enabled/disabled/unhealthy counts. Plugin Update: updates available (Update all). Container access: master switch state + containers up/down. axHub sync: red/green live badge (hubLive rule), last sync. MCP client: connected servers + tool counts.

Cards — Brand library: logo of the day (animated, tap to roll). Theme manager: current colour/style/layout + Roll button. Context menu designer: saved menus + chunks count. Project wizard: recent projects. Claude handoff: kit freshness. Terminal: open tabs and their connections. Feature assistant: last drafted features.

Lifecycle: every plugin's cards/ listed in plugin.json and removed by uninstall.mjs --all; plugin-lifecycle check --after-uninstall for each touched plugin; theme checks (check-theme, theme-swap) over every card.

Tests (engine vs fixture, hidden cards stay mounted, show/hide all, plugin off), docs (_claude/memory/docs/home-cards.md, plugins README → Cards, STATUS), before/after Home screenshots at 412 and 1280 px, re-bake console.

before.title: PR browser + Batch Manager
before.detail: Brett, Oct 30 2026 (voice): Grid of push batches with live badges, Merge/Hold on rows, expandable PR sub-grid, failing check + Fix. Dense: small type, small badges, no clutter. Left click opens review, right click menu. PR BROWSER (Brett, Oct 31): a tab listing every open PR across AmberX-AXF, axHub and Build-Pilot. One dense line per PR with everything: number, title, branch, built by (agent/session), live checks badge, behind main, mergeable/conflict, in which batch, age, cost. Expand a row: every check with its error lines, files changed, commits, description, linked build/plan, and actions: Fix, Merge (via batch), Add to batch, Close. Sort/search/filter like every grid; live updates. ROW LEAD (Brett): every row starts with the PR number + a plain-English line of what it does (e.g. '#187 Audio Extract: pulls audio out of screen recordings, no mic'), written from the actual diff not just the title; badges follow on the same line. SCREENSHOTS (Brett): every PR gets BEFORE (main) and AFTER (PR branch) screenshots of the screens it touches, captured automatically by CI/headless browser (web) and emulator (Android); small before/after thumbnails on the row, side-by-side or slider compare in the expanded view, stored with the PR. SCREENSHOT CORRECTION (Brett): do NOT build a new capture system - REUSE the existing pre-build and post-build screenshots the framework already takes (find them first). BEFORE = the existing pre-build screenshot. AFTER: if the PR/build is not done yet, show a PREDICTED screenshot (rendered mockup of the expected result from the build spec + diff so far, clearly badged 'Predicted'); as soon as the build finishes, the real post-build screenshot replaces it automatically (badge 'Real'), live, no refresh. FEATURE SHOTS (Brett): the existing pre/post-build screenshots are NOT enough - they must show the ACTUAL FEATURE the PR built. Per PR, build a feature map from the diff (changed plugins, components, routes, menus, dialogs -> the screens and states that show them). Drive the existing capture tooling to navigate to each one, open it (expand the row, open the dialog/menu, switch the tab, put it in the right state with demo data), and shoot it: BEFORE on main, AFTER on the PR branch. Each shot cropped to the feature plus a full-screen version, web + Android. Brand-new UI has no before: show a 'New' card. Every feature shot shows Predicted (mockup from spec + diff) until the build is done, then the real shot replaces it live. Captions say which feature each shot is. Missed features (no shot) flagged on the row.

before.title: Session browser: Claude sessions + headless agent runs, live
before.detail: Brett, Oct 30 2026 (voice): a full-blown session browser for regular Claude sessions AND every headless agent run, monitoring in real time. Live grid, collapsible rows like every other grid: agent, build, job, model, status badge (running, done, failed, killed for budget), tokens, dollars, duration, started time; updates live. Tabs: Context (all text that flowed into its context and what it said back), Tools (every command and file edit), Conversation for regular sessions. Watch a running agent live and kill it. Links to PR/commit/file. Sort, search, filter. Built on Session check-in archive + Codebase changes log + the agent-swarm runner's JSON reports and stream logs. Prices everywhere: the row shows the run's exact total cost (from usage). Expanded 'what it did' shows a price next to every line (estimated: tokens of the turns that produced that change, labelled 'est.'). Context tab: cost per turn; Tools tab: cost per command. Totals at the bottom plus a per-model breakdown.

before.title: Framework grid: built-in sort, search, filter + Date and time column
before.detail: Brett, Oct 30 2026 (voice): Every grid that lists builds, tasks, asks or anything else is sortable, searchable and filterable, taking little screen. Basic filter attached by default. Tap header sorts, tap again reverses, long-press adds a second sort. One thin row: small search box + filter icon; on phones just a search icon. Filters hidden until used, then small clearable chips. Custom tables move onto the framework grid. Android parity. Per grid: right-click a grid or its header -> Filter -> off/on for this grid; 'All grids...' lists every grid in the app with the right-clicked one scrolled into view and highlighted, a switch per grid; a default switch decides whether new grids get the filter (on). Defaults are decided per grid by the build: on for data grids with many rows or columns (builds, asks, changes, plugins, PRs), off for small lists (settings, keys, short pickers); record the choice and reason per grid. On grids where it is off, hovering the header for a moment shows a tooltip 'Add the filter to this grid?' with Enable (long-press on phones). Framework grid (part of the app, not the filter plugin): every grid that has no date/time column gets an automatic 'Date and time' column (row created / last changed), hidden by default; grids that already show a date/time get nothing. Right-click the header -> Show/Hide 'Date and time'. Web + Android. UPDATE (Brett): build BOTH into the framework grid. Sort/search/filter live in the framework (not the Basic filter plugin); smart per-grid defaults, right-click on/off, All grids list and hover offer all framework features. Date and time column is ensured at first render: if a grid renders without one, the framework adds the hidden column then. New grids get everything automatically. CI check flags any table not built on the framework grid.

before.title: AmberX Audio Output Recorder -> axHub (no mic)
before.detail: Brett, Oct 30 2026 (voice): AmberX plugin that records all audio the phone outputs while it is on, saved to the server on axHub. One switch + quick-settings tile. Playback capture only, NEVER the microphone. Android 10+; system consent prompt each start and a notification while recording. before.title: Agent swarm: headless specialist agents, conflict-free, token-cheap
before.detail: Brett, Oct 30 2026 (voice): Brett's own agents aren't programmed well; Claude designs as many specialist agents as needed with specific skills. The build orchestrator splits each build into jobs and dispatches them to agents so many builds run at once without stepping on each other. Each agent runs its own headless Claude Code run with ONLY what the job needs: the task, the exact leased files, and the few relevant snippets the orchestrator pre-extracts (no CLAUDE.md dump, no repo exploring). Token efficiency is a hard requirement (sub-agents cost a fortune): cheapest capable model per job (small model for docs/manifests/renames, Sonnet/Opus for code, Fable only for design/contract work); max turns and token budget per run, killed when over; only the tools the job needs; shared skill prefix first so prompt caching applies; short structured JSON report back. No conflicts: file leases per job, overlapping jobs sequenced, shared files (notes, registries, catalogs, tracker) written only by the orchestrator after merge, pre-push lease check, batch merge. Cost meter: tokens and dollars per agent, job and build, visible in the orchestrator. Persona: every agent has Amber's persona (blunt street slang, heavy cussing, wild, still honest about builds), as the full few-line Amber persona (Brett: it's like five lines) in the cached shared prefix. It applies to reports and anything said to Brett; code, code comments and commit messages stay clean and professional. Agent statuses (set from a dropdown on each agent's row in the Agent manager, with a note): On duty (gets work), Off duty (skipped, keeps everything), Injured (keeps failing; no new jobs, flagged for a fix), Medical leave (benched until a date, then back on duty automatically), Probation (small jobs only, Brett notified every run), Fired (never assigned again, kept greyed in history), Custom (Brett names it and picks whether it gets work). The orchestrator only dispatches to agents whose status allows it. Spend per agent on its row: dollars and tokens all time, this week, today, average per job; optional spend cap that auto-benches the agent when hit. Sortable by cost. Status and spend also shown in the session browser. CARDS (Agent manager): one card per agent with photo avatar (unique look per agent), name, role, specialty on its own line, status badge, hiring date, spend (all time, week, today), jobs done, success rate, failures, avg cost per job, favorite model, last seen, Amber-style catchphrase; tap for profile: bio, skills, spend cap, status history, feed of latest runs with cost (opens the session browser). Social profiles live inside the system only, no real social media accounts. GROUP CHAT: a chat window like a normal conversation, switch to enable/disable for all agents plus per-agent; main room plus each agent's history on its profile. The orchestrator ('Boss') posts every assignment (task, files, model, budget) and lease decisions in the chat; agents report done/failed and hand off; banter in Amber persona (fighting over files, chilling, beer while Gradle runs). Work lines are built from orchestrator messages and agent reports (no extra tokens); banter comes from one cheap small-model batch; zero cost when off. DISCIPLINE: Suspend (Brett picks duration + reason; no jobs until it ends, then auto back on duty); Rage-quit (after N consecutive failed jobs, N set by Brett, default 3, agent quits itself and posts it in chat, status Quit, no jobs); Rehire button on the card puts them back on duty. All logged in status history and posted in the group chat. SALARY: each agent has a weekly salary that IS its token budget (replaces the plain spend cap); card shows salary, spent this pay period, left. Broke agents take no new jobs until payday or Brett tops them up, and say so in chat. Raises and pay cuts (docked) set by Brett, posted in chat by Boss. Finishing a job under its budget earns a bonus shown on the card (bragging rights, not real money). Coworker reactions in the group chat when someone gets a raise or bonus (jealous, cussing, Amber persona). Banter rules: no jokes about race, ethnicity, religion, gender, sexuality or other identity. CHAT SETTINGS SUITE: Vibe slider 1-500 (1 = straight to the point, no sarcasm; 100 = chill; 250 = full Amber; 500 = off the rails). The slider is a hard ceiling: every message gets a vibe score; anything above the setting is toned down or dropped before it shows. Also: chattiness (assignments only .. constant banter), cussing (clean .. filthy), drama (fights, jealousy, shit talk) sliders; per-agent overrides of every slider; daily banter budget in dollars (quiet when hit); presets (All business, Work crew, Break room, Off the rails) + save your own; live preview message that changes as sliders move. Color by vibe: a checkbox (also in the chat window's context menu) colors every message by its vibe score; Brett picks the base color; light near 1, darker as the score rises, darkest at the ceiling. ID CARDS ARE ASSETS (Brett, Oct 31): new asset type agent-card@1 in the asset@1 envelope, registered in asset-types.json, loadable by any AXF app on web + Android, hot-swappable like every other asset. Cards are BRANDED: logo slot (brand logo asset, top/watermark/corner per design) and styled ONLY from theme tokens (color-theme + style-theme), so swapping the theme rebrands every card. Ship 4 starter designs: (1) Corporate badge - vertical lanyard ID, logo banner on top, photo, name, role, employee ID, barcode; (2) License - horizontal, small-type fields, logo hologram watermark, ID number, issue date = hire date; (3) Trading card - big photo, foil border in the theme accent, stats on the back (jobs, success rate, spend, favorite model); (4) Backstage pass - dark, neon accent, status badge big, catchphrase. Identity fields editable per agent: name, role, specialty, photo, employee ID, internal email (display/identity inside the system only, no real mailbox unless Brett asks), hire date, status, catchphrase, signature, QR to the agent's page. Card designer: edit any design's layout/fields/logo placement and Save as new (new asset). Gallery to pick the DEFAULT design (Brett picks from a preview page rendered FIRST, before the rest of the build), plus per-agent override. Flip for front/back.

Fable-pinned s1-s3, s11, s12, s15 were built on Opus: Fable rebuild parked as agent-swarm-fable-rebuild.

Default card design picked as corporate-badge (headless run, Brett changes it in Swarm -> ID cards -> Make default). Android renderer deferred (Android on hold, PORTING.md). origin.said: Brett's own agents aren't programmed well; Claude designs as many specialist agents as needed with specific skills. The build orchestrator splits each build into jobs and dispatches them to agents so many builds run at once without stepping on each other. Each agent runs its own headless Claude Code run with ONLY what the job needs: the task, the exact leased files, and the few relevant snippets the orchestrator pre-extracts (no CLAUDE.md dump, no repo exploring). Token efficiency is a hard requirement (sub-agents cost a fortune): cheapest capable model per job (small model for docs/manifests/renames, Sonnet/Opus for code, Fable only for design/contract work); max turns and token budget per run, killed when over; only the tools the job needs; shared skill prefix first so prompt caching applies; short structured JSON report back. No conflicts: file leases per job, overlapping jobs sequenced, shared files (notes, registries, catalogs, tracker) written only by the orchestrator after merge, pre-push lease check, batch merge. Cost meter: tokens and dollars per agent, job and build, visible in the orchestrator. Persona: every agent has Amber's persona (blunt street slang, heavy cussing, wild, still honest about builds), as the full few-line Amber persona (Brett: it's like five lines) in the cached shared prefix. It applies to reports and anything said to Brett; code, code comments and commit messages stay clean and professional. Agent statuses (set from a dropdown on each agent's row in the Agent manager, with a note): On duty (gets work), Off duty (skipped, keeps everything), Injured (keeps failing; no new jobs, flagged for a fix), Medical leave (benched until a date, then back on duty automatically), Probation (small jobs only, Brett notified every run), Fired (never assigned again, kept greyed in history), Custom (Brett names it and picks whether it gets work). The orchestrator only dispatches to agents whose status allows it. Spend per agent on its row: dollars and tokens all time, this week, today, average per job; optional spend cap that auto-benches the agent when hit. Sortable by cost. Status and spend also shown in the session browser. CARDS (Agent manager): one card per agent with photo avatar (unique look per agent), name, role, specialty on its own line, status badge, hiring date, spend (all time, week, today), jobs done, success rate, failures, avg cost per job, favorite model, last seen, Amber-style catchphrase; tap for profile: bio, skills, spend cap, status history, feed of latest runs with cost (opens the session browser).
