before.title: Planner: select items and build them
before.detail: In Plan Studio, select any parts (single steps or features at any depth, or the whole plan) with multi-select, then click Create build to make one build from the selection.

notes.text: Brett: "Without AI." Select and create build must work with no AI: plain UI that assembles the brief from the selected items directly.

Brett: "So whenever you plan something, it gets a file that writes out what it would prompt AI to say. What it would tell you, but it doesn't say anything until you, unless you add it to a new build." Every plan item has a stored, prewritten prompt file. Nothing is sent to AI until the selection is added to a new build, and then those prompts make up the brief.

Brett: "You can view that file through hooks, the theater. The different steps, maybe the context menu. Or you can do multiple selection, make them rebuild and view the prompt that it generates. Without AI." The prompt file can be viewed per step (theater/hover view, context menu). Multi-select, then rebuild or preview the generated prompt before sending. All of it without AI.

Brett: progress tracking applies to ALL builds, not only ones started from the planner (builds already split into steps). Every build_start brief includes the check-off instruction, and the console reads the progress live for every build. Resume from the first unchecked step.

Re-added (lost in an overwrite): (a) AmberX task and checklist rows: click a row to see the text discussed; expandable rows show amendments; send a row straight to its own new build. (b) A build from the planner auto-ticks items as it finishes them; the brief lists the item IDs and tells it to tick them. (c) The console tracks progress live without AI, through the console API or a progress file in the build dir; no stopping or resending context; if a build dies, the next run resumes at the first unchecked item.

CORRECTION from Brett: the build manager already tracks build progress, so drop the console-tracking and progress-file notes above. NEW: every build (anything Amber or anyone starts) automatically creates a plan in Plan Studio and goes into a build registry. That plan uses the same steps the build manager will use, so they stay in sync (one source of truth) and tick off together, along with the linked AmberX checklist rows. Registry and planner are categorized by app, plugin, edit, feature, in collapsible trees with sorting and filters.
Brett: the build manager and the planner both read and write progress in the SAME registry, one source of truth, with no separate copies to sync.

Brett: backfill the registry: import every existing build (the 79 finished-but-not-landed, the running/queued ones, and landed ones, going back as far as the history goes) as plans with their steps and status, read from the build dirs, briefs, logs, and git branches.
Brett: each registry/plan entry shows its addenda and amendments: every later change, note, or restart (e.g. r2/r3 runs), in order with timestamps, in expandable rows. Backfill them too.

OVERLAP: token-usage-log-accounts-plan-studio-control steps 14-15 (orchestrator IDs/registry), 26-29 (parked plans, multi-select, right-click new build, checklist grid) cover much of this. Prompt-file/preview parts not covered.

# today: approve/deny axHub approvals inside the Dev Console

Brett's words (voice, Nov 6 2026): "It does pop it up in my approval, but when I click it, it brings me to axHub. I don't want it to bring me to axHub."

## Problem
When an axHub approval (confirm or veto countdown) is waiting, the console pops it up (approvals-banner / approval popup), but tapping it navigates to https://axhub.amberxai.com/auth/admin/approvals/<id>. Brett wants to stay in the console.

## Build
1. In the console's approval popup/banner (and any approval row in the console, incl. phone layout), tapping the approval opens an in-console approval view: title, description, the exact call/command, countdown if veto, and Approve / Deny buttons.
2. Approve / Deny call axHub's approval API server-side from the console (console proxy using its existing axHub auth), never by sending Brett to the axHub site. Show the result in place (approved, denied, ran, failed).
3. No link to the axHub page as the default tap. At most a small secondary "open in axHub" option.
4. Register console actions (e.g. approvals.approve / approvals.deny with id) so they work through console commands too, and make console_show approval:<id> open this in-console view.
5. AmberX phone notifications for approvals should open the console's in-console view, not axHub.

Follow CLAUDE.md and _claude/rules/RULES.md. Never print or log secrets/tokens. Tests for approve/deny from the console. Update help/docs, THREADS row, orchestrator entry, report. Don't land; leave it for Brett's go.

# Build: Headless progress file + lean CLAUDE.md chain
Orchestrator build id: headless-progress-file-lean-claude-md-chain (planner.builds). Follow the CLAUDE.md chain and rules as usual.

Goal: headless sessions never stop to update the console; they write progress to a small file the console reads. Cut tokens spent on the CLAUDE.md chain.

Steps (each ~10 min, commit after each):
1. Define progress file format + location per build (current step, status, last update, notes).
2. Headless runner (deploy/claude-headless.sh etc.): write/update progress file after each step without pausing. Use it yourself in this build from step 2 on.
3. Orchestrator: include progress file in every new build on registration.
4. Console: read progress file on demand and show where the build is.
5. Remove old stop-to-update-console behavior from headless sessions.
6. Audit the CLAUDE.md chain headless sessions load (files, size, tokens per step).
7. Headless: load a slim build brief instead of full chain; pull rules files only when a step needs them.
8. Load chain once per session, not every step; verify.

Tick each step done in the orchestrator as you go. Finish with README/help update, report, PR to merge queue.

origin.brief:
# Build: gizmo-rebuild-fable

## Brett said (verbatim)
"I want to use Fable on the highest possible thinking level on ultra code to rebuild Gizmo." "Go ahead."
Also: "I need more powerful controls over the background listeners for AmberX. I've had problems with the microphone... it's crashing with other apps, and sometimes it'll just do that sound over and over."

Thinking: MAX (AXF_THINKING=max / --effort max). Model Fable for every step.

Rebuild Gizmo (AmberX companion plugin) properly on Fable:
1. Review the existing companion plugin + shared claude-session lib + assistant-chat-mode fast path; keep what is solid, rebuild what isn't. Report what changed and why.
2. Talk mode works with the screen off / app backgrounded (foreground service), transcript in the chat, stop from the notification (replaces the stopped gizmo-voice run; reuse /root/axf-builds/gizmo-voice if it has useful work).
3. Mic / background listener fixes and controls: proper Android audio focus (yield the mic to calls and other apps, resume after), no restart loop replaying the start sound (backoff, max retries, silent restarts), one owner of the mic at a time. Listener control panel in AmberX + console: list every listener, on/off, auto-pause on calls/other apps, sound on/off, retry limits, status and last error, REST/MCP/CLI.
4. Fix the message box sitting under the bottom nav at phone width.
5. Tests, APK via CI, README, report, screenshots to UI Review, PR to the merge queue. Do NOT land directly. Tick pending items gizmo-voice and gizmo-companion where covered.

Nothing removed. One session, lean chain. Stay out of notes/tasks, badges and notification-panel code (other builds running).
## Addendum 1 (Brett, voice)
"I'm thinking maybe we should take Assistant out of AmberX since we just have Gizmo... there's a lot of bloat."
- Move what Gizmo needs from ai-assistant (server chat route, provider, turn router) into the companion plugin / shared claude-session lib.
- Then remove the old Assistant plugin from AmberX (UI, nav, server part, bundle). Gizmo is the only assistant in AmberX. Console's own assistant is not affected unless it only depends on the AmberX copy; check and report.
- Report bundle size before/after.

## Addendum 2 (Brett, voice) - overrides Addendum 1's direction
"It should be the other way around. Gizmo should control everything; the assistant should run off of Gizmo."
- Gizmo owns the chat engine: server route, provider, turn router, tools, sessions.
- Any remaining assistant (console assistant, AmberX) becomes a thin client running on Gizmo's engine, no own copy of the logic.
- Remove the duplicated AmberX Assistant bloat once it runs on Gizmo.

## Addendum 3 (Brett, voice) - the goal
"Gizmo needs to be powerful, hardcore. He's got to be my full Claude client. He's gonna replace the Claude app on my phone. I'm not gonna use the Claude app no more. It's all gonna be Gizmo."
- Target: full Claude app replacement on Brett's phone. Parity list to plan against: voice mode (hands-free, interrupt, screen off), chats with history/search, projects with instructions + files, memory, connectors/MCP (axHub services), web search + fetch, file/photo/camera attach, artifacts/docs, model + thinking picker, timers/alarms/calendar/location on the phone, notifications.
- This run: write the parity plan as a pending item with ~10-min steps (what exists, what's missing, order), build the core (engine ownership, voice screen-off, mic fixes) first, and as much of the rest as fits. Remaining steps stay in the plan for the next run. Don't pad; no extras beyond the list.

## Addendum 4 (Brett, voice)
"I don't really need chat history. I've already got the session logs in AmberX. Don't put that in Gizmo, that'd be dumb."
- Drop chat history/search from the parity list. Gizmo uses AmberX's existing session logs (link to them), no second history store.

## Addendum 5 (Brett, voice) - narrows Addendum 3
"When I say replace Claude on my phone, I mean my interface, my chat, my input interface. Just the chat part."
- Scope = the chat/input experience only: talking and typing to Claude (voice mode hands-free, interrupt, screen off; text input; attachments; streaming replies; tool use through axHub/MCP; model + thinking picker).
- Not in scope: chat history, projects, memory UI, artifacts, phone extras. Drop them from the parity plan.

## Addendum 6 (Brett, voice) - orchestrator-first, no resending
"I don't want you sending everything every time we exchange words. I don't want to resend the whole conversation... Everything I say is gonna go to the orchestrator first. Everything from Gizmo goes through the console. No AI. Until I send it to Claude."
- Gizmo input goes to the console/orchestrator first, plain code, zero tokens. Never resend the whole conversation; send Claude only what's needed.
- Console holds Gizmo input in a sorted, manageable queue (reorder, edit, group/split into threads, delete). Nothing goes to Claude until Brett sends it (one item, a selection, or a thread).
- Settings: Gizmo plugin carries a settings-interface ASSET (every settings interface is an asset) that attaches to the orchestrator's settings interface as its own Gizmo tab (Gizmo-orchestrator integration settings). Gizmo has hooks to open it. Gizmo's existing AmberX settings stay as they are.
- API/MCP/CLI for the queue and settings.

## Addendum 7 (Brett, voice) - searchable transcript database
"I want to be able to search them. I don't want them to be read as memory every time the project loads, but I do want a database created that is searchable."
- Build on PR #365 (ui-review-notify-audio: session recording + transcripts); don't rebuild it.
- One searchable database of every session transcript (full-text, plain code; optional local embeddings later): who, when, session, build, text with timestamps, link to the audio at that moment.
- NEVER loaded into context on project start or by default. Only queried on demand.
- Search tool for Gizmo/Claude (MCP + REST + CLI: transcripts_search, transcript_get) returning short snippets with links; search UI in the console recorder page.

## Addendum 8 (Brett, voice) - make the transcript search full RAG
"Go ahead." (make it a real RAG, search by meaning)
- Install Ollama on the VPS with a small local embedding model (e.g. nomic-embed-text, ~0.5 GB RAM, CPU only). Zero Claude tokens.
- Index every transcript in chunks with embeddings in the background after each session (niced, one at a time); backfill existing transcripts.
- Hybrid search: meaning (vectors) + keywords, ranked; results = short snippets with session, time and audio link.
- Still never auto-loaded into context; only on demand through transcripts_search.

origin.brief:
# Build: gizmo-rebuild-fable

## Brett said (verbatim)
"I want to use Fable on the highest possible thinking level on ultra code to rebuild Gizmo." "Go ahead."
Also: "I need more powerful controls over the background listeners for AmberX. I've had problems with the microphone... it's crashing with other apps, and sometimes it'll just do that sound over and over."

Thinking: MAX (AXF_THINKING=max / --effort max). Model Fable for every step.

Rebuild Gizmo (AmberX companion plugin) properly on Fable:
1. Review the existing companion plugin + shared claude-session lib + assistant-chat-mode fast path; keep what is solid, rebuild what isn't. Report what changed and why.
2. Talk mode works with the screen off / app backgrounded (foreground service), transcript in the chat, stop from the notification (replaces the stopped gizmo-voice run; reuse /root/axf-builds/gizmo-voice if it has useful work).
3. Mic / background listener fixes and controls: proper Android audio focus (yield the mic to calls and other apps, resume after), no restart loop replaying the start sound (backoff, max retries, silent restarts), one owner of the mic at a time. Listener control panel in AmberX + console: list every listener, on/off, auto-pause on calls/other apps, sound on/off, retry limits, status and last error, REST/MCP/CLI.
4. Fix the message box sitting under the bottom nav at phone width.
5. Tests, APK via CI, README, report, screenshots to UI Review, PR to the merge queue. Do NOT land directly. Tick pending items gizmo-voice and gizmo-companion where covered.

Nothing removed. One session, lean chain. Stay out of notes/tasks, badges and notification-panel code (other builds running).
## Addendum 1 (Brett, voice)
"I'm thinking maybe we should take Assistant out of AmberX since we just have Gizmo... there's a lot of bloat."
- Move what Gizmo needs from ai-assistant (server chat route, provider, turn router) into the companion plugin / shared claude-session lib.
- Then remove the old Assistant plugin from AmberX (UI, nav, server part, bundle). Gizmo is the only assistant in AmberX. Console's own assistant is not affected unless it only depends on the AmberX copy; check and report.
- Report bundle size before/after.

## Addendum 2 (Brett, voice) - overrides Addendum 1's direction
"It should be the other way around. Gizmo should control everything; the assistant should run off of Gizmo."
- Gizmo owns the chat engine: server route, provider, turn router, tools, sessions.
- Any remaining assistant (console assistant, AmberX) becomes a thin client running on Gizmo's engine, no own copy of the logic.
- Remove the duplicated AmberX Assistant bloat once it runs on Gizmo.

## Addendum 3 (Brett, voice) - the goal
"Gizmo needs to be powerful, hardcore. He's got to be my full Claude client. He's gonna replace the Claude app on my phone. I'm not gonna use the Claude app no more. It's all gonna be Gizmo."
- Target: full Claude app replacement on Brett's phone. Parity list to plan against: voice mode (hands-free, interrupt, screen off), chats with history/search, projects with instructions + files, memory, connectors/MCP (axHub services), web search + fetch, file/photo/camera attach, artifacts/docs, model + thinking picker, timers/alarms/calendar/location on the phone, notifications.
- This run: write the parity plan as a pending item with ~10-min steps (what exists, what's missing, order), build the core (engine ownership, voice screen-off, mic fixes) first, and as much of the rest as fits. Remaining steps stay in the plan for the next run. Don't pad; no extras beyond the list.

## Addendum 4 (Brett, voice)
"I don't really need chat history. I've already got the session logs in AmberX. Don't put that in Gizmo, that'd be dumb."
- Drop chat history/search from the parity list. Gizmo uses AmberX's existing session logs (link to them), no second history store.

## Addendum 5 (Brett, voice) - narrows Addendum 3
"When I say replace Claude on my phone, I mean my interface, my chat, my input interface. Just the chat part."
- Scope = the chat/input experience only: talking and typing to Claude (voice mode hands-free, interrupt, screen off; text input; attachments; streaming replies; tool use through axHub/MCP; model + thinking picker).
- Not in scope: chat history, projects, memory UI, artifacts, phone extras. Drop them from the parity plan.

## Addendum 6 (Brett, voice) - orchestrator-first, no resending
"I don't want you sending everything every time we exchange words. I don't want to resend the whole conversation... Everything I say is gonna go to the orchestrator first. Everything from Gizmo goes through the console. No AI. Until I send it to Claude."
- Gizmo input goes to the console/orchestrator first, plain code, zero tokens. Never resend the whole conversation; send Claude only what's needed.
- Console holds Gizmo input in a sorted, manageable queue (reorder, edit, group/split into threads, delete). Nothing goes to Claude until Brett sends it (one item, a selection, or a thread).
- Settings: Gizmo plugin carries a settings-interface ASSET (every settings interface is an asset) that attaches to the orchestrator's settings interface as its own Gizmo tab (Gizmo-orchestrator integration settings). Gizmo has hooks to open it. Gizmo's existing AmberX settings stay as they are.
- API/MCP/CLI for the queue and settings.

## Addendum 7 (Brett, voice) - searchable transcript database
"I want to be able to search them. I don't want them to be read as memory every time the project loads, but I do want a database created that is searchable."
- Build on PR #365 (ui-review-notify-audio: session recording + transcripts); don't rebuild it.
- One searchable database of every session transcript (full-text, plain code; optional local embeddings later): who, when, session, build, text with timestamps, link to the audio at that moment.
- NEVER loaded into context on project start or by default. Only queried on demand.
- Search tool for Gizmo/Claude (MCP + REST + CLI: transcripts_search, transcript_get) returning short snippets with links; search UI in the console recorder page.

## Addendum 8 (Brett, voice) - make the transcript search full RAG
"Go ahead." (make it a real RAG, search by meaning)
- Install Ollama on the VPS with a small local embedding model (e.g. nomic-embed-text, ~0.5 GB RAM, CPU only). Zero Claude tokens.
- Index every transcript in chunks with embeddings in the background after each session (niced, one at a time); backfill existing transcripts.
- Hybrid search: meaning (vectors) + keywords, ranked; results = short snippets with session, time and audio link.
- Still never auto-loaded into context; only on demand through transcripts_search.

# Build: ui-registry-shortcuts

## Brett said (verbatim)
"Let's go with a UI shortcuts plugin. All the UIs need to be in a registry. Every single dialog, pop-up, settings interface, main plugin screen, every UI element has to be an asset. Every single asset in the whole app and all its plugins, from a button to a pop-up to a link to a menu to a menu entry, every thing needs to be an asset. That needs to be visible to the API." "Create a registry so I can open them with my voice."

1. Audit: list what is already an asset (chrome assets, settings-ui@1, tab-group@1, jump-menu@1, control@1 screens/dialogs, voice-command@1) and what isn't. Report the gap. Reuse existing contracts; don't duplicate control@1 or voice-command@1.
2. One UI registry (framework contract): every screen, dialog, pop-up, settings interface, menu, menu entry, button, link across console, AmberX, Molly, axHub web, and every plugin. Stable id, kind, owner app/plugin, label, aliases, how to open it. Plugins declare theirs; a scanner fills gaps; CI check that new UI is registered.
3. API/MCP/CLI: list, search, get, open/show/trigger any registered item.
4. Voice: UI Shortcuts plugin opens any registered item by voice (aliases, fuzzy match), wired to voice-command@1 and Gizmo; user-defined shortcuts.

- Share the Ollama install with the Gizmo rebuild (it installs Ollama + an embedding model for transcript RAG); don't install twice. Setting to turn the model off; memory limit; unload when idle.

# Build: ui-registry-shortcuts

## Brett said (verbatim)
"Let's go with a UI shortcuts plugin. All the UIs need to be in a registry. Every single dialog, pop-up, settings interface, main plugin screen, every UI element has to be an asset. Every single asset in the whole app and all its plugins, from a button to a pop-up to a link to a menu to a menu entry, every thing needs to be an asset. That needs to be visible to the API." "Create a registry so I can open them with my voice."

1. Audit: list what is already an asset (chrome assets, settings-ui@1, tab-group@1, jump-menu@1, control@1 screens/dialogs, voice-command@1) and what isn't. Report the gap. Reuse existing contracts; don't duplicate control@1 or voice-command@1.
2. One UI registry (framework contract): every screen, dialog, pop-up, settings interface, menu, menu entry, button, link across console, AmberX, Molly, axHub web, and every plugin. Stable id, kind, owner app/plugin, label, aliases, how to open it. Plugins declare theirs; a scanner fills gaps; CI check that new UI is registered.
3. API/MCP/CLI: list, search, get, open/show/trigger any registered item.
4. Voice: UI Shortcuts plugin opens any registered item by voice (aliases, fuzzy match), wired to voice-command@1 and Gizmo; user-defined shortcuts.
5. Tests, README, report, screenshots to UI Review, PR to the merge queue. Do NOT land directly.

One session, lean chain. Stay out of Gizmo, badges, notifications code (other builds running).
## Addendum 1 (Brett, voice) - local assistant, no AI
"Without AI, I need an assistant that doesn't need Claude, that just knows my app. I should be able to tell it in plain English like: 'yo, make a notification to do this.'"
- Build a local, zero-token assistant on top of the UI registry + voice-command@1 + control@1: plain-English parsing with a grammar/intent matcher (no LLM), fuzzy matching, slots (names, times, on/off), confirmation for writes.
- It can: open any registered UI, change any setting, run any registered command, create/edit notifications and their style (through the notifications plugin's API), queue items for Claude (Gizmo queue) when the request really needs AI.
- Lives on the console; AmberX and Gizmo send it text/voice. 'What can I say?' lists commands. API/MCP/CLI.

## Addendum 2 (Brett, voice) - local LLM fallback
"Yes, we're gonna do that." (run a small local model through Ollama)
- The local assistant uses a small CPU model through Ollama (e.g. llama3.2:3b or qwen2.5:3b, ~4 GB RAM) ONLY as a fallback when the pattern matcher can't map the sentence: the model picks a command from the UI registry, never free-form actions. Zero Claude tokens.
- Share the Ollama install with the Gizmo rebuild (it installs Ollama + an embedding model for transcript RAG); don't install twice. Setting to turn the model off; memory limit; unload when idle.

# Build: badges-notify-followup

## Brett said (verbatim)
"Run a follow-up." (for requests that arrived after claude-badge-vps and notifications-control-panel finished)

Base: merge branches claude/claude-badge-vps and claude/notifications-control-panel (both finished, not landed) and build on top. Read their briefs' addenda: /root/axf-builds/claude-badge-vps/.brief.md and /root/axf-builds/notifications-control-panel/.brief.md.

A. Badges (one plugin):
1. Claude, axHub, VPS and AmberX badges in ONE plugin; move existing ones in (old ones can be disabled).
2. Per badge: show/hide, icons only or icon + label, label text, icon per state (ok/warn/error/off), banner order.
3. VPS account usage meter (5-hour + weekly used of total, reset time) in the same plugin; reuse the existing usage-meter widget code.
4. Configurable tap action per badge (drop-down, open screen, run command, toggle, nothing). Usage meter default tap = drop-down of every saved Claude account with credits left, reset times, active marker, status. Plain code, zero tokens, cached + refresh.

B. Notifications panel:
5. Groups (user-made, group on/off), triggers (event, conditions, thresholds, schedule), actions/commands on each notification (approve, open screen, run console command, custom per group). Editable in the panel and via REST/MCP/CLI.

Tests, README, report, screenshots to UI Review, ONE PR to the merge queue that supersedes the two branches. Do NOT land directly. One session, lean chain. Stay out of Gizmo and UI registry code (running builds).
## Addendum 1 (Brett, voice) - notifications architecture
"Everything's gonna go through the console. It needs to exist on the console, and then that sends the thing to AmberX to do the notification. It doesn't live on AmberX. AmberX just processes commands from the console."
- The notifications engine (registry, rules, groups, triggers, actions) lives on the console only.
- AmberX is a dumb delivery end: it receives notification commands from the console (show, sound, open link, action buttons that call back to the console) and nothing else. No notification logic or rules in AmberX; any that exist there get moved to the console.

## Addendum 2 (Brett, voice)
"Can I make it so a notification will be a vibration or an alarm or a certain sound, from the console?"
- Yes: per notification type/group on the console: delivery style = silent / vibrate (pattern) / sound (pick from a list, custom upload) / alarm (full-screen, repeats until dismissed). AmberX executes it (notification channels per style so Android honours it). Test button per type.

## Addendum 3 (Brett, voice) - bring to front
"When something is sent over from the console, AmberX opens it up and brings it to the front of my phone. If I say 'open up the console UI Review and bring this project into focus', it brings that right up to the front."
- Console command -> AmberX: bring AmberX to the foreground on the phone (Android full-screen intent / overlay permission as needed) and open the target directly: a screen, a UI Review group, a specific item scrolled into focus.
- New UI Review items auto-open this way (setting to turn off; notification is the fallback).
- Works by voice through the local assistant / Gizmo: 'open UI Review and focus <project>'.
- Builds on PR #365 (ui-review-notify-audio, truthful wake); merge its branch claude/ui-review-notify-audio first, don't rebuild it. APK change via CI.

origin.brief:
# Build: claude-settings-tabs-veto

## Brett said (verbatim)
"The Claude settings interface is getting pretty big. We need to organize it. Give it multiple views, one of them being tabular. If you have it on the tab view, you can set where you want them to appear and how you want them to appear: on the left, on the right, on the top, and the bottom, whether you want the words or an icon." "The veto and the approve are gonna be their own tab in there. Break it down and put it into tabs."
Also: "You don't need to run the 90-second veto thing unless you are writing stuff to the VPS."

1. Audit Claude settings (plugin claude-settings): list every setting, group them into sensible tabs. Report the breakdown.
2. Views: classic (one page, collapsible sections) and tabbed. Tabbed uses the tab-group@1 asset: tab position left / right / top / bottom, labels as words / icons / both. Settings for the view saved per device. Claude settings stays a settings-interface asset.
3. New tab 'Approvals & veto': per axHub tool (or group) choose allow / veto / confirm, veto hold length (seconds), pass durations; reads go without a hold, only VPS writes and account switches hold by default. Writes to the axHub policy through its API (owner-only). Show the current policy table live.
4. REST/MCP/CLI for the view settings and the policy tab.
5. Tests, README, report, screenshots to UI Review, PR to the merge queue. Do NOT land directly. Overlap check with pending item approvals-no-window-spam-on-approve-veto-only-for-vps-writes-and-account-switc; tick its veto step if covered, note it.

One session, lean chain. Stay out of Gizmo, UI registry, badges/notifications code (other builds).
## Addendum 1 (Brett, voice) - where the veto/approval settings live
"Those settings should not be part of the Claude plugin. They can be accessed by any MCP server, the API or the CLI. They can be in Claude settings, they can be in framework settings."
- The approvals/veto policy settings are their own framework-level settings asset (settings-ui@1), owned by the framework, not the claude-settings plugin. Store: framework settings. Exposed on REST + MCP + CLI.
- Mounted in two places as the same asset: Framework settings and a tab in Claude settings. One source of truth.

## Addendum 2 (Brett, voice) - predicted options first
"Give me a bunch of options in UI Review to pick from, like ten."
- BEFORE building the UI: submit 10 predicted screenshots (ui-review-predicted) of where/how Framework settings and the Approvals & veto settings sit in the main settings interface: e.g. own top-level Framework tab; a section inside General; a left-rail group; a settings home card; a gear in the banner; icon tabs top/left/right/bottom variants; a compact phone layout; a two-pane layout. Phone + desktop each.
- Wait for Brett's pick in UI Review, then build that one. The 10 are mockups only, no code written for the losers.

before.title: Plan Studio backfill: every build of the last 12 hours as a live plan
before.detail: Every build started in the last 12h gets a Plan Studio plan (verbatim said, brief, addenda, steps buildId-N, ticks + status from the builds store), linked to its build and pending item. build_start / claude-headless.sh create the plan on launch. Addenda = check-off item with said, summary, sub-steps buildId-N-M, ticked by the orchestrator. Fix: sync must not reset a pending item's status or drop added steps.

notes.text: Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

origin.said:
"Go retro. Go back to all the builds we've started in the last 12 hours. Make the plan, put them in Plan Studio and check off their statuses, all the steps, each individual step that's completed."

Plain code where possible, zero tokens for the sync itself.
1. Every build started in the last 12 hours (refresh-token-save, token-optimize, assistant-chat-mode-r4, md-chain-control, md-chain-default, notes-tasks-sync, ui-review-notify-audio, shipped-features-fable, claude-badge-vps, notifications-control-panel, gizmo-voice (stopped), gizmo-rebuild-fable, ui-registry-shortcuts, badges-notify-followup, claude-settings-tabs-veto, settings-sections-everywhere, and any others in /root/axf-builds newer than 12h) gets a Plan Studio plan: verbatim 'Brett said', the brief, every addendum in order, steps with IDs = buildId-N.
2. Tick each step that is done, from the build's progress file, report, log and PR state. Status mirrors the build (running / built / in merge queue / merged).
3. Link each plan to its build record and pending item; one source of truth with the builds store (no second copy).
4. Going forward: build_start / claude-headless.sh create the plan automatically on launch. Document it.
5. Fix: Plan Studio sync must not reset a pending item's status or drop added steps (today's bug on token-usage-log-accounts-plan-studio-control). Test it.
6. Report, PR to the merge queue. Do NOT land directly. Don't touch other builds' code.

One session, lean chain.

"Any time something in a plan is edited or changed, put that in Plan Studio as a sub-step, something you can check off. origin.brief:
# claude-accounts-edit: Edit button per account that reruns the wizard

(r2: r1 died at launch, account-2 OAuth expired.)

Brett's words (voice, Nov 6 2026): "Where it lists the accounts, I need to have an edit button next to the switch buttons... that runs the wizard again."

## Problem
In the console's Claude accounts list (ai-keys "Manage Claude accounts" view and the claude-accounts screen), each account row only has Switch. When an account's login expires, there is no way to re-log that specific account. The add-account wizard only adds a new one. Also: the wizard's "Save current account" fails with a bare 'VPS command failed, exit 1' when nobody is logged in (claude-account save prints 'nothing to save: log in or pass a token'); show that message in the UI.

## Build
1. Add an **Edit** button on every account row, right next to Switch, in every place the account list is shown.
2. Edit opens the existing add-account wizard bound to that account (pre-filled name/slot). Finishing it replaces that account's login/credentials in place: same slot, no new account. Per-build login copies for that account pick up the new credentials.
3. Show a clear state on rows whose login is expired/invalid (e.g. "Login expired").
4. Wizard: surface the claude-account command's own output on failure instead of only 'exit 1'.
5. Register a console action claude-accounts.edit (account id arg) so it runs through console commands too.

## Rules
Follow CLAUDE.md and _claude/rules/RULES.md. Never print or log secrets/tokens. Tests for the edit path (re-log replaces creds in place, no duplicate). Update help/docs, THREADS row, orchestrator entry, report. Don't land; leave it for Brett's go.

origin.said:
"We need a plugin that will let AmberX open up any website I tell her to."
(Context: amberx.open_url refused www.hostinger.com: "open_url only opens Brett's own sites (amberxai.com)".)

1. amberx.open_url (axHub device service) opens any http/https URL on Brett's paired phone, not only amberxai.com. Block non-http(s) schemes (intent:, file:, javascript:). Audit-log every open.
2. Setting in axHub (owner-only): mode = own sites only / allowlist / any site (default: any site, per Brett). Allowlist editable.
3. AmberX app: opens external sites in the phone's default browser; own sites keep opening in AmberX.
4. Tests, docs (decisions), PR to the merge queue. Do NOT land directly. If the AmberX APK needs a change, note it for an AmberX-AXF follow-up.

One session, lean chain.

origin.said:
"It's gonna be linked to our Gmail through axHub's MCP server, not Claude's. axHub is gonna connect to my Gmail, my Google Calendar, my Google Sheets. axHub needs to connect to my whole Google ecosystem."

1. Google service(s) in axHub: one OAuth sign-in (Brett clicks Connect in axHub web; tokens in the vault, refresh saved on every use). Scopes: Gmail, Calendar, Sheets, Drive, Contacts, Tasks (enable per service).
2. MCP tools per service (gmail.search/read/send/draft/label, calendar.list/create/update/delete/freebusy, sheets.read/write/append, drive.search/read/upload, contacts, tasks). Policies: reads allow; send email, delete, and calendar invites to others = confirm; other writes veto.
3. Events/webhooks (Gmail push, Calendar watch) published on axHub so the console can sync.
4. Docs (decisions), tests with a fake Google, PR to the merge queue. Do NOT land directly. Brett signs in after deploy.

One session, lean chain.

# Build: notes-tasks-calendar

## Brett said (verbatim)
"In the notes, task manager and to-do (one plugin), we're gonna add a calendar where we can set events and schedules. We can set weekly schedules. And it's gonna be hooked up to our Gmail / Google Calendar through axHub's MCP server."

Base: branch claude/notes-tasks-sync (PR #363, shared notes-tasks plugin); merge it first, build on it.
1. Calendar inside the notes-tasks plugin (console + AmberX): day / week / month / agenda views; events (time, location, notes, reminders); recurring + weekly schedules; tasks with due dates show on it.
2. Two-way sync with Google Calendar through axHub's Google service (build axhub-google, queued). Until that lands, local calendar works on its own; sync switches on when the service exists.
3. Reminders go through the console notifications engine (AmberX only delivers).
4. REST/MCP/CLI + voice commands (UI registry).
5. Tests, README, screenshots to UI Review, PR to the merge queue. Do NOT land directly.

One session, lean chain.
## Addendum 1 (Brett, voice)
"I need a really sweet interface for the scheduling stuff, the schedules. Make it sick."
- Polished, modern calendar UI (framework tokens + theme only): smooth view transitions, drag to create / move / resize events, colour-coded calendars, now-line, mini-month, quick-add bar (plain English: 'gym every Mon Wed 6pm'), weekly schedule editor with drag blocks, phone gestures (swipe days/weeks, long-press drag), dark/light. Phone-first, desktop great too.
- Screenshots of every view (phone + desktop) to UI Review.

## Addendum 2 (Brett, voice)
"Open that in its own window with multiple layouts. Open numerous schedules, days and weeks: a week here and a month there, and drag events from here to there. Attach an RSVP list / invite list to an event with a check mark of who's replied. Send automatic emails to RSVP people, or emails asking people to confirm they've read/seen it. It needs to update in the scheduler on AmberX."
- Calendar opens in its own window (windows@1 / dock@1); multiple panes side by side, each any view/date/calendar; save named layouts; drag events between panes.
- Invite / RSVP list per event: guests, status (invited / yes / no / maybe / seen), check marks, counts. Emails sent through axHub Google (Gmail) when it exists: invites, automatic RSVP reminders, read/seen confirmation requests (tracked link). Replies update the event status live on console and AmberX. Sending email = confirm approval (axHub policy).

## Addendum 3 (Brett, voice)
"Any replies to the emails get logged. They type their reply in a text field that's sent in the email; they have to reply in the text field so it gets logged in the system."
- Each invite/reminder email has a link to a small public reply page (per-guest signed token, no login): RSVP buttons + a text field. Submissions are logged on the event (who, when, answer, message) and update status live on console + AmberX.
- Plain email replies are also caught via Gmail (axHub) and logged on the event when possible, but the reply page is the main path.
- Reply page is rate-limited, token expires, no other data exposed.

Opus phase: the host plugin, six standalone add-on plugins, voice + API/MCP/CLI, tests, UI Review. Plan Studio: Proposed > Assets (proposed-fzf3). notes.text: Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

origin.said: "We're gonna build a UI asset designer, which will create assets with their manifest and their identifier. It's going to create separate plugins for the app menu designer, the nav menu designer, the toolbar designer, the banner designer, the embedded widget designer, the widget designer. These are not dependent on the designer, but the designer interface will inherit those other designers. The UI designer plugin will have add-ons, each with their own settings interface and the designer's interface." "Redo them all from scratch." "Make it a build and get the Fable stuff going. Make it super powerful: full-blown context menu, drag and drop, map-based. Every UI asset will also have a context menu section which gives you a preview of the UI, and informs you in multiple ways (tooltips etc)."

steps.text: designer@1 contract: host + add-on model (designer-addon@1: id, asset types, designer UI view, settings interface asset, designer interface asset, manifest fields, capabilities, drops, voice), the designer asset type (the designer's interface with inherit@1 copies per add-on), rules file + .d.mts, exported from core

Asset output contract: designed@1 manifest + stable identifier (uid, ref, revision, hash, origin), registration as a ui-registry@1 item (coordinated with ui-registry-shortcuts, no duplicate engine) and in the designer library index (designer-library@1, paths per output target); the embed asset type (embed-asset@1)

Interaction contract for every designer (designer-doc@1): one document model with families per asset type (toolbar, banner, nav, app menu, context menu, flat) and asset round trips, ops, multi-select, map canvas (snap, align, distribute, auto layout, zoom), drag-and-drop (parseDrop / canDrop / applyDrop), undo / redo with coalescing, the designer context menu + keyboard map

asset-context@1: the context-menu section every UI asset gets (identity with tooltip, live Preview entry, About, Help, Edit in its designer, Copy id, Where used) and assetInfo in every mode (tooltip, hover card, side panel, help text, say); MenuEntry gains tip / preview / disabled; data-axf-asset attribute contract

Fixtures + validators + checks: spec/fixtures/designer.json replayed by spec/check-designer.mjs (CI), both validators agree, starters (designer ×7, settings ×7, embed ×3), JSON Schemas, re-bake + shared-assets bake, PORTING.md row, DESIGNER.md spec, report, Opus steps written into the plan
PR into the merge queue (never landed directly), THREADS.md + STATUS.md + decisions.md, build linked (builds-live.mjs link)

# Icon Browser + Icon Manager (Brett, voice)

## 1. Icon Browser plugin
- Ship a starter library: download a couple thousand icons (open-licensed sets), stored as assets.
- Views: tree, grid, list, etc. Categorized, sortable, filterable, searchable. Tree thumbnails toggle on/off.
- Sources (configurable, any type): FTP/SFTP (credentials + root folder), MCP, REST API, HTTP/online, local folder, Google Drive folder, Google Photos album, Dropbox, etc. Per-type config form: credentials when needed, root/path, auth. 'Online' shows a big list of known icon repositories, each with a section for what's needed to access it (API key etc.). Secrets in the secure store.
- Packs: create icon packs by drag and drop between panes. Panes are collapsible and floatable.
- Tab groups: open one or many selected icons into a floating tab group, a docked tab group, or a pane. 'Open new tab group' spawns docked or floating; with a selection it holds those icons, empty it shows a + to add. Drag icons from tree to groups and group to group.
- Save a pack as an icon-pack asset.

## 2. Icon Manager
- Every UI and plugin gets an icon map (icon slots/tags -> icon). All of AmberX, Console, axHub, everything.
- List/grid of every UI with an icon map, filterable by app. Open a map, or open a live preview of the UI and drag icons onto the preview. Save / Apply makes it permanent for that icon tag.
- Global icon pack asset listing every icon in the whole system.
- Inheritance: assign a pack to the whole app (root), or per UI, or per plugin. The child overrides the parent.
- Save changes as a new pack: root/global pack, or a UI/plugin-scoped pack.
- Icon packs are separate from design/style packs. A design pack MAY reference an icon pack but does not have to.
- Switch packs globally; a randomize button reshuffles the whole icon set; generate cohesive packs that follow one theme/style.

## Rules
- Everything is registry assets, with API/MCP/CLI parity and voice control.
- Settings in categorized collapsible sections.
- Submit UI options to UI Review first (at least 3).

steps.text: Contracts: icon-map@1 (slots -> icon refs, scope app | ui | plugin, extends, inheritance child over parent) and icon-source@1 (kind, config, secretRef) asset types in asset-types.json; iconmap-rules.mjs + .d.mts (normalize, errors, ref parsing name | pack:<id>/<glyph>, resolve chain, randomize, cohesive generation), engine iconmap.ts exported from core; fixture spec/fixtures/icon-map.json + check-icon-map.mts; starter assets; validate --framework and schemas green; Kotlin twin recorded as deferred in PORTING.md
steps.why: new shared asset types + cross-port contract

steps.text: Icon library: framework/cli/icon-import.mjs (SVG -> icon-pack glyphs: path, circle, ellipse, rect, line, polyline, polygon; 24 grid; <= 600 glyphs per pack, sets split by category) downloads open-licensed sets (Lucide ISC, Tabler MIT, Feather MIT, Heroicons MIT, Bootstrap Icons MIT, Phosphor MIT) from npm into framework/icon-library/ (icon-library@1 index.json: sets -> packs, licence, counts, categories, tags), every pack a valid icon-pack@1; `icon-import.mjs library --check` (valid, in sync, size budget) wired into CI
steps.why: library format + converter correctness is a contract every port reads

steps.text: Runtime: rt.iconFor(name, scope) resolves through the icon maps (plugin / UI map -> app root map -> active icon pack -> framework glyph), React IconScope context, Icon.tsx reads it; settings keys axf.icons.* (map picks per scope, slot overrides) count as appearance settings so the hub look carries them to every app; actions icons.set | icons.apply | icons.pack | icons.randomize | icons.generate | icons.reset registered for voice / MCP / CLI; check-icon-map covers the runtime path
steps.why: cross-app GUI behaviour in the runtime + appearance contract

steps.text: Icon Browser plugin core (apps/console-web/plugins/icon-browser): plugin.json (lifecycle, commands block, help.json, builtWith), server part (library index + search from framework/icon-library, sources CRUD, private secret store in the data dir, packs save as icon-pack assets, maps list), web: page head, tree / grid / list views with categories, sort, filter, search, thumbnails toggle, virtualised grid; menu.ts entries; settings tab in categorized collapsible sections
steps.why: first consumer of the icon-library and icon-map contracts; shapes the plugin's data model

steps.text: Panes, packs and tab groups: collapsible / floatable panes (library, pack composer, details) on the dock engine; drag icons between panes to compose a pack; Save pack as an icon-pack asset (server writes it, runtime registers it); open one or many selected icons into a docked or floating tab group or a pane through WindowManager (openGroup / openFloating / addTab); 'Open new tab group' docked or floating, empty shows a + to add; drag tree -> group and group -> group
steps.why: changes how GUIs work across apps (window / dock engine use, drag-drop between hosts)

steps.text: Icon Manager page: list / grid of every UI with an icon map (console, plugins, axHub web, AmberX, Molly), filterable by app; map editor (slot -> icon, drops from the browser); live preview of the UI with drops onto its icons; Save / Apply makes the pick permanent for that slot; inheritance view (root -> UI -> plugin, child overrides); assign a pack at root, UI or plugin; Save changes as a new root / scoped pack; global 'every icon' pack; switch packs globally; Randomize; Generate cohesive pack (one set / style)
steps.why: cross-app GUI behaviour: icon maps for every app

steps.text: Sources: per-type config forms (local folder, HTTP, REST, MCP, FTP / SFTP, Google Drive, Google Photos, Dropbox, online repository) with credentials, root / path and auth; secrets saved to the plugin's private store by reference only; framework/schemas/icon-repos.json: the known online icon repositories with what each needs (API key, token, none) shown per repository; test connection; import from a source into the library
steps.why: forms and integrations on top of the contracts

steps.text: Icon maps for every app: framework/cli/icon-map.mjs scan | list | check scans the icon names each UI and plugin uses (console, plugins, axHub web, AmberX, Molly) and writes / updates their icon-map assets; CI check that no UI is without a map; MCP / CLI parity of the plugin commands checked (plugin-commands.mjs check)

origin.brief:
# Postgres: ONE true location for all data sets, in its own container (Brett, Nov 7)

Orchestrator build id: `postgres-console` (profile all, 7 steps) with Plan Studio plan `postgres-for-the-console-orchestrator-id-registr-anyx` — read both (`node apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/orchestrator.mjs brief postgres-console`) and follow them, with this change: Postgres runs in its OWN Docker container, not inside the console's.

Problem: the same data lives in 3+ places (builds store, per-profile orchestrator files, pending list, journal, plans, tracker/catalog, feature-ledger, origins) read by different tools, constantly out of sync.

1. Contract (Fable): schema for builds, steps, plans, blueprints, journal, queue, accounts/workers usage, Shipped features, origins, ID registry (orchestrator assigns every id). Migrations versioned.
2. Own container: `axf-postgres` (official image, pinned), internal Docker network only (no public port), named data volume, healthcheck, restart policy, nightly backup + restore script, credentials in the vault/env (never in git). Compose/deploy files + docs.
3. Importer: every existing JSON source loaded losslessly, counts/hashes verified, duplicates resolved with a report.
4. Switch every reader/writer (orchestrator, Build manager, Builds page, Plan Studio, builds-live, merge queue, MCP/CLI, AmberX, axHub) to the DB. JSON files become generated read-only exports for git/sessions. Kill file locks.
5. CI check: no code writes those JSON files directly anymore.
6. Tests + perf check. Add to Shipped features.

Deploying the container is a VPS write: prepare it, and leave a one-command deploy for Brett/orchestrator. Progress: append `<time> START|DONE <step>` to PROGRESS.md here at each step; don't stop between steps. Commit, don't push.

Migration design: import every JSON file losslessly, dual-write period, rollback, JSON exports stay generated read-only for git/claude-sync
Bundle Postgres into the console container with data on a persistent volume (survives redeploys), backups
Orchestrator is the ID registry: planner requests IDs, orchestrator assigns + registers build ID and pending ID
Switch readers/writers over (Build manager, orchestrator, Plan Studio, to-do sync, Codebase changes, MCP/CLI); kill file locks, use transactions
Query screen in the console (read-only queries, saved queries)

origin.said:
# Style override rule (Brett, Nov 7) — contract + enforcement

The rule:
1. Main apps — Dev Console, axHub web, AmberX, Patches — SHARE one style/theme/design. Their override switch is OFF by default.
2. Every plugin and every UI asset has its own override switch, ON by default. On first install it stores its own copy seeded from the shared style, so everything looks the same until someone changes it.
3. A plugin/asset override changes ONLY that plugin/asset. It never changes the app it belongs to, other plugins, or the shared style.
4. Turning a plugin's override OFF makes it follow its app's (shared) style live.
5. Turning an app's override ON gives that app its own style; its plugins keep their own copies.

Do:
- Find the existing pieces (app-style-override branch/build, apply-all-levels, appearance-asset-tokens, skins, theme engine, settings assets) and reuse them; finish app-style-override if it fits.
- Implement the resolution order in the shared theme/style engine (both web and Android twins where they exist): asset own copy (if override on) → app (if app override on) → shared main style.
- Switch in each app's and each plugin's settings (settings asset, no hard-coded UI). Migration: existing plugins get override ON with a copy of the current shared style; apps OFF.
- Write the rule to RULES.md and the brief template so every build follows it. CI check: every UI asset/plugin declares the override field.
- UI Review: submit the switch UI with three options (--choices).
- Tests for each rule above. Add to Shipped features.

origin.said:
Plan Studio: Blueprints (Brett, Nov 7)

FIRST: the queued build plan-archive (queue id hl-mw6dmjiy-7w) is SUPERSEDED by this one. Remove it from the headless launch queue before it starts (or, if it already started, stop it with tmux kill axf-plan-archive-* and discard its branch). Note it in PROGRESS.md.

## What a Blueprint is
A named package of plans in Plan Studio, like build profiles but for plans. Only one blueprint is active at a time; Plan Studio shows only the active blueprint's plans. Plans keep their exact structure (steps, sub-items, status, build links) inside a blueprint.

## Do
1. Contract (Fable): blueprint@1 (id, name, description, created, plans). Plans gain an optional `blueprint` field (backward compatible). Store alongside plans; orchestrator/build links unaffected.
2. Plan Studio gets a **Blueprints** section: list, create (name), rename, duplicate, delete (with confirm; plans move, never lost), move plans between blueprints (bulk select).
3. **Context menu**: Plan Studio's context menu gets a **Blueprints** submenu listing every blueprint; selecting one switches the active blueprint. Same switch available via control@1 (planner.blueprints list/add/act switch), MCP, CLI and voice ("switch blueprint to X").
4. Migration: create blueprint **"Existing"** (or similar) and move ALL current plans into it, structure untouched. Plan named "New Hire" (if present) goes in a new blueprint "New Hire".
5. UI from assets, no hard-coded styling; settings in place. UI Review: three options (--choices) for the Blueprints section + submenu.
6. Tests: migration keeps every plan identical, switch filters correctly, move between blueprints, links intact. Add to Shipped features.

before.title: Orchestrator: cheap redundancy check at split time
before.detail: Every build the orchestrator takes (add, import) runs a cheap duplicate check before it is registered: plain code, zero AI tokens, under 2 s. Checks the build and each step against the builds store (any status), Plan Studio plans + blueprints, shipped features / merged PRs, open branches + worktrees and the asset registry (UI steps). Hits go on the build as a note with a suggested action (reuse, extend, merge into, skip step, proceed); default proceed + flag, setting to hold for Brett; phone alert on a likely duplicate, answered in the orchestrator. Findings in the shared redundancy-finding@1 format feed the Maintenance redundancy report.

origin.said: Plan Designer in AmberX: voice plans at zero Claude tokens (Brett, Nov 7). Trigger: Brett says "let's make a plan" (voice, AmberX) or taps Plan Designer. It's part of Plan Studio, lives in AmberX (phone first; console view too). 1. Talk back and forth with a LOCAL agent: Ollama on the VPS (Brett is installing it), through assistant@1's existing Ollama provider. Small model (3-8B, CPU only, no GPU) chosen in settings; never uses Claude while drafting. Agent role: interviewer that asks clarifying questions, keeps an outline (goal, what, why, steps, acceptance, open questions), reads it back. 2. Voice in/out via AmberX talk mode (same mic/echo-safe path as Amber). Text editing too. 3. Draft saved locally/on the VPS as it goes (no loss on disconnect). Works if the VPS model is slow: show progress, allow plain dictation with no agent replies. 4. Send to orchestrator: one button/voice "send it" sends the whole draft in ONE request; the orchestrator (Claude) picks models, splits into <=30-min steps, assigns the id. Show the token saving estimate. 5. If Ollama isn't installed/running: say so plainly with the setup line; dictation-only mode still works. 6. UI from assets, settings in place, no hard-coded styling. UI Review three options (--choices). Tests (mock Ollama). Add to Shipped features.

origin.said:
Blueprints switch notes, tasks and to-dos too (Brett, Nov 7)

1. Switching the active blueprint switches EVERYTHING scoped to it: Plan Studio plans, AND AmberX/console notes, tasks, to-do items and lists (notes-tasks plugin, amberx.items, amberx.lists).
2. Items/lists get an optional `blueprint` field (backward compatible). Existing notes/tasks/to-dos go to the same blueprint the existing plans went to.
3. Global lists: some lists are shared across all blueprints. "Quick notes" is global by default. A per-list switch "show in every blueprint".
4. Voice: "add X to quick notes" always works; "switch blueprint to X" switches all of it. control@1, MCP, CLI.
5. Active blueprint visible in AmberX and the console (chip), settings in place, assets only, no hard-coded styling. UI Review three options (--choices).
6. Tests: switch filters plans + notes + tasks + to-dos; global lists stay; nothing lost. Add to Shipped features.

Addendum (Brett, Nov 7): permanent Global group
- Notes/tasks/to-do manager AND Plan Studio each get a permanent group called **Global** (can't be deleted or moved).
- Global holds repo-wide items: they show no matter which blueprint is open.
- Any plan, note, task, to-do or list can be set to Global (toggle + drag in), and back.
- Quick notes lives in Global by default. Replaces the per-list "show in every blueprint" switch: Global is that switch.

before.title: Patches/AmberX redesign: 8 game-style PREVIEWS for UI Review (no build until pick)
before.detail: Rebuild the entire AmberX UI (app and console) from scratch, ignoring the current look. Overall direction: make it look really good, like a polished Windows PC game UI — game-launcher / game-menu feel, rich depth, glow, motion, HUD-style panels, bold typography. Produce 8 distinct concepts within that game direction, each with its own style, colour theme and layout (e.g. sci-fi HUD, fantasy RPG menu, cyberpunk neon, racing/sports dashboard, tactical military, sleek AAA launcher, retro arcade, space strategy), and post each to UI Review so Brett can pick one. Reference: the Gizmo chat restyle from October. Brett's words: "The entirety of, of AmberX. Rewrite, rebuild the whole thing. Use its own style, its own design, its own color theme, its own layout. Just build that shit from scratch. Give me a whole shitload of fucking UI reviews to pick from, man." and "Make it look good, give it a really good, like a Windows game."

notes.text: Every concept must look and feel like a real, working desktop application, not a mockup or static screenshot: real navigation, working screens, real controls and states, using AmberX's actual features and data. Brett: "I love the design to look like a real application, dude."

PREVIEWS FIRST. Each of the 8 steps now only produces a preview (static mockup screens of what Patches / AmberX would closely look like in that style) and posts it to UI Review. Do NOT build any real app code. Stop after all 8 previews and wait for Brett to pick one in UI Review; only the picked concept gets fully built. Note: patches.amberxai.com (the Patches app) was deleted; the picked concept becomes its from-scratch rebuild. Brett: "before you go crazy building, I need some previews in the UI review. Okay, what it closely might look like."

ARCHITECTURE for the real build (after Brett picks a preview): compile Patches, AmberX, the Dev Console and axHub controls into ONE app with one look and one login. Front end: a game-launcher style home hub with a tile per module (AmberX, Console, Builds, UI Review, etc.) plus a sidebar to jump between them. Modular and stable: each module is its own service/container on the VPS with axHub as the gateway, so one module can crash, restart or be rebuilt without taking down the rest. Every module gets a health check and auto-restart; code for each module lives in its own folder on GitHub with nightly backups so nothing is lost again. MODELS: the orchestrator picks the model for every step; ignore the Opus set on the steps. Brett: "I want to do all those things but yeah the orchestrator is supposed to pick the model"

before.title: URGENT: rebuild pipeline — orchestrator IDs, splits, Pending→Queue, slot-driven headless launches
before.detail:
Rebuild the build pipeline from scratch:
1. Everything Brett asks for becomes a build sent to the orchestrator.
2. Orchestrator assigns a build ID.
3. Orchestrator uses Claude to split it into steps (<=30 min) and picks a model per step: Fable only when needed, Opus otherwise.
4. Build goes to Pending. Brett moves Pending -> Queue.
5. Orchestrator watches the VPS: connected Claude accounts, which have Fable, max parallel and free slots per account.
6. Whenever a slot opens, the orchestrator grabs the next build in the Queue and starts a headless session on it: Fable steps to an account with Fable, everything else to Opus accounts. Never launches right away, only when a slot is free.
7. Steps tick off in the progress files per existing rules; a monitor watches them and updates progress live.

notes.text: Reconciler: PR #384 merged

origin.said: You need to start the pipeline over from scratch. From now on, what I say, send a build to the orchestrator. The orchestrator is going to assign an ID. A build ID. He's going to use you to break it up into steps select a model Babel or Opus Babel when it's needed and then he's going to see how many subscriptions are connected to the VPS how many accounts are available How many, what's the max parallel for each one? And uh, if it's a account that has Fable, he'll send the Fable to that. He'll send everything else to Opus. He will, no, he will check the BPS to see what accounts have what slots. Available parallel. Dish out the steps, okay? The steps are marked. We already have the rules for how the steps are marked down into a, in a progress pile and blah blah blah. Updated in real time because you have a monitor watching the progress files. And um, the orchestrator starts starts the head, headless. The orchestrator then sends it to the queue, or he sends it to pending. Yeah, he sends everything to the pending. And I have to send them from pending to queue.

steps.text: Contract: add the `queued` status to builds@1 / orchestrator@1 / build-hook@1 (Pending → Queued → Building = running), a `pipeline` record on every build (account, session, runs, split, last run) kept across orchestrator writes, pending@1 shows queued as pending, derivedStatus keeps queued; fixtures and check-builds-store updated
steps.why: shared build contract across store, orchestrator, hooks and ports

steps.text: pipeline-core.mjs (pure): account capabilities (which account has Fable, max parallel each, limits), the queue order, pick the account for a queued build's next phase, slot-open launch decision, session-end outcome (requeue / back to Pending / failed), idle reasons, the split prompt + step parser (≤30 min, Fable only where needed) and a rules-based fallback split
steps.why: the dispatcher's rules are a contract every port reads

steps.text: pipeline.mjs CLI (IO): status | queue | unqueue | split | intake | accounts | tick; store writes under the lock (queue/unqueue/pipeline record/steps from the split); splitter providers (claude -p on a login copy, AXF_PIPELINE_SPLITTER for tests, rules fallback); intake splits every new build with no steps

Dispatcher tick: read VPS accounts + agent slots, when a slot is free take the next Queue build, make its worktree + brief (Brett said block + phase brief), launch deploy/claude-headless.sh --account on a Fable account for Fable phases / Opus otherwise, mark running + account + session; monitor events.jsonl + slots for session end → built / requeue / Pending / failed, relaunch cap; dispatcher state file for the console; cron line in deploy/install-console.sh

Idle alert + notifications: notify.json types (pipeline.idle, pipeline.launched, pipeline.ended, pipeline.failed) raised through the console alerts API from the host (AmberX push for idle: nothing running while the Queue has work, with the reason), keyed and resolved when a build runs

Console: Pipeline tab on the Build orchestrator page (Pending / Queue / Building columns, accounts strip with Fable + parallel + running, dispatcher status, Queue / Back to Pending / Split now, live refresh while visible); server routes GET /pipeline, POST /pipeline/queue | unqueue | split; plugin commands for voice/MCP (queue a build, pipeline status); help entries; Launch builds without asking ON = new builds queue by themselves

Tests: check-pipeline.mjs end to end on a scratch store with a fake launcher, fake splitter and fake accounts (intake → Pending → Queue → launch on the right account → session end → built / requeue / failed, idle alert once, slot cap respected); python route test; CI wiring; plugin-lifecycle check; existing suites green

Close out: report _claude/builds/reports/pipeline-rebuild.md, _claude/builds/README.md Pipeline section, rules + decisions lines, THREADS row, fold the overlapping builds (idle-alert-phone-flag-when-nothing-is-building, orchestrator-start-a-build-through-the-api-mcp-and-cli) as complete with this PR, commit, push, PR, link the build

before.title: Slot-aware plan optimizer (pre-launch)
before.detail: Before the orchestrator launches a plan from the queue, it checks how many parallel sessions are enabled and how many slots are open, then optimizes/refactors the plan to use all available slots: build a dependency graph of the steps, group independent steps into parallel tracks (one per free slot), keep dependent steps in order, and give each track its own brief. Re-check slots at launch time; if slots change, re-balance.

notes.text: Moved to the Archive from pending (console).

steps.text: Read enabled parallel sessions and currently open slots at launch time
Late account binding: no account or session assigned in pending/queue; when the plan's turn comes up, count free slots on every Claude account and assign tracks across all accounts to fill every slot
Step dependency graph for a plan (which steps can run independently)
File ownership: each parallel track owns its own files; steps only run in parallel when their files don't overlap; lock shared files (configs) so sessions don't step on each other
Optimizer: split independent steps into N parallel tracks to fill free slots
Generate a separate brief per track; merge/progress markers per track
Rebalance when slots open or close mid-build + end-to-end test

Model-aware slots: when scanning accounts/slots, also read which models each account has available (Fable limit hit or not); Fable steps only go to accounts with Fable available; if no Fable anywhere, only Opus runs

The header on Terminal windows that open when a headless session starts (shows the output pane and the context chain) gets squished on smaller screens: items overlap.

1. Make the header measure its available width (ResizeObserver, not just viewport) and adapt live.

4. Never overlap or clip at any width; check desktop, tablet and phone widths.

before.title: Orchestrator checks Shipped features before splitting any job
before.detail: When the orchestrator receives a job and splits it into steps, it first checks the Shipped features ledger (which must hold every feature the orchestrator has ever built). It must: not build anything twice; not break or redo anything already done; and if a step would conflict with or change something already built, notify Brett (AmberX notification) and wait before going on. Make the Shipped features ledger complete (backfill every landed build) and keep it updated on every land. Also standing rule: ONLY the orchestrator launches builds, picks model and account, owns pending/queue and monitors status; voice/chat sessions only hand it requests.

notes.text: Conflict flow (Brett): a conflicting step is moved to a special Conflicts section and removed from the build; the other steps still build. Brett gets an AmberX notification-panel item that explains the conflict and offers suggested resolutions; he taps a suggestion or types a prompt, which goes to the orchestrator, and the orchestrator makes a new build from it. Then test it: Brett will send a 3-4 step build that deliberately overlaps existing shipped features to confirm the orchestrator catches it.
Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.

Brett (Nov 9): "needs a way to go through all the pending builds and the build queue and search for steps that are gonna break existing work or conflict with it, or it's already done, or it doesn't need it anymore." Add a Sweep: a button on the builds page (and API/voice: 'sweep the builds') plus an automatic run on every land. It checks every step of every pending and queued build against the Shipped features ledger, main's code, and the other pending/queued builds, and flags each step: Already done (shipped by build X), Conflicts (would change/break feature Y, shows the files and lines), Duplicate (same as a step in build Z), Obsolete (no longer needed: superseded or its target was removed), OK. Results: badges on each build and step, a Sweep report with a filter per flag, and one-tap fixes per flag: drop step, merge into the other build, move to Conflicts for Brett, keep. Nothing is changed without Brett's tap. Cheap first pass in plain code (ledger + file overlap); Claude only for the unclear ones.

Correction (Brett): the Sweep does NOT run automatically on every land. It runs only (1) when Brett runs it (button / API / voice), and (2) by the orchestrator on a single build at two points: when it receives the job, and again right before it dispatches it (launches the session). Flags found at dispatch hold the build for Brett instead of launching.

Merged with orchestrator-checks-each-build-against-main-righ for the 'never build twice' part: every build is now checked against main (Shipped features, its PR, its branch, the files its steps create) right before it is queued and again at dispatch; done = closed, partly done = only what is left is queued. Still open here: the check at split time, the AmberX conflict notice and the ledger backfill.

# Build: orchestrator-checks-shipped-features-before-spli

## Brett said (verbatim)
> when he get receives a job, he splits it up into steps. And when he does that, he needs to make sure he needs to check with the shipped features... he needs to make sure he's not doing something twice or fucking up something that's already been done and if it's gonna conflict with something or change something that's already built he's gonna let me know

## What to build
Continue build "Orchestrator checks Shipped features before splitting any job" (orchestrator-checks-shipped-features-before-spli) — Phase 1, model Opus.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said:
"when he get receives a job, he splits it up into steps. And when he does that, he needs to make sure he needs to check with the shipped features... he needs to make sure he's not doing something twice or fucking up something that's already been done and if it's gonna conflict with something or change something that's already built he's gonna let me know"
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 30 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. Make the Shipped features ledger complete (backfill every landed build) and keep it updated on every land. Also standing rule: ONLY the orchestrator launches builds, picks model and account, owns pending/queue and monitors status; voice/chat sessions only hand it requests.
[ ] s2 (~30 min) when he get receives a job, he splits it up into steps. And when he does that, he needs to make sure he needs to check with the shipped features... he needs to make sure he's not doing something twice or fucking up something that's already been done and if it's gonna conflict with something or change something that's already built he's gonna let me know
[ ] s3 (~20 min) Tests green, report _claude/builds/reports/orchestrator-checks-shipped-features-before-spli.md, THREADS row, commit, push, PR
Read first: _claude/builds/reports/orchestrator-checks-shipped-features-before-spli.md, _claude/THREADS.md
Tick each step: node apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/orchestrator.mjs act step orchestrator-checks-shipped-features-before-spli <stepId> done — it reaches main at once (builds-live). Link your branch / PR: node framework/cli/builds-live.mjs link orchestrator-checks-shipped-features-before-spli --branch <b> --pr <n>.

origin.said:
Standing rule: anything with a UI must have API functions that can do everything the UI can (open, read state, every action, every setting). Voice control is the app's main selling point and rides on this.

1. Orchestrator: every brief it writes for a build that touches UI includes this requirement explicitly (brief template + brief writer). Keep it short.
2. CI check: every registered UI asset/control/plugin view maps to API operations covering its actions and settings; fail when missing; report gaps.
3. Audit: list every existing UI lacking full API coverage, starting with the glossary/index Demonstration Designer and Book Builder; fix those two here, add the rest as pending builds.
4. Deep link per plugin view (URL that opens it) so agents can open any UI on the phone.

before.title: Account health probe + failover + phone alerts
before.detail: A (new): probe every Claude account (subscriptions + API keys) on console load and on a schedule with a tiny headless session (no rules, no CLAUDE.md, no MCP): login valid, usage left (5-hour + weekly, resets; API balance/spend vs cap), models it can use. One shared account-status store every plugin reads (usage badge, Claude accounts screen, routing); routing only sends a job to an account the store says can take it with the model it needs. E: phone notification before and after the probe (type account-status). B/C/D are built by account-failover-notify (same branch line); this build stacks on it.

notes.text: Claude account: live (axf-account-health-failover--earl, own login copy)

origin.said: Account health probe + failover + phone alerts (Brett). A. Health probe (new): On console load and on a schedule, the orchestrator probes EVERY Claude account (subscriptions + API keys): a tiny headless session with a minimal brief, NO rules, NO CLAUDE.md, no MCP. It checks: login valid, credits/usage available (5-hour + weekly used/left, reset times; API: balance or last-known spend vs cap), which models it can use (opus/fable/etc.). It saves each account's status in ONE shared store all plugins read (status: ok / limited / no credits / login expired; credits left; models; checked at). Usage badge, Claude accounts screen and routing all read it. Keep probe cost near zero. The orchestrator only sends a job to an account that the store says can take it, with the model it needs. B. Failover: If a build still fails on auth or limit, mark the account out, update the store, and relaunch the same build on the next able account. Today 5 builds died in 1-3 s on account-1 (expired) and account-3 Hulu (no credits) and nothing retried. C. Phone alerts (AmberX): Notify on every account problem: which account, what (expired / limit / no credits), which build moved where, what Brett must do. D. One home per login: Each account's credentials live in exactly ONE store; every token refresh from any build/console/session writes back there. Audit claude-login.mjs, claude-token-save.mjs, claude-headless.sh, console AI keys for duplicate copies; find why account-1's refresh failed and report. Rules: Full API + voice + MCP/CLI control; settings in categorized collapsible sections (probe interval, alerts); tests; report, STATUS, THREADS. E. Probe notifications (Brett): When the console loads: send a phone notification that the account checks are about to run; when done, send another with the result per account (ok / limited / no credits / expired, credits left, models). Uses the AmberX notification panel (build amberx-notify-panel) as its type 'account-status'.

before.title: Slot watchdog crew member (Slot Warden)
before.detail: Plain-code watchdog (zero tokens) on the headless build slots and queue: every ~30 s checks each running slot against reality (tmux alive, claude pid alive, log advancing); dead / finished / hung -> release slot, mark build failed with reason (auth, limit, crash, hung), tell the orchestrator, notify Brett (type slot). Live status + intervention log in console and AmberX. Root fix: claude-headless.sh always releases its slot when Claude exits. Duplicate guard on launch and in the watchdog (reuses orchestrator-dup-check). Crew member Slot Warden on the roster.

notes.text: Moved to the Archive from pending (console).

origin.said:
Assign a crew member (agent profile in the roster, e.g. a 'Slot Warden') whose only job is watching the headless build slots and queue, all the time, in plain code (zero tokens).

1. Every ~30 s: check each running slot in framework/cli/agent-slots.mjs against reality (tmux session alive, claude -p pid alive, log advancing). Today 3 builds died in 1-3 s on bad logins but kept all 3 slots, freezing the queue.
2. Dead / finished / hung (no log progress past a threshold) -> release the slot, mark the build failed with the reason (auth, limit, crash, hung), tell the orchestrator so it can relaunch/fail over (account-health-failover build), and notify Brett's phone (AmberX notification panel, type 'slot').
3. Report: a live slot/queue status the console and AmberX show; a log of every intervention.
4. Also fix the root: claude-headless.sh must always finish/release its slot when Claude exits, even on instant auth failure.

Duplicate guard (Brett): The watchdog and the launcher refuse or stop duplicate builds: same brief/goal running twice (e.g. memory-manager-r2 and -r3 both ran). On launch, compare against running + queued builds (name stem, brief source, build id); keep the furthest-along one, stop/dequeue the other, tell the orchestrator and notify Brett. Reuse the unlanded orchestrator-dup-check branch.
