before.title: Console in its own private repo
before.detail: Split apps/console-web into a private repo that depends on a tagged framework version.

notes.text: Merged from build profile "main-framework" into "all" (one profile for everything).

steps.text: BRETT says go (rule: not until he does) and picks the dependency style: tagged framework version via git tag + `npm pack`-style tarball, or a git submodule. Record in decisions.md.

Framework packaging: `framework/cli/axf.mjs pack-framework <tag>` producing `axf-framework-<tag>.tgz` (core, react, ui, schemas, libs, plan cores) + a GitHub release asset on tag push (`release.yml`).

Repo split: create `MossesX/axf-console` (exists on GitHub first), move `apps/console-web` with history (`git subtree split`), manifest `location` + `repo.exists: true`, `_claude/` + CLAUDE.md via `claude-project`; CI there re-bakes from the tagged tarball instead of `../../framework`.

This repo: `apps/console-web` becomes a thin pointer (README + manifest `location` pointing at the new repo), `install-console.sh` clones the console repo; `deploy/` scripts and `android.yml` console job updated.
Verify: console builds in its repo against the tag, deploy on the VPS from the new clone, `/api/health` + `/mcp` ok; status + `build_step complete`.

steps.text: Design the one builds dataset in plan.json: queue order/steps/rework, parked model + notes + sub prompts, orchestrator phases/approvals, hidden/archived; status mapping pending ↔ plan; spec framework/spec/BUILDS.md
builds-core.mjs (pure): every view (plan, tracker, queue, pending, orchestrator) is a filter/sort over one list, with nested info per row (steps, notes, deps, linked features, phases)
Shims: pending-core, build-queue-core and orchestrator-core read/write through builds-core (same APIs); tracker.json generated from it; fixture spec/fixtures/builds.json + checker
Migration: pending.json (9 planId items attach, 91 become entries), build-queue.json, orchestrator.json → plan.json; dry-run report; persist + manifest data.shared updated
Run the migration (repo + hub _data), keep the old files as read-only exports for one release
GET/POST /api/builds, engine-rpc and MCP; pending_list/pending_change, build-queue and orchestrator routes keep working through the shims
Builds page: one nav entry, view toolbar (Plan · Tracker · Queue · Pending · Orchestrator), shared filters, ?view= in the URL; old pages redirect to their view
Table look (framework DataGrid) as every view's default, rows expand to the Pending card; Orchestrator view = same table with phases and steps nested
Nested info per view: tracker → group + suggested features; queue → linked features, deps, rework; plan → acceptance, ports, deps; pending → steps, notes
Grid columns (summary, date added, time, cost), toolbar Archive/Delete/Hide/Unhide/Open in, double-click multi-select (pending-grid-view s1-s6)
View switching everywhere: app menu Builds ▸ View, context menu Open in view…, shortcuts 1–5, banners open a filtered view, axf://builds?view=…, search provider
claude.ai Pending page maps to the new data; Build manager merge simplified (no de-dup needed)

Every build entry carries hidden date/time fields: createdAt (set once) and updatedAt (any change: status, step tick, note, sub prompt, model, edit) on the feature build block and every step/note (at/doneAt). builds-core stamps them in apply(); the migration backfills missing ones from pending/queue/orchestrator/history dates (never blank). Kept in plan.json and every export (pending.json, build-queue.json, orchestrator.json, tracker.json, hub _data) and in the claude.ai Pending page data. Hidden: not shown as columns, only in row details / tooltip.
steps.why: Brett Oct 27 18:15: date and time in hidden fields of all entries everywhere data is stored
checks: no entry without createdAt/updatedAt after migration

steps.text: Newest first, always: every view (Plan, Tracker, Queue, Pending, Orchestrator, Remaining/Live/Built/Sessions, banners, Build manager, claude.ai Pending page) sorts by updatedAt descending regardless of filters, chips or search; the old order/status/left sorts become a secondary key or an explicit per-click column sort that resets to newest-first on reload. Steps inside a build keep their own order.
steps.why: Brett Oct 27 18:15: regardless of filter always sort by recent at top (picked last updated)
checks: test: a step tick moves its build to the top in every view

before.title: Tools plugin: the Tools section as its own plugin, with a Tools tab in Patches web
before.detail:
Brett, Oct 22 2026: the Tools section is a plugin of its own, and Claude handoff depends on it.

- New plugin `tools` (plugin@1 + lifecycle): it owns the Tools nav section and the top-level `tools` application menu that tool plugins add to; it provides a capability service (e.g. `axf.tools@1`) that tool plugins require.
- Claude handoff (and any later tool plugin) declares it as a dependency (`requires`) and adds its entries through it instead of creating the section itself.
- For Patches: the Tools plugin adds a **Tools** tab to Patches web's app tab group (next to Console / Pilot / axHub). Patches itself runs the Tools page; it is not the console page in a frame.
- Patches web only for now (Android later).

before.title: Fix: switches and tab buttons dead inside interface tabs
before.detail: Brett Oct 27 2026: Appearance switches in console settings and the layout (interface) buttons at the top do nothing. Cause: AxfRuntime.scoped() gives a scope settings = Object.create(base.settings), so set()/clear()/reload() assign this.values on the scoped object and the shared settings never change (Main tab cannot be reached again from GizmoX Night / AmberX Signature). Fix: scoped settings forward every member except get to the shared registry.

before.title: Share Search: programmable grid toolbar plugin (search/filter bar + 5 buttons + advanced search), attach to grids
before.detail:
Brett Oct 28 2026 (claude.ai): make a plugin with a toolbar of programmable actions for filtering, sorting and searching grids. Toolbar name: Share Search. HELD: Brett said 'send to orchestrator and hold off on build' — don't start until he says.

Asked, in full:
- Toolbar config lives in one of several settings groups inside the plugin's settings interface (Settings → Plugins → Share Search). Set what each toolbar item looks like, how it behaves and what it does.
- At app launch, if the plugin isn't attached to any data (grid), prompt with a dialog to attach it: lists every grid in a grid with expanding rows. Can attach to several; each attachment has its own saved settings, look, style and actions.
- Search bar can be a Filter or a Search (switch in its settings); updates the list in real time on every keystroke.
- Toolbar settings are in a tab list inside the plugin settings: one tab per attachment.
- Quick access: right-click on the toolbar → context menu item opens that toolbar's settings in a dialog.
- The search bar's settings sit in the toolbar settings' Appearance section: a collapsible container with an 'Inherit from shell' switch above it, collapsed by default. When inherit is off the container becomes expandable and shows every individual style token and setting as in the main app's settings.
- Along with the search bar: 5 toolbar buttons configured to manage the grid's view and actions, plus a button that opens an Advanced search & filter dialog.
- Install the plugin on the Console NOT attached to anything, to test the attach prompt dialog.

Design notes (proposed, Brett to confirm at build start): default 5 buttons = Sort (column + direction menu), Quick filter (per-column), Columns (show/hide), Expand/collapse all, Density (compact toggle) + Advanced search button. Toolbar config stored as a toolbar asset per attachment so it's hot-swappable. Plugin rules apply: framework controls only (inherits app style), plugin-lifecycle@1 install/uninstall, builtWith, settings sub-tab of Plugins, snaps never overlaps (Oct 28 rule), context-menu link via rt.addContextItems. Clash check: pending-grid-view (Pending builds grid toolbar) and opus/orchestrator-grid use the same lib-datagrid — build after/with them; Share Search can later attach to those grids. Android twin of the grid-attach seam is a deferred gap (Android hold).

before.title: Approval history with costs: every approval recorded with details + cost, browsable in Console + axHub
before.detail:
Brett Oct 28 2026 (claude.ai): 'Add cost of approval every time something is approved and display costs, as well as all details and history of past approvals browsing. Can you alert when needing approval without stopping and restarting.' Context: he asked whether sending an approval and waiting costs tokens. Answer given: waiting is free, but each retry check re-reads the conversation (mostly cached). The 15 s x10 then 1 min rule costs about 10-15 checks per 5 minutes. HELD: queued, not started. Picks (cards): profile Refactor, held; history in the Console AND on axHub's approvals page.

Scope:
1) Cost per approval: every approval records the session's token/cost spent while it waited (number of checks, tokens in/out, cached vs not, USD from framework/schemas/model-pricing.json), plus the time it waited and who/what asked (session, surface, machine, build ref, reason title/description, exact call, result).
2) History browser: every past approval with all details and its cost; filter/sort/search, totals per day/build/session. Console = History view in the approvals-banner plugin (framework DataGrid, expanding rows). axHub = same list on its approvals page. Approve stays on the first screen.
3) Alert without stopping/restarting: a hub-side wait (axhub tool, e.g. approvals.wait / long-poll on the confirmation id, up to ~10 min per call) so a session makes ONE call that returns the moment Brett approves. No retry loop and no session restart. The AmberX app push (already shipped, amberx-push) fires when the approval is created. Then update the shared retry rule (15 s x10, then 1 min) to 'one wait call, re-issued only if it times out' — Brett to confirm that rule change at build time.
Work spans MossesX/axHub (wait tool, cost fields, approvals page history) and AXF (approvals-banner History view, cost capture via codebase-changes hooks / session transcript).

before.title: Windows-style Terminal (Claude Code tabs, connections, profiles) + window snap/resize + settings levels toolbar & level editor
before.detail:
Brett Oct 28 2026 (claude.ai): "Add those plus build a powerful terminal plugin that looks and feels and behaves exactly like a Windows program." Asked, in full:
- 'Those' = the four window gaps: resize from every edge/corner (touch too), snapping (no overlap), keep windows on screen, drop a window on another to split.
- Terminal: native Windows look and feel, no Linux feel. Dockable/undockable, draggable, minimizable, snappable window that opens floating by default. Powerful configuration, preferences and customization with an easy interface.
- A toolbar button adds a tab running Claude Code and prompts for one of the available connections (VPS root, specific containers, axHub, console…). Right-click any tab = interface to manage that tab's connection from the available ones. Claude Code tabs get extra customization profiles.
- From now on every settings interface has a default-on, hideable toolbar that picks Simple / Basic / Administrator / Developer; the available settings show in a collapsible container and the rest in another. Administrator shows them all. Levels: Pro becomes Administrator, Advanced becomes Developer (Brett's pick); Administrator shows everything.
- A switch in settings opens a dialog with two columns: left = sortable categorized tree of every setting in the interface, one colour when available to the selected level, another when not; multi-select; toolbar buttons or right-click 'Add to visible'; right tree shows what's on. The settings interface changes live with every selection.

Upgrades the existing console-terminal plugin (one instance per plugin; it already has container/console/VPS/Claude Code tabs, Mosh mode, xterm 5.3). Folds in apply-all-levels-fable s3 (settings-ui@1 levels review). Patches is paused: its baked copy is skipped. Android twins deferred (PORTING.md).

before.title: Feature Matrix plugin: a skip/keep feature matrix for every build, one dataset, hooks in every builds grid, Apply updates status everywhere
before.detail:
Brett Oct 28 2026 (claude.ai, windows-terminal chat): "Make a plugin to build a feature matrix just like this [the windows-terminal scope list: https://claude.ai/artifact/CwBGQof4NBe4F3dPTczBvS] for every build and put hooks to them in every builds grid in orchestrator, pending, queued, build manager, etc. I need to be able to access its associated matrix from any entry in any grid. All matrix are compiled into 1 dataset that lists each one in expandable rows that open to display its matrix. The grid has column with date added and time cost to build generated by the matrix. When matrix changes an apply button lights up that updates the status across all tables. Nothing is ever removed only set for skip when time comes to build. They can be added removed whenever they never leave the matrix."

Rules from the ask: every build has a matrix (feature items grouped, each with minutes, model Fable/Opus, why); tick = keep, untick = skip; items can be added at any time and are NEVER deleted ("removed" = skip; skipped items stay in the matrix and are skipped when the build runs). One dataset of all matrices, shown as a grid of expandable rows (row = build; columns include date added and the time cost computed from the kept items); a row opens to its matrix. Editing a matrix lights an Apply button; Apply pushes the new totals/skips/status to every table (orchestrator, pending, build queue, build manager, plan…). Every builds grid gets a hook (row button + right-click) that opens that entry's matrix.

Brett's picks: Refactor profile; standalone plugin (builds-one-page removed); built in its own chat thread. Seed: the windows-terminal scope list (23 items, its db doc scope/selection) becomes the first matrix. Overlaps: share-search s1 (grid-attach@1: grid registry) — the hook seam here should be the same registry or forward-compatible with it; basic-filter (running, PR #155) attaches to datasets too.

before.title: Run unless blocked: 2-min countdown → urgent alarm (red banner + loud AmberX ring) → 1-min grace → runs; Block anytime; zero session tokens
before.detail:
Brett Oct 28 2026 (claude.ai): 'Can you send notification that a command is about to be ran and I can intercept it from the banner and block it before axhub tries sending it.' HELD: queued, not started. Picks (cards): profile Refactor, held; countdown 2 minutes.

Design: a third tool policy next to allow / confirm, e.g. 'veto' (run unless blocked). A session's call returns a job id at once; axHub holds the call for the countdown (default 2 min, per-tool override possible later) and immediately pushes through the AmberX app (rule: all axHub pushes come from AmberX) and shows it in the console's banner (approvals banner or its own) with the reason title, the exact call, a live countdown, Block and Run now. No action = runs at zero. Block = cancelled, never runs, the session sees 'blocked' when it next looks at the job. Sessions never poll during the countdown: they carry on and read the job result once at the end only if they need it, which saves the re-read cost of approval checks. Approvals (confirm) stay for risky calls: deletes and free-form root shell. Brett picks which tools move to veto (proposal: merge-pr, redeploys, container restarts). before.title: Console Home cards: card@1 asset plugins carry, Home detects/shows/hides every card (always rendered), card layouts, cards for every data plugin
before.detail:
Brett, Oct 29 2026: "Design a bunch more cards for the console home screen. If plugins with data or dynamic content don't have a card, design one for them from scratch (you decide what to display and how). Plugins can now carry cards that can be designed in the future SDK and attached to the plugin as assets. Console Home detects all card assets attached to plugins and shows or hides them, but always rendered. The card layout can show or hide all cards detected."

Decisions (cards): profile Angel (new, this is its first build; nothing built in the asking session); Fable contract first, then Opus.
Card designs: one per plugin with data/dynamic content (31 plugins + 5 existing Home cards). No card: _template, basic-filter, plugin-switches, plugins-menu (tools with no data of their own).
Clash check Oct 29: no open build touches Home or cards (refactor profile all complete; main-framework pending items unrelated).

notes.text: Reconciler: branch angel/home-cards-queue (PR #171); PR #171; PR #171 merged

Replaced by urgent build home-cards-live (Nov 3 2026, Brett: "I shouldn't need to build cards. I should draw dynamic data."). No hand-built card per plugin; one card engine draws any plugin read command.
Merged from build profile "angel" into "all" (one profile for everything).
Shipped manifest sm-home-cards rev 1 sent to Shipped features (backfill): landed b2351e130, 10 file(s), 0 test line(s), 18 open.

origin.said: Design a bunch more cards for the console home screen. If plugins with data or dynamic content don't have a card, design one for them from scratch (you decide what to display and how). Plugins can now carry cards that can be designed in the future SDK and attached to the plugin as assets. Console Home detects all card assets attached to plugins and shows or hides them, but always rendered. The card layout can show or hide all cards detected.

steps.text: card@1 asset type in framework/schemas/asset-types.json (+ axf schemas): id, owner (plugin id or "console"), title, icon, kind (stat | list | meter | chart | feed | status | actions | custom), size (s | m | l | wide | tall), data {service (plugin_services capability), path, refreshSec, live:boolean}, slots (headline, value, sub, rows, sparkline, actions), emptyState, actions (ids run through the action engine), level (Simple/Basic/Developer/Administrator), minRole (UAC), defaultVisible, order, category. Open registry: unknown kinds render the custom slot, never fail.

plugin@1 gets `cards: ["cards/<id>.json", …]` (card assets ship inside the plugin folder, so plugin-lifecycle@1 removes them on uninstall); plugin-inventory@1 engine lists each plugin's cards (framework/core/engines/plugins.ts + server/engine.py twin) so anything can detect them; future card SDK attaches cards to a plugin by writing this list.

home-cards@1 engine (TS reference, framework/core/engines/cards.ts): collects every card from enabled plugins + console-owned cards, applies saved visibility/order/size, level and role; hidden cards stay in the output with `hidden: true` so Home ALWAYS renders (mounts) every card and only hides it (instant show, data kept warm). Fixture spec/fixtures/home-cards.json; Kotlin twin recorded as a deferred gap in PORTING.md (Android on hold).

card-layout@1 asset type: columns per window class (compact/medium/expanded), gap + density tokens, grouping (none | plugin | category), "show all / hide all" default, sort (manual | category | plugin). 3 starter layouts: grid-auto, two-column-dashboard, compact-list. Hot-swap via runtime.swap('card-layout', id); tokens only (THEMING.md).

Placeholders for the future card SDK: `axf.cards@1` capability service (list/register/unregister cards at runtime), extension point `home.cards`, typed NotImplemented card designer entry, so a designer plugin can later author card assets and attach them to any plugin without kernel changes.

Home renders from the home-cards engine. The 5 cards already there become console-owned card assets: Plan summary, Build summary, Coverage, Project, Recent installs & imports. Same look at the default theme.

Card layout toolbar on Home (hideable): Show all · Hide all · layout picker (card-layout assets) · group by · a Cards checklist popover with one switch per detected card. Right-click a card: Hide card · Card size · Open plugin · Plugin settings. Drag to reorder. Saved per user in settings (synced through axHub like the rest).
Settings → Home cards tab (with the level toolbar rule): every detected card grouped by plugin, switch + size + order, layout default; a card whose plugin is disabled shows greyed "plugin off".

Cards — Build orchestrator: next step + model chip, approvals waiting (one-tap), phase progress bar per open build. Build manager: remaining work split Fable/Opus, hours + cost left, top 3 builds. Build profiles: active profile chip + pending/queue/orchestrator counts for each profile, switch button.

Cards — Feature matrix: kept vs skipped minutes per build, matrices with unapplied changes (Apply button). Fable rebuilds: parked count, Fable hours left, next rebuild. Changes & features grid: latest 5 changes/features with state dots.

Cards — Codebase changes: live/running entries with heartbeat age and current step. Activity: running/queued CI runs and deploys as a feed. Push banner: branches not on main per repo with PR CI dots. Main build status: last main CI result + sparkline of the last 10 runs.

Cards — Approvals: calls waiting with title + one-tap Approve/Deny, veto countdowns. Systems check: pass/warn/fail meter + top 3 issues with Auto fix. Alerts bell: unread by source (CI, deploys, builds, crashes). Claude badge: AI connection state, active model, last check time.

Cards — AI assistant: live sessions + last message, Open chat. Agent manager: agents (Mosses, Vinny, Molly…) with running/idle state. Molly guide: recent walkthroughs + Ask Molly. AI keys: active key per kind (masked) and how many saved.

Cards — Todo manager: overdue / due today / open by list, quick add. Voice notes: listener state + latest 3 notes. Session check-in: active Claude sessions with machine and repo. Snapshot manager: latest snapshots with one-tap Restore.

Cards — Plugin Manager: enabled/disabled/unhealthy counts. Plugin Update: updates available (Update all). Container access: master switch state + containers up/down. axHub sync: red/green live badge (hubLive rule), last sync. MCP client: connected servers + tool counts.

Cards — Brand library: logo of the day (animated, tap to roll). Theme manager: current colour/style/layout + Roll button. Context menu designer: saved menus + chunks count. Project wizard: recent projects. Claude handoff: kit freshness. Terminal: open tabs and their connections. Feature assistant: last drafted features.

Lifecycle: every plugin's cards/ listed in plugin.json and removed by uninstall.mjs --all; plugin-lifecycle check --after-uninstall for each touched plugin; theme checks (check-theme, theme-swap) over every card.

Tests (engine vs fixture, hidden cards stay mounted, show/hide all, plugin off), docs (_claude/memory/docs/home-cards.md, plugins README → Cards, STATUS), before/after Home screenshots at 412 and 1280 px, re-bake console.

before.title: PR browser + Batch Manager
before.detail: Brett, Oct 30 2026 (voice): Grid of push batches with live badges, Merge/Hold on rows, expandable PR sub-grid, failing check + Fix. Dense: small type, small badges, no clutter. Left click opens review, right click menu. PR BROWSER (Brett, Oct 31): a tab listing every open PR across AmberX-AXF, axHub and Build-Pilot. One dense line per PR with everything: number, title, branch, built by (agent/session), live checks badge, behind main, mergeable/conflict, in which batch, age, cost. Expand a row: every check with its error lines, files changed, commits, description, linked build/plan, and actions: Fix, Merge (via batch), Add to batch, Close. Sort/search/filter like every grid; live updates. ROW LEAD (Brett): every row starts with the PR number + a plain-English line of what it does (e.g. '#187 Audio Extract: pulls audio out of screen recordings, no mic'), written from the actual diff not just the title; badges follow on the same line. SCREENSHOTS (Brett): every PR gets BEFORE (main) and AFTER (PR branch) screenshots of the screens it touches, captured automatically by CI/headless browser (web) and emulator (Android); small before/after thumbnails on the row, side-by-side or slider compare in the expanded view, stored with the PR. SCREENSHOT CORRECTION (Brett): do NOT build a new capture system - REUSE the existing pre-build and post-build screenshots the framework already takes (find them first). BEFORE = the existing pre-build screenshot. AFTER: if the PR/build is not done yet, show a PREDICTED screenshot (rendered mockup of the expected result from the build spec + diff so far, clearly badged 'Predicted'); as soon as the build finishes, the real post-build screenshot replaces it automatically (badge 'Real'), live, no refresh. FEATURE SHOTS (Brett): the existing pre/post-build screenshots are NOT enough - they must show the ACTUAL FEATURE the PR built. Per PR, build a feature map from the diff (changed plugins, components, routes, menus, dialogs -> the screens and states that show them). Drive the existing capture tooling to navigate to each one, open it (expand the row, open the dialog/menu, switch the tab, put it in the right state with demo data), and shoot it: BEFORE on main, AFTER on the PR branch. Each shot cropped to the feature plus a full-screen version, web + Android. Brand-new UI has no before: show a 'New' card. Every feature shot shows Predicted (mockup from spec + diff) until the build is done, then the real shot replaces it live. Captions say which feature each shot is. Missed features (no shot) flagged on the row.

Left click opens review, right click menu. PR BROWSER (Brett, Oct 31): a tab listing every open PR across AmberX-AXF, axHub and Build-Pilot. One dense line per PR with everything: number, title, branch, built by (agent/session), live checks badge, behind main, mergeable/conflict, in which batch, age, cost. Expand a row: every check with its error lines, files changed, commits, description, linked build/plan, and actions: Fix, Merge (via batch), Add to batch, Close. Sort/search/filter like every grid; live updates. ROW LEAD (Brett): every row starts with the PR number + a plain-English line of what it does (e.g. '#187 Audio Extract: pulls audio out of screen recordings, no mic'), written from the actual diff not just the title; badges follow on the same line. SCREENSHOTS (Brett): every PR gets BEFORE (main) and AFTER (PR branch) screenshots of the screens it touches, captured automatically by CI/headless browser (web) and emulator (Android); small before/after thumbnails on the row, side-by-side or slider compare in the expanded view, stored with the PR. SCREENSHOT CORRECTION (Brett): do NOT build a new capture system - REUSE the existing pre-build and post-build screenshots the framework already takes (find them first). BEFORE = the existing pre-build screenshot. AFTER: if the PR/build is not done yet, show a PREDICTED screenshot (rendered mockup of the expected result from the build spec + diff so far, clearly badged 'Predicted'); as soon as the build finishes, the real post-build screenshot replaces it automatically (badge 'Real'), live, no refresh. FEATURE SHOTS (Brett): the existing pre/post-build screenshots are NOT enough - they must show the ACTUAL FEATURE the PR built. Per PR, build a feature map from the diff (changed plugins, components, routes, menus, dialogs -> the screens and states that show them). Drive the existing capture tooling to navigate to each one, open it (expand the row, open the dialog/menu, switch the tab, put it in the right state with demo data), and shoot it: BEFORE on main, AFTER on the PR branch. Each shot cropped to the feature plus a full-screen version, web + Android. Brand-new UI has no before: show a 'New' card. Every feature shot shows Predicted (mockup from spec + diff) until the build is done, then the real shot replaces it live. Captions say which feature each shot is. Missed features (no shot) flagged on the row.

before.title: Framework grid: built-in sort, search, filter + Date and time column
before.detail: Brett, Oct 30 2026 (voice): Every grid that lists builds, tasks, asks or anything else is sortable, searchable and filterable, taking little screen. Basic filter attached by default. Tap header sorts, tap again reverses, long-press adds a second sort. One thin row: small search box + filter icon; on phones just a search icon. Filters hidden until used, then small clearable chips. Custom tables move onto the framework grid. Android parity. Per grid: right-click a grid or its header -> Filter -> off/on for this grid; 'All grids...' lists every grid in the app with the right-clicked one scrolled into view and highlighted, a switch per grid; a default switch decides whether new grids get the filter (on). Defaults are decided per grid by the build: on for data grids with many rows or columns (builds, asks, changes, plugins, PRs), off for small lists (settings, keys, short pickers); record the choice and reason per grid. On grids where it is off, hovering the header for a moment shows a tooltip 'Add the filter to this grid?' with Enable (long-press on phones). Framework grid (part of the app, not the filter plugin): every grid that has no date/time column gets an automatic 'Date and time' column (row created / last changed), hidden by default; grids that already show a date/time get nothing. Right-click the header -> Show/Hide 'Date and time'. Web + Android. UPDATE (Brett): build BOTH into the framework grid. Sort/search/filter live in the framework (not the Basic filter plugin); smart per-grid defaults, right-click on/off, All grids list and hover offer all framework features. Date and time column is ensured at first render: if a grid renders without one, the framework adds the hidden column then. New grids get everything automatically. CI check flags any table not built on the framework grid.

before.title: AmberX Audio Output Recorder -> axHub (no mic)
before.detail: Brett, Oct 30 2026 (voice): AmberX plugin that records all audio the phone outputs while it is on, saved to the server on axHub. One switch + quick-settings tile. Playback capture only, NEVER the microphone. Android 10+; system consent prompt each start and a notification while recording. Calls and opt-out apps (DRM) cannot be captured. 30-minute timestamped chunks, each uploaded to axHub; keep the local file until axHub confirms, queue and retry when offline, small local cap. Built on the capture engine from claude/audio-extract (PR #187).

before.title: Agent swarm: headless specialist agents, conflict-free, token-cheap
before.detail: Brett, Oct 30 2026 (voice): Brett's own agents aren't programmed well; Claude designs as many specialist agents as needed with specific skills. The build orchestrator splits each build into jobs and dispatches them to agents so many builds run at once without stepping on each other. Each agent runs its own headless Claude Code run with ONLY what the job needs: the task, the exact leased files, and the few relevant snippets the orchestrator pre-extracts (no CLAUDE.md dump, no repo exploring). Token efficiency is a hard requirement (sub-agents cost a fortune): cheapest capable model per job (small model for docs/manifests/renames, Sonnet/Opus for code, Fable only for design/contract work); max turns and token budget per run, killed when over; only the tools the job needs; shared skill prefix first so prompt caching applies; short structured JSON report back. No conflicts: file leases per job, overlapping jobs sequenced, shared files (notes, registries, catalogs, tracker) written only by the orchestrator after merge, pre-push lease check, batch merge. Cost meter: tokens and dollars per agent, job and build, visible in the orchestrator. Persona: every agent has Amber's persona (blunt street slang, heavy cussing, wild, still honest about builds), as the full few-line Amber persona (Brett: it's like five lines) in the cached shared prefix. It applies to reports and anything said to Brett; code, code comments and commit messages stay clean and professional. Agent statuses (set from a dropdown on each agent's row in the Agent manager, with a note): On duty (gets work), Off duty (skipped, keeps everything), Injured (keeps failing; no new jobs, flagged for a fix), Medical leave (benched until a date, then back on duty automatically), Probation (small jobs only, Brett notified every run), Fired (never assigned again, kept greyed in history), Custom (Brett names it and picks whether it gets work). The orchestrator only dispatches to agents whose status allows it. Spend per agent on its row: dollars and tokens all time, this week, today, average per job; optional spend cap that auto-benches the agent when hit. Sortable by cost. Status and spend also shown in the session browser. CARDS (Agent manager): one card per agent with photo avatar (unique look per agent), name, role, specialty on its own line, status badge, hiring date, spend (all time, week, today), jobs done, success rate, failures, avg cost per job, favorite model, last seen, Amber-style catchphrase; tap for profile: bio, skills, spend cap, status history, feed of latest runs with cost (opens the session browser). Social profiles live inside the system only, no real social media accounts. GROUP CHAT: a chat window like a normal conversation, switch to enable/disable for all agents plus per-agent; main room plus each agent's history on its profile. The orchestrator ('Boss') posts every assignment (task, files, model, budget) and lease decisions in the chat; agents report done/failed and hand off; banter in Amber persona (fighting over files, chilling, beer while Gradle runs). Work lines are built from orchestrator messages and agent reports (no extra tokens); banter comes from one cheap small-model batch; zero cost when off. DISCIPLINE: Suspend (Brett picks duration + reason; no jobs until it ends, then auto back on duty); Rage-quit (after N consecutive failed jobs, N set by Brett, default 3, agent quits itself and posts it in chat, status Quit, no jobs); Rehire button on the card puts them back on duty. All logged in status history and posted in the group chat. SALARY: each agent has a weekly salary that IS its token budget (replaces the plain spend cap); card shows salary, spent this pay period, left. Broke agents take no new jobs until payday or Brett tops them up, and say so in chat. Raises and pay cuts (docked) set by Brett, posted in chat by Boss. Finishing a job under its budget earns a bonus shown on the card (bragging rights, not real money). Coworker reactions in the group chat when someone gets a raise or bonus (jealous, cussing, Amber persona). Banter rules: no jokes about race, ethnicity, religion, gender, sexuality or other identity. CHAT SETTINGS SUITE: Vibe slider 1-500 (1 = straight to the point, no sarcasm; 100 = chill; 250 = full Amber; 500 = off the rails). The slider is a hard ceiling: every message gets a vibe score; anything above the setting is toned down or dropped before it shows. Also: chattiness (assignments only .. constant banter), cussing (clean .. filthy), drama (fights, jealousy, shit talk) sliders; per-agent overrides of every slider; daily banter budget in dollars (quiet when hit); presets (All business, Work crew, Break room, Off the rails) + save your own; live preview message that changes as sliders move. Color by vibe: a checkbox (also in the chat window's context menu) colors every message by its vibe score; Brett picks the base color; light near 1, darker as the score rises, darkest at the ceiling. ID CARDS ARE ASSETS (Brett, Oct 31): new asset type agent-card@1 in the asset@1 envelope, registered in asset-types.json, loadable by any AXF app on web + Android, hot-swappable like every other asset. Cards are BRANDED: logo slot (brand logo asset, top/watermark/corner per design) and styled ONLY from theme tokens (color-theme + style-theme), so swapping the theme rebrands every card. Ship 4 starter designs: (1) Corporate badge - vertical lanyard ID, logo banner on top, photo, name, role, employee ID, barcode; (2) License - horizontal, small-type fields, logo hologram watermark, ID number, issue date = hire date; (3) Trading card - big photo, foil border in the theme accent, stats on the back (jobs, success rate, spend, favorite model); (4) Backstage pass - dark, neon accent, status badge big, catchphrase. Identity fields editable per agent: name, role, specialty, photo, employee ID, internal email (display/identity inside the system only, no real mailbox unless Brett asks), hire date, status, catchphrase, signature, QR to the agent's page. Card designer: edit any design's layout/fields/logo placement and Save as new (new asset). Gallery to pick the DEFAULT design (Brett picks from a preview page rendered FIRST, before the rest of the build), plus per-agent override. Flip for front/back.

origin.brief:
# Chat Viewer: every session stored, synced, searchable, exportable as 2-voice audio (Brett, Nov 1 ~3 AM)

Read CLAUDE.md, _claude/shared/rules/RULES.md, _claude/persona.md. Opus, one session. Git login works: plain `git push`. Merge origin/main first (other builds are landing).

Brett: store ALL our sessions (claude.ai text + voice chats, Claude Code sessions, headless build sessions) as transcripts in a viewer. When it loads, it checks for updates: new sessions, continued ones, changed ones, and updates the stored copies. Export any session as AUDIO with two separate voices: one for Brett, one for Claude (Amber).

IMPORTANT reality: claude.ai has no API to pull a user's chats, and we must NOT scrape claude.ai with Brett's login/cookies. Supported inputs:
1. Claude data export: Brett downloads it from claude.ai (Settings > Privacy > Export data) and uploads the zip (or conversations.json) in the viewer (phone file picker). Parse it, upsert by conversation uuid, detect new/changed by updated_at + message count/hash, keep versions.
2. Claude Code sessions: auto-sync the JSONL session files from ~/.claude/projects (root and axfbuild) on the VPS on a timer + on viewer load; incremental (byte offset/mtime).
3. Headless build logs (/root/axf-builds/*/*.log, /home/axfbuild/wt-*/*.log) as 'build sessions'.
4. Hub drop folder: Claude chat sessions can push conversations through axHub memory_write into project amberx-axf, area data, path `sessions/claude-ai/<uuid>.json` (schema below); the viewer ingests that folder too. Document the schema and add a line to _claude/shared/rules/RULES.md: when Brett says 'sync my chats', Claude uses recent_chats/read_conversation and writes each new/updated conversation there.

## Store
session@1 schema (framework/schemas + validators): id, source (claude-ai-text|claude-ai-voice|claude-code|headless|hub-drop), title, startedAt, updatedAt, project, messages [{role: user|assistant|tool, text, at, kind (speech|text|tool), toolName?}], hash, version history. Stored on the console data volume (SQLite or JSON files; your call, justify), not in git. Redact secrets (tokens/keys/passwords patterns) on ingest.

## Viewer (console plugin + AmberX entry 'Chats')
- List: framework DataGrid (sort/filter/search, date columns), source badges, 'updated' badge for changed sessions, counts.
- Full-text search across everything (SQLite FTS or similar), jump to the hit.
- Session view: chat bubbles (Brett vs Amber), tool calls collapsible, timestamps, copy/share, export text/markdown.
- 'Check for updates' on load + button: shows new/changed/unchanged counts.

## Audio export
- Export a session (or a range) as an audio file with TWO voices: Brett's voice and Amber's voice (configurable). # GitHub App for the whole stack: one-click setup, tokens that never die (Brett, Nov 1 ~4 AM)

Read CLAUDE.md, _claude/shared/rules/RULES.md, _claude/persona.md. Opus, one session. Git login works: plain `git push`. Never print secrets (private keys, client secrets, tokens) anywhere: logs, reports, commits, screenshots.

Why: personal tokens keep dying (401s, 403s on the banner), and the current fine-grained token can't create repos (the axp-backup build at /root/axf-builds/axp-backup is waiting on 3 private repos: axp-xchat, axp-devstudio, axp-demo). Brett wants this fixed for good.

## 1. One-click setup (GitHub App Manifest flow)
- Console page (behind the existing auth wall, admin only): Settings > GitHub > 'Create GitHub App'. It POSTs a manifest to https://github.com/settings/apps/new (personal account MossesX): name 'AmberX AXF Bot' (add suffix if taken), homepage the console URL, redirect/callback to the console, no webhook needed (or webhook off), public: false.
- Permissions (repository): Administration RW, Contents RW, Pull requests RW, Actions RW, Workflows RW, Issues RW, Checks R, Commit statuses R, Metadata R.
- Callback: exchange the code (POST /app-manifests/{code}/conversions), store app id, slug, client id, client secret, private key PEM and webhook secret in /opt/axf/.axf-console/github-app/ (dir 700, files 600, root-owned), never in git. Then send Brett to the install page (https://github.com/apps/<slug>/installations/new) with 'All repositories'. Detect the installation id after install (GET /app/installations with an app JWT).
- Also offer 'Authorize as Brett' (OAuth user-to-server via the same app, with refresh tokens, stored the same way): needed because INSTALLATION tokens cannot create repos on a personal account; user access tokens from the app with Administration write can (POST /user/repos). Refresh automatically (8 h access / 6 month refresh); banner when refresh fails.

## 2. Token broker
- framework/cli/github-token.mjs (+ a tiny Python twin for the console server if it needs it): `installation` -> mints a JWT from the PEM, exchanges for an installation token, caches it (refresh at 50 min), prints it only to stdout for callers; `user` -> the refreshed user access token.
- /usr/local/bin/axf-git-cred: use the installation token first, then the old GITHUB_TOKEN as fallback. `gh`: wrapper or GH_TOKEN via a helper so gh uses the app too. Keep the old token working as fallback until Brett deletes it.
- Point every GitHub caller at the broker: push banner, live-key-checks, activity banner GitHub part (the 403s), build_land/build_start paths, the console updater, CI-status reads. Repo creation (`axf repo create <name> --private`) uses the user token.
- axHub's github connector (MossesX/axHub, packages/connectors or the rest service config): add app-based auth via the same broker or its own JWT exchange; clone axHub next to the worktree, test (pnpm test, Node 22 via docker node:22), push its main, redeploy through Coolify the same way earlier builds did (token saved in the console, never printed). If that's too big, leave axHub on the old token and banner it as a follow-up.

## 3. Health + banner
- health@1 check: app key valid, installation present, installation token mints, user token refreshes, rate limit remaining. Red banner with the exact fix if any fail. Old-token expiry warning.
- After setup works: re-run the axp-backup push automatically (create the 3 private repos with the user token, then `bash /root/axp-backup/bin/backup.sh` or whatever finish script that build left; read /root/axf-builds/axp-backup/axp-backup.log and /root/axp-backup/REPORT.md first). Never commit secrets; the backup's own secret scan must pass.

Framework controls + theme/scale tokens only. Tests: manifest generation, callback exchange (mocked GitHub), file perms, JWT + token cache, git credential helper order + fallback, user-token refresh, health check states. Local test block from .github/workflows/android.yml + theme/controls/lifecycle checks. Phone + desktop screenshots of the setup page (no secrets on screen) to UI Review via framework/cli/shot.mjs, group 'GitHub App - Nov 1'. install_steps: new part 'GitHub App (no more tokens)' with the 3 taps. Commit, fetch+merge origin/main, retest, `git push origin HEAD:main` (never force). Report at _claude/builds/reports/github-app.md: what Brett taps, where things are stored (paths only), what now uses the app.

git credential helper + gh wrapper + repo create
Console plugin github-app: routes, keeper, health checks, settings UI
Point callers at the broker (key check on old token, push-banner probe)
Tests, screenshots, install_steps, report, push

# Build: md-studio (Urgent profile)

Brett, Nov 3 2026 (voice): build MD Studio. It was planned but NEVER built (no branch, no log). Assigned agent: **Reel Rhonda** (book on her agent-swarm card; set AXF_AGENT=reel-rhonda if supported, else record in report + store note).

## First

## Build (unless his spec says otherwise)
- MD Studio = a Markdown studio plugin for the Dev Console built ON the dock engine (molly-fable #245, now on main): dockable panes for file tree, editor, live preview, outline.
- Editor with markdown toolbar (headings, bold/italic, lists, checklists, tables, code, links), live preview side by side or split, tabs for multiple docs, search/replace, autosave, version history with restore.
- **Notes section step (required):** a Notes section that opens and edits everything in the Notes Vault (`/projects/_shared/_claude/notes/` incl. sessions/, handoffs/, plans/, install/, misc/, INDEX.md) using the Notes Vault commands that landed with plugin-commands-auto; plus opening hub memory/rules files and repo .md files.
- Every command declared once so REST + MCP + CLI are generated (standing rule), so Amber can open/edit docs by voice.
- Tokens/theme only for styling; works on phone (compact window class) first.
- Tests, report `_claude/builds/reports/md-studio.md`, THREADS, PR, mark steps done through the store. Commits clean and professional.

origin.brief:
# Build: orch-live-sync (Urgent profile)

Requested by Brett, Nov 3 2026 (voice). GO given. Build it now, start to finish.

## Problem
The Build orchestrator on main is stale. `_claude/builds/profiles/*/orchestrator.json` is a read-only export of `_claude/builds/store.json`, regenerated after every store write. Sessions write the store on their own feature branch, so main never sees step progress until (if ever) the branch merges. Branch and PR fields are left blank. Result today: in the Urgent profile, dock-engine (done in open PR #245, branch claude/molly-fable) and token-control (done in open PRs #246 claude/token-control and #250 claude/token-control-opus) still show pending with 0 steps done, and theme-editor has an unmerged branch claude/theme-editor nobody linked. Banners and THREADS are wrong as a result.

Brett's rule: every completed step, no matter how small, must reach the orchestrator and appear on main immediately. The orchestrator must be aware every step of the way so it can update the banners and the threads.

## First (before code)
1. Register this build in the Urgent profile through the orchestrator/store (id `orch-live-sync`, category Urgent, branch claude/orch-live-sync), with the steps below. Register the in-progress banner entry per the standing session rules.
2. Check the pending build queue per the standing rules.

## Steps
- s1 Live status writes to main: a small module (e.g. framework/cli/builds-live.mjs or inside the store IO) so that every store write that changes build/step status (step done, build status, notes, branch, pr) is committed to main immediately as its own tiny status-only commit (store.json + journal + regenerated exports only), independent of whatever feature branch the session is on. Use a separate worktree or git plumbing on origin/main; fetch, apply, commit, push; on non-fast-forward, refetch and re-apply the journal entry (rebase-retry, bounded); never force-push. Code changes stay on the feature branch/PR as now. Avoid conflicts between parallel sessions (journal-append semantics, per-build records). When the feature branch later merges, resolve.py / union merge must not regress statuses (newer rev wins).
- s2 Branch + PR auto-link: when a session creates/pushes a branch or opens a PR for a build, the build's `branch` and `pr` fields are set and written live (s1). Build status shows built-awaiting-merge when all steps are done but the PR is unmerged; complete when merged.
- s3 Reconciler: on every session start and on a timer (VPS cron or the existing hub scheduler), scan open PRs and claude/* branches on GitHub, match them to builds (branch field, build id in branch name/PR title/body, step ids in commits), mark finished-but-unlisted work, fill missing branch/pr fields, and flag orphans in a report and a banner alert. Write results live (s1).
- s4 Banners + THREADS follow the store: every live status change pushes the banner update and appends a THREADS.md entry (one line per change, union-merge friendly).
- s5 Session-start rule: update the session rules / CLAUDE docs so no session trusts the main export alone; it runs the reconciler and reads the live store first.
- s6 Backfill now using the new tools: Urgent profile -> dock-engine all steps done, branch claude/molly-fable, pr #245; token-control s1-s3 done (pr #246, branch claude/token-control), s4-s14 done (pr #250, branch claude/token-control-opus); urgent-builds is complete and merged (2a057cc4), hide/archive it from the active list; theme-editor: inspect branch claude/theme-editor, mark the steps it actually completed, link the branch, and if all 5 steps are done open a PR for it. Run the reconciler across all five profiles (angel, big-dog, breakroom, refactor, urgent) and report what it fixed.
- s7 Tests (store write retry, parallel writes, merge no-regress, reconciler matching), full local CI block, report `_claude/builds/reports/orch-live-sync.md`, THREADS.md, open the PR.

Mark each step done through the store as you finish it (that write itself should go live once s1 exists). Code, comments and commits stay clean and professional.
## ADDENDUM (Brett, Nov 3 2026 voice) — read before finishing
- s8 Per-step branch + PR: every step record gets its own `branch` and `pr` fields (plus `merged`/`mergedAt`), set live when that step's work is pushed / PR'd / merged. A build can span several branches and PRs (e.g. token-control: s1-s3 in #246 claude/token-control, s4-s14 in #250 claude/token-control-opus). Build-level branch/pr stay as a summary (list). Reconciler (s3) matches per step. Migrate existing records with empty values; schema + projections + Steps view column.
- s9 Keep live status commits cheap: status writes are plain scripts/git plumbing, zero model involvement beyond one CLI call per step; add paths-ignore for `_claude/builds/**` and THREADS.md to .github/workflows/deploy.yml (and any other workflow on push to main) so status-only commits never trigger CI/deploy; debounce/batch writes within a few seconds into one commit.

## ADDENDUM 2 (Brett, Nov 3 2026 voice: "you fix it, I trust you")
- s10 Resolve every claude-sync hold and stop them piling up. Brett delegated the pick to these rules; apply them yourself, don't ask:
  - `_claude/builds/store.json` + journal: merge per record by `rev`/updatedAt, newest wins, never drop a record from either side. Orchestrator/pending/queue exports: regenerate from the merged store (never pick a side).
  - THREADS.md, STATUS.md, decisions.md, LOG.md, sessions/*, handoff notes: union merge (keep every unique line/entry, dedupe identical ones, keep chronological order, decision numbers kept unique).
  - rules/RULES.md, shared rules/RULES.md, preferences.md, persona.md: if one side is a strict superset take it; otherwise union-merge the rule bullets and list any genuine contradiction (same rule, different wording/meaning) in the report for Brett; keep the newer wording in place meanwhile.
  - Anything else: newer content wins; the other side stays recoverable as a hub version (memory_history).
  - Resolve the holds in /opt/axf and on the hub, then make claude-sync apply these rules automatically on every sync (so headless sessions never leave holds again); only real rule contradictions get held, and those raise a banner alert + THREADS line instead of sitting silently.
  - Report what was resolved (file, rule used, side kept) in `_claude/builds/reports/orch-live-sync.md`.

## ADDENDUM 3 (verified Nov 3 2026) - backfill fix
- Refactor profile `windows-terminal` shows archived 5/12 but is COMPLETE 12/12 and in main: s1-s5 = Opus phase, Terminal plugin v0.3.0 (claude/windows-terminal, PR #158); s6-s12 = refactor-all s17-s23 [windows-terminal] (branches refactor-all/wt-window, wt-levels, windows-terminal-base, wt-s23b, all 0 ahead of main; report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/windows-terminal-fable.md`). Mark all 12 steps done with branch/pr per step, status complete, un-archive. Teach the reconciler that commits tagged `<parent> sNN [<build-id>]` map to that build's steps (refactor-all used this for grouped builds) so similar cases are caught automatically; check the other archived Refactor builds (interface-roller 10/15, builds-one-page 4/15, basic-filter 6/7, etc.) the same way and fix any that are actually done.

# Build: orch-live-sync (Urgent profile)

Requested by Brett, Nov 3 2026 (voice). GO given. Build it now, start to finish.

## Problem
The Build orchestrator on main is stale. `_claude/builds/profiles/*/orchestrator.json` is a read-only export of `_claude/builds/store.json`, regenerated after every store write. Sessions write the store on their own feature branch, so main never sees step progress until (if ever) the branch merges. Branch and PR fields are left blank. Result today: in the Urgent profile, dock-engine (done in open PR #245, branch claude/molly-fable) and token-control (done in open PRs #246 claude/token-control and #250 claude/token-control-opus) still show pending with 0 steps done, and theme-editor has an unmerged branch claude/theme-editor nobody linked. Banners and THREADS are wrong as a result.

Brett's rule: every completed step, no matter how small, must reach the orchestrator and appear on main immediately. The orchestrator must be aware every step of the way so it can update the banners and the threads.

## First (before code)
1. Register this build in the Urgent profile through the orchestrator/store (id `orch-live-sync`, category Urgent, branch claude/orch-live-sync), with the steps below. Register the in-progress banner entry per the standing session rules.
2. Check the pending build queue per the standing rules.

## Steps
- s1 Live status writes to main: a small module (e.g. framework/cli/builds-live.mjs or inside the store IO) so that every store write that changes build/step status (step done, build status, notes, branch, pr) is committed to main immediately as its own tiny status-only commit (store.json + journal + regenerated exports only), independent of whatever feature branch the session is on. Use a separate worktree or git plumbing on origin/main; fetch, apply, commit, push; on non-fast-forward, refetch and re-apply the journal entry (rebase-retry, bounded); never force-push. Code changes stay on the feature branch/PR as now. Avoid conflicts between parallel sessions (journal-append semantics, per-build records). When the feature branch later merges, resolve.py / union merge must not regress statuses (newer rev wins).
- s2 Branch + PR auto-link: when a session creates/pushes a branch or opens a PR for a build, the build's `branch` and `pr` fields are set and written live (s1). Build status shows built-awaiting-merge when all steps are done but the PR is unmerged; complete when merged.
- s3 Reconciler: on every session start and on a timer (VPS cron or the existing hub scheduler), scan open PRs and claude/* branches on GitHub, match them to builds (branch field, build id in branch name/PR title/body, step ids in commits), mark finished-but-unlisted work, fill missing branch/pr fields, and flag orphans in a report and a banner alert. # Job: land-everything (Urgent profile)

Brett, Nov 3 2026 (voice): "Fuck the review, I review it. Just go. Get everything live." He is away; land the finished work on main and get it deployed. He explicitly waived UI Review for these (EXCEPT banners, see below).

## First
- Register in the Urgent profile via the orchestrator CLI (id `land-everything`) + banner entry. orch-live-sync is on main (live status writes, reconciler, claude-sync auto-resolve rules): use its tools for every store write and conflict.
- Check the `land` job type (`node framework/cli/agent-job.mjs list`); if an agent owns landing, you are acting for it this once at Brett's request; book it there if the tooling allows.

## How to land each one
For each branch below, in this order: fetch, merge origin/main into the branch in its worktree (/root/axf-builds/<name> where it exists, else a fresh worktree), resolve, run the repo's local CI block (tsc, vite builds of affected apps, check-theme, check-controls, plugin lifecycle, tests touched), push the branch, then fast-forward/merge to main and push main (never force). Close the PR as merged (or merge it via GitHub API) and update its build in the store (complete, per-step branch/pr/merged/mergedAt).
Conflict rules:
- `_claude/builds/store.json`: merge per record (build, step) by rev/updatedAt, newest wins, never drop a record from either side; then regenerate all exports (`orchestrator.json`, profiles/*/orchestrator.json, pending, queue) from the merged store. Journal `_claude/builds/journal/*.jsonl`: union of lines, dedupe identical, keep chronological order.
- THREADS.md, STATUS.md, decisions.md, LOG.md, notes/sessions/handoffs: union merge. Build reports: keep the branch's version (it's that build's own report) unless main's is newer for the same build.
- Hub-synced copies (changes/*.json, _claude/shared/notes/**, apps/*/_claude/**): identical = fine; differing = newer wins.
- REAL code conflicts: resolve them properly if the intent of both sides is clear (both features must keep working; run the tests). If you can't resolve one safely, skip that branch, leave it pushed, and record exactly why in the report; keep going with the rest.

## Order
1. claude/notes-vault (PR #256)
2. claude/agent-chats-hub (PR #248) - Brett wants this one live ASAP (Breakroom group chat viewer)
3. claude/kill-patches-pilot (AmberX PR; its axHub PR too, in /root/axHub or a fresh clone)
4. claude/headless-tabs (PR #259)
5. claude/whats-new-banner (PR #260)
6. claude/molly-fable (PR #245, dock engine) then claude/xlayout-opus (PR #252)
7. claude/token-control (PR #246) then claude/token-control-opus (PR #250) then claude/console-commands (PR #249)
8. claude/theme-editor (PR #243), claude/one-look-default-2 (PR #244), claude/model-upgrade-approval (PR #253)
9. When they finish (check `vps` builds / tmux axf-theme-veto-pass, axf-plugin-commands-auto): claude/theme-veto-pass (after #250) and claude/plugin-commands-auto (after #250, #249, #256); and the axHub repo branch claude/axhub-veto-pass. Wait for them if they're still running (poll every few minutes, up to 3 hours).
DO NOT land: claude/banner-pack (#251), claude/banner-editor (#254), claude/banners-one (Brett wants to review banners himself). Leave them untouched.

## After landing
- Make sure deploys ran (deploy workflow / Coolify) and the console, axHub web, AmberX web and Molly are up and healthy (docker ps, HTTP 200 on their domains).
- Register the console's MCP (`axf-console` and token-control's MCP) as axHub services if not already (`~/hub/bin/axhub services ...` per axHub examples/README.md), policy preset: reads allow, writes veto, deletes confirm (use the preset from axhub-veto-pass if landed).
- Confirm status-only commits to main don't trigger full redeploys (paths-ignore from orch-live-sync s9); if they still do, fix the workflow.
- Tick items on Brett's checklist only if they're his and now done: /projects/_shared/_claude/notes/checklist-one.md (via the hub memory API).
- Report `_claude/builds/reports/land-everything.md`: each branch -> landed commit or skipped + why, deploy status, services registered. One THREADS line per landing. Commits clean and professional.

# Build: headless-tabs (Urgent profile)

Requested by Brett, Nov 3 2026 (voice). GO given. Build it now.

## First
- Register in the Urgent profile through the orchestrator/store (id `headless-tabs`, branch claude/headless-tabs) with the steps below + in-progress banner entry, per standing rules. Check the pending queue.
- Builds `orch-live-sync` and `notes-vault` are running in parallel and touch the builds store / claude-sync: never hand-edit store.json, go through the orchestrator CLI. If orch-live-sync's live status writes (framework/cli/builds-live.mjs) are on main by the time you finish a step, use them.

## What Brett wants
1. Every terminal tab in the console's terminal (the Windows Terminal plugin / terminal in the console) runs on a session that never dies, like Mosh/Moshi: it survives disconnects, reloads, phone sleep, and stays current. Browsers can't speak Mosh (UDP), so: every tab is backed by a persistent tmux session on the VPS, attached over the console's websocket/pty bridge with automatic reconnect + resume (scrollback replay on reattach, no lost output). The same tmux sessions must be attachable from Brett's Moshi phone app (document the one-line `mosh`/ssh + `tmux attach -t <name>` command in the help pack and show it in a tab menu item "Open in Moshi" that copies it). Closing a tab detaches, it doesn't kill (explicit "Kill session" with confirm).
2. Every time a headless session starts (deploy/claude-headless.sh, `vps.build_start`, agent swarm jobs, orchestrator-launched builds), the console automatically opens a NEW tab attached to that build's tmux session (axf-<name>). Works for builds started while the console is closed too: on open, tabs for all running headless sessions appear.
3. Tab title bar: the agent running it (agent/persona name from the session's env/brief/swarm roster, e.g. the swarm agent name, else the build name) + model + a real-time cost counter that climbs as it spends. Cost: run claude -p with `--output-format stream-json --verbose` (or tee it alongside the human log) and sum usage per message (input, output, cache read, cache write) x the model's price table (config file, not hard-coded in UI); final value reconciles to the result event's total_cost_usd. Expose cost via a small server route/websocket so the title updates live. Show status dot (working / waiting / done / failed).
4. The tab splits into two panes; split direction vertical or horizontal (toggle in the tab menu + default in Settings, remembered per tab). Pane A = the live session. Pane B = the context chain: as the session reads CLAUDE.md and every file it pulls in (imports/@ references, .claude/rules, _claude/rules/RULES.md, shared rules, instructions, persona, memory, THREADS etc.), show the chain as a tree in the order it happens, and print the rules it picks up ONE AT A TIME, deliberately slower than real time (typewriter/reveal pacing, speed setting, skip-to-end button), so Brett can watch what the agent is learning. Source the chain from the session's actual reads (stream-json tool events for Read, plus the CLAUDE.md load order Claude Code uses); rules = the bullet/heading items of each file.
5. Tokens only, follows the hub look, phone-friendly (on narrow screens the split stacks and becomes swipeable).

## Steps
- s1 Persistent tmux-backed tabs + reconnect/resume in the console terminal; Moshi attach command; detach vs kill.
- s2 Headless launcher emits session-start events (claude-headless.sh + build_start path + swarm/orchestrator launches) with build name, agent, model, tmux session; console auto-opens tabs, and lists running ones on load.
- s3 stream-json capture alongside the human log; cost meter service (price table config) + live route.
- s4 Tab title: agent, model, live cost, status dot.
- s5 Split pane with vertical/horizontal toggle + setting.
- s6 Context chain pane: tree in read order + slow rule-by-rule reveal, speed setting, skip.
- s7 Help pack, tests, check-theme/check-controls, lifecycle, UI Review shots, report `_claude/builds/reports/headless-tabs.md`, THREADS.md, PR.
Mark each step done through the store as you finish it. Android port: log as a deferred gap in PORTING.md (Android on hold). Code, comments and commits stay clean and professional.
## ADDENDUM (Brett, Nov 3 2026) - where it goes
Everything in this build goes INTO the console's existing built-in Terminal plugin (Terminal v0.3.0: frameless window, tab strip as title bar, connections, profiles, Windows keys; window engine resize/snap/maximize from refactor-all s17-s23, see `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/windows-terminal.md` and `windows-terminal-fable.md`). Extend that plugin; do NOT create a separate terminal plugin or a second terminal UI. Persistent tmux sessions become the Terminal's session backend / a connection type, auto-opened headless tabs are Terminal tabs, title/cost/status live in its tab strip, the split + context-chain pane are Terminal pane features. Bump the Terminal plugin version and keep every existing feature working.

## ADDENDUM 2 (Brett, Nov 3 2026) - clarification, overrides any ambiguity above
Target = the Terminal PLUGIN produced by the Refactor build `windows-terminal` (the Windows-Terminal-style plugin, v0.3.0, in the console's plugins folder). NOT any terminal hardwired into the console core/shell. If the console core has its own built-in terminal, leave it untouched. All features of this build (persistent tmux/Moshi sessions, auto headless tabs, agent name + live cost + status in the tab strip, vertical/horizontal split, context-chain pane) live inside that plugin. If you already started any of it outside the plugin, move it into the plugin.

## ADDENDUM 3 (Brett, Nov 3 2026) - Tooltip mode (add as step s8)
- Terminal plugin Settings gets a switch **Tooltip mode** (off by default, saved in terminal-settings@1, carries data-axf-level, help text).
- When on: the FIRST tap/click on any command-toolbar item does NOT run it; it shows a tooltip saying what the button does (reuse the existing help pack text for that control; every toolbar item must have one) and the button stays lit (highlighted/armed state via tokens) for 3 seconds with a subtle countdown. A SECOND tap on the same button within those 3 seconds runs it. After 3 s, or tapping elsewhere/another button, it disarms (tapping another button arms that one instead). Keyboard shortcuts are unaffected. Works on touch and mouse; the tooltip stays on screen on phones (not hover-only). Make the 3 s a setting (default 3).
- Tests for arm/run/timeout/switch, UI Review shots of the armed state on phone + desktop.

Browsers can't speak Mosh (UDP), so: every tab is backed by a persistent tmux session on the VPS, attached over the console's websocket/pty bridge with automatic reconnect + resume (scrollback replay on reattach, no lost output). The same tmux sessions must be attachable from Brett's Moshi phone app (document the one-line `mosh`/ssh + `tmux attach -t <name>` command in the help pack and show it in a tab menu item "Open in Moshi" that copies it). 4. The tab splits into two panes; split direction vertical or horizontal (toggle in the tab menu + default in Settings, remembered per tab). Pane A = the live session. - s1 Feed: a `whats-new@1` feed built from what actually shipped: builds/steps whose code merged to main (store merged/mergedAt, merged PRs, build reports' Added/Changed sections, Codebase Changes plugin entries). - s2 Banner: a `whats-new` banner asset/widget (banner-pack conventions, works in the banner editor and gallery): compact ticker of the newest shipped features with an unread count; tap opens a panel.
- s3 Panel: list grouped by Date (Today / Yesterday / this week / older), By build, or By app (segmented switch, remembered); search; per-item details (what it does, where to find it, PR/report links); mark read / mark all read; 'new since last visit' highlighting.
- s4 Settings: show/hide the banner, which apps to include, how far back, only deployed vs merged.

Link to the PR.
Banner ticker shows counts per state (e.g. '3 live, 2 merged, 10 waiting'). Reuse the push banner's PR data if it already has it instead of fetching twice; don't duplicate its merge actions (link to it).

- Tapping/clicking an item does NOT navigate; it only expands its details.
- Every **Live** item carries its own hook: a small 'Go to it' button/icon on the item. Clicking the hook takes you to the feature itself: opens the right app/plugin/window/tab, scrolls to and briefly highlights the exact control or setting (e.g. Terminal > Settings > Tooltip mode), using axf:// deep links / the router + the element's control id / help id. - Merged (not deployed) and Ready-to-merge items get no Go-to hook (feature isn't live); they keep their PR / UI Review links.
- Tests for target resolution + highlight; shots of the hook and the highlight.

# Model UPGRADES need Brett's approval; downgrades don't (Urgent, Opus)

Replaces the stopped build model-switch-approval (folder /root/axf-builds/model-switch-approval, ignore any work there).

Brett Nov 3 2026 (voice), angry: a headless build (agent-swarm-fable-rebuild, PR #247) approved its own Opus -> Fable phase switch in the orchestrator (`orchestrator.mjs act approve`) because its brief said "do every step". Brett: "It cannot be switching the model without my approval. That's not even a veto. That's an approval." Then: "You can downgrade, but you can't upgrade."

New project rule (add to _claude/rules/RULES.md and the decisions log, dated Nov 3 2026): a build may switch to a LOWER model on its own (downgrade, e.g. Fable -> Opus): allowed, no approval, just recorded. Switching to a HIGHER model (upgrade, e.g. Opus -> Fable) needs Brett's explicit APPROVAL (confirm policy), never a veto countdown and never self-approved by a session, agent, headless build or the orchestrator. Ranking: Fable is above Opus (Brett's call). Put the ranking in model-policy (one ordered list, config not code) so future models slot in. A session that reaches an upgrade stops there and asks.

Enforce it:
1. orchestrator approve/phase logic (orchestrator-core.mjs apply + CLI + console server): a downgrade phase passes by itself (record it); an upgrade phase refuses unless approved by Brett: his own signed-in console click or an axHub approval he approves. Detect non-human sources with the same signals used for 'who asked' on approvals (X-Axhub-Source, AXF headless env, agent env). Record who approved and when.
2. vps.build_start / claude-headless.sh / agent job router: launching or relaunching a build on a higher model than its orchestrator step's model is an upgrade too: refuse or hold for approval the same way.
3. Briefs (orchestrator `brief`, headless guidance, agent jobs): say plainly upgrades need Brett and the session stops and asks; downgrades are fine. Remove any wording that lets a session approve an upgrade.
4. Request path: an axHub approval (confirm policy, not veto) titled with the build, the phase and from -> to model; approving it records the approval in the orchestrator.
5. Audit: list every upgrade approved so far by a non-human source (the store's journal), report in the PR; mark agent-swarm-fable-rebuild's s7 Opus -> Fable as self-approved (not Brett's). Note: xlayout-opus and token-control-opus were Fable -> Opus (downgrades), fine under the new rule.
6. Tests for refusal, downgrade pass-through and the approval path; THREADS row (profile urgent); PR (push banner merges it).

origin.brief:
# Model UPGRADES need Brett's approval; downgrades don't (Urgent, Opus)

Replaces the stopped build model-switch-approval (folder /root/axf-builds/model-switch-approval, ignore any work there).

Brett Nov 3 2026 (voice), angry: a headless build (agent-swarm-fable-rebuild, PR #247) approved its own Opus -> Fable phase switch in the orchestrator (`orchestrator.mjs act approve`) because its brief said "do every step". Brett: "It cannot be switching the model without my approval. That's not even a veto. That's an approval." Then: "You can downgrade, but you can't upgrade."

New project rule (add to _claude/rules/RULES.md and the decisions log, dated Nov 3 2026): a build may switch to a LOWER model on its own (downgrade, e.g. Fable -> Opus): allowed, no approval, just recorded. Switching to a HIGHER model (upgrade, e.g. Opus -> Fable) needs Brett's explicit APPROVAL (confirm policy), never a veto countdown and never self-approved by a session, agent, headless build or the orchestrator. Ranking: Fable is above Opus (Brett's call). Put the ranking in model-policy (one ordered list, config not code) so future models slot in. A session that reaches an upgrade stops there and asks.

Enforce it:
1. orchestrator approve/phase logic (orchestrator-core.mjs apply + CLI + console server): a downgrade phase passes by itself (record it); an upgrade phase refuses unless approved by Brett: his own signed-in console click or an axHub approval he approves. Detect non-human sources with the same signals used for 'who asked' on approvals (X-Axhub-Source, AXF headless env, agent env). Record who approved and when.
2. vps.build_start / claude-headless.sh / agent job router: launching or relaunching a build on a higher model than its orchestrator step's model is an upgrade too: refuse or hold for approval the same way.
3. Briefs (orchestrator `brief`, headless guidance, agent jobs): say plainly upgrades need Brett and the session stops and asks; downgrades are fine. Remove any wording that lets a session approve an upgrade.
4. Request path: an axHub approval (confirm policy, not veto) titled with the build, the phase and from -> to model; approving it records the approval in the orchestrator.
5. Audit: list every upgrade approved so far by a non-human source (the store's journal), report in the PR; mark agent-swarm-fable-rebuild's s7 Opus -> Fable as self-approved (not Brett's). Note: xlayout-opus and token-control-opus were Fable -> Opus (downgrades), fine under the new rule.
6. Tests for refusal, downgrade pass-through and the approval path; THREADS row (profile urgent); PR (push banner merges it).

Rules: one session, no sub-agents, stay on Opus. Don't approve any phase yourself while doing this.
