steps.text: Design the shared screenshot registry: record schema (id, screen id, element selector, app, captured_at, file path, links[] of {kind: build|feature|plan|error, ref}), storage layout, and a migration that imports existing UI Review screenshots into it without losing their current links.
steps.why: Schema and migration design for a store shared across apps

steps.text: Define the screenshot hook contract (screenshots.attach / screenshots.forRef / screenshots.onCapture) that any plugin calls to link or list screenshots by ref, with a typed event payload. UI Review becomes one caller of the hook, not its owner.
steps.why: Cross-port contract every app and plugin builds against

steps.text: Design the screen skin asset type: schema (target screen id, colour tokens, style overrides, layout params, behavior flags, icon theme), versioning, and the migration that registers it beside the existing asset types.
steps.why: New asset schema and migration in the shared asset store

steps.text: Theming engine: resolve the token stack as global theme → app theme → screen skin for the active screen id only, plus a hot-apply path that pushes a draft skin into a render without saving it.
steps.why: Engine internals that change how GUIs are themed across apps

steps.text: Implement the screenshot registry store and REST routes (list, get, by ref, attach, detach, delete), using the step 1 schema, and run the UI Review migration.
Hook callers: Shipped Features entries, Plan Studio plans, orchestrator builds, and the errors log call screenshots.attach and forRef. Remove any Build Manager-only paths.
Mention linker: anywhere a build, feature or error id is rendered (shared ref chip component), show a screenshot count and thumbnail strip from the registry.

Registry API parity: console_show/console_open target 'screenshots' and 'screenshot/<id>' deep links, state read, MCP tools (screenshots_list/get/attach/detach), CLI 'axf screenshots …', and AmberX voice intents.
Screen skin asset store and REST routes (create, get, list by screen, update, delete, apply, unapply) on top of the step 3 schema.

Screenshot viewer side pane: when you open a screenshot of an element, list every token, style and parameter for that screen, grouped as colour, style, layout, behavior and icons, with editable fields.
Live preview: render the same screen in an iframe or sandbox, hot-apply pane edits through theme hot-apply, then Save to create or update the screen skin asset, with Revert and Discard.

Skin editor and screen skin API parity: deep links (console_open 'screenshot/<id>/edit', 'asset/screen-skin/<id>'), state read of the draft and saved skin, actions and settings (set token, preview, save, revert, apply, unapply) via REST, MCP console actions and plugin commands, CLI 'axf skins …', and voice.
Docs: registry hook usage for plugin authors, screen skin asset type, and the API reach table (deep link, state, actions, settings across REST, MCP, CLI and voice).

Tests (registry store, migration, hook callers, skin resolve order, hot-apply, REST/MCP/CLI parity), report at _claude/builds/reports/shared-screenshot-registry-hooked-everywhere-liv.md, THREADS row, and PR stating how each UI is reached through deep link, REST, MCP, CLI and voice.

before.title: Shipped Features: show each landed build's screenshots on its entry
before.detail: Each Shipped Features entry shows the screenshots and before/after shots of what that build did (pulled from the shared screenshot registry / UI Review screenshots grouped by build name), inline with a gallery view. Goes with the shared screenshot registry build.

Split by Claude into 7 steps (1 Fable).

origin.said: Screenshots and everything of what it did? Yep.

steps.text: Define the contract between Shipped Features entries and the shared screenshot registry: how a build id/name maps to its screenshots, how before/after pairs are marked (role: before|after|shot, pair key, caption, captured_at, source = registry|ui-review), and the fallback lookup through UI Review screenshots grouped by build name. Write it as a schema doc and a JSON schema both sides read; if the shared screenshot registry build has not landed, define the read interface it must satisfy.
steps.why: Cross-port contract between the screenshot registry, UI Review and Shipped Features

steps.text: Server side: add a resolver that, for a shipped build, collects its screenshots from the shared screenshot registry (and UI Review screenshots grouped by build name as fallback), pairs before/after shots, dedupes, and returns them sorted and capped per the contract. Cache per build id.

REST API: GET /api/shipped/:id/screenshots (list, pairs, counts) and GET /api/shipped/:id/screenshots/:shot (one shot with metadata and image URL); include screenshot count and cover thumbnail on the existing shipped list/entry responses. Settings for the gallery (default view grid|before-after, thumbnail size, show on list on/off) readable and writable at GET/PUT /api/shipped/settings/gallery.

UI: on each Shipped Features entry show an inline screenshot strip (cover + count) and a gallery view: grid of shots, before/after side-by-side or slider for pairs, lightbox with prev/next and captions, empty state when the build has none. Built on the console plugin framework components.

API parity for the gallery UI: deep links console_show/console_open targets shipped-features/<build id>/screenshots and shipped-features/<build id>/screenshots/<shot> (opens gallery or lightbox at that shot, before/after mode); gallery state readable (open build, current shot, view mode); actions open_gallery, show_shot, next/prev, set_view, and gallery settings registered as console actions for MCP.

CLI and voice: add 'shipped screenshots <build> [--shot n] [--before-after] [--open]' and 'shipped gallery settings get|set' plugin commands calling the same REST/actions; add AmberX voice intents ('show me the screenshots for <build>', 'next shot', 'before and after') mapped to the same actions.

Tests: resolver (registry hit, UI Review fallback, before/after pairing, no screenshots), REST endpoints and settings, deep link parsing, action/MCP/CLI/voice parity (same results through all four), and a UI test that the gallery renders and the lightbox navigates. Then write the report _claude/builds/reports/shipped-features-show-each-landed-build-s-screen.md (what changed, screenshots of the gallery, how each UI part is reached via deep link, REST, MCP, CLI and voice), add the THREADS row, and open the PR stating the API reach for every UI piece and the dependency on the shared screenshot registry build.

before.title: Skin rule: overrides are local only; global changes only by applying a whole skin
before.detail: Amends the skins naming-contract build. Precedence: axHub base < skin (by canonical role) < per-screen skin < per-element override. An override changes only that element. Enforce in the inline editor (no 'apply everywhere' outside the skin editor) and document in CLAUDE.md rules.

before.title: Dispatcher: a worktree store write can erase a fresh launch record (double launch, then a stuck build)
before.detail: Seen on pass-approval-hook-deep-link-amberx-notification, Nov 10 2026 (journal _claude/builds/journal/2026-11-p4.jsonl): 18:11:16 pipeline:launch wrote status running + pipeline.session earl; 18:11:19 the worktree's orchestrator:note ('Claude account: ...', written by claude-headless.sh at start from a store copy taken before the launch) landed with status queued and no pipeline record, and the per-build newer-wins merge kept it; 18:12:11 the next tick launched the same build again (gina), both runs numbered 1. Earl's 's1 done' tick at 18:24:48 erased the second record the same way, so the live build sat in 'running' with no session: checkEnds and reapBuilds both skip a build without pipeline.session / pipeline.account, so the phase end was never handled (set to queued by hand). Fix, in this order: (1) builds-merge-core: merge the pipeline record per field, never let an incoming copy with no pipeline record replace a newer launch record on main (or have orchestrator.mjs act pull main's record before a note/tick write); (2) pipeline-core plan(): never launch a build whose status is running/waiting or that has a running or queued agent slot for its id (agent-slots status lists build per slot); (3) checkEnds/reapBuilds: a build 'running' with no pipeline record and no live slot for it ends by the phase rule (exit 0 + model switch -> queued) instead of being skipped forever; (4) claude-headless.sh: write the 'Claude account' note only after the launch record is published, or through the per-field merge. Add a check in framework/spec/check-builds-live.mjs that replays this journal sequence.

origin.brief:
# Build: orchestrator-checks-each-build-against-main-righ

## Brett said (verbatim)
At: 2026-11-10T18:57:34.689Z
> Instead of checking all the pending against main, just have the orchestrator check each one at a time before it puts it in the queue.

## What to build
Continue build "Orchestrator checks each build against main right before queuing it (done = close, partly done = queue only what's left)" (orchestrator-checks-each-build-against-main-righ) — Phase 1, model Opus.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said (2026-11-10 18:57):
"Instead of checking all the pending against main, just have the orchestrator check each one at a time before it puts it in the queue."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 30 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. "I need a switch in the orchestrator to set the number of mergers and the number of builders. It needs to assign merges to an employee just like builds. Put all my processing power towards merging."

Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.

before.title: Molly gap: the console frame hands Molly its token once (embed@1 credentials) and the console API allows Molly's origin
before.detail: Found by molly-sign-in-once s1. Two halves. (1) The console API refuses cross-origin calls from Molly: OPTIONS https://console.amberxai.com/api/me with Origin https://molly.amberxai.com answers 401 with no CORS headers (the token check runs before FastAPI's CORSMiddleware, and allow_origins * cannot be used by the wall). Let preflights through and answer an allow-list of amberxai.com app origins with Access-Control-Allow-Headers authorization, content-type, accept. (2) The console token lives only in the console origin's storage (axf-console:token); Molly keeps its own copy (molly:console-token) that today a person must paste. Add an embed@1 message (guest to host, e.g. credentials with {app, scheme, token}) the console frame sends once to a host it recognises (frame-ancestors origin, embed host name), handled by Molly's xLayout host into the console provider's signIn(token); never to a URL or a log. Molly side is in place: apps/molly/src/molly/credentials.ts (console provider, bearer, credentials omit).

## Brett said (verbatim)
You need to start the pipeline over from scratch. From now on, what I say, send a build to the orchestrator. The orchestrator is going to assign an ID. A build ID. He's going to use you to break it up into steps select a model Babel or Opus Babel when it's needed and then he's going to see how many subscriptions are connected to the VPS how many accounts are available How many, what's the max parallel for each one? And uh, if it's a account that has Fable, he'll send the Fable to that. He'll send everything else to Opus. He will, no, he will check the BPS to see what accounts have what slots. Available parallel. Dish out the steps, okay? The steps are marked. We already have the rules for how the steps are marked down into a, in a progress pile and blah blah blah. Updated in real time because you have a monitor watching the progress files. And um, the orchestrator starts starts the head, headless. The orchestrator then sends it to the queue, or he sends it to pending. Yeah, he sends everything to the pending. And I have to send them from pending to queue.

## Addendum (Brett, voice)
The orchestrator doesn't start a headless session right away. If he has slots open, he grabs the next build in the queue and starts the headless session.

## Context found tonight
- The orchestrator (apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator) has NO launch code: nothing in it starts headless sessions. Only deploy/claude-headless.sh enqueues into agent-slots (framework/cli/agent-slots.mjs).
- Pending items are never auto-imported into the orchestrator; 'import' (orchestrator-core.mjs) only copies existing subPrompts, nothing splits.
- HARD RULE in force: no build starts without an orchestrator build ID (launcher enforces it).
- 'Launch builds without asking' (claude-settings) defaults off.
- Profiles were merged into 'all' on Nov 7; queue flagged needsReprocess.

## Do
1. Intake: every new pending item is auto-imported into the orchestrator with a build ID.
2. Split: the orchestrator calls Claude to split into <=30 min steps and pick Fable only where needed, Opus otherwise; write steps to the build.
3. Flow: builds sit in Pending until Brett moves them to Queue (no auto-queue).

# Orchestrator self-check when stuck: verify each account one by one, clear stale jobs

Launched directly by Brett's request (voice) because the dispatcher is stuck. Orchestrator build record id (filed separately, will be marked built after): `orchestrator-self-check-when-stuck-verify-each-a`.

## Problem
The build pipeline (build-orchestrator plugin, pipeline-status) shows every queued build waiting with "no Claude account is signed in on the VPS" and an empty accounts list, while claude-accounts/list shows mossesx-max- (Max) active and signed in, account-3 (Hulu) saved, and API workers mossesx-api and account-5. The dispatcher's account view is out of sync with claude-workers / claude-login.

## Do
1. Find why pipeline-status `accounts` is empty and why the dispatcher thinks no account is signed in (compare build-orchestrator pipeline code with deploy/claude-workers.mjs and claude-login.mjs). Fix the root cause.
2. Self-check: on console load, on every dispatcher tick where queued builds wait with no launch, and on demand, the orchestrator checks each saved account one by one (subscription logins and API keys: signed in, limited, key valid, free slots), rebuilds its account list from that, and logs what it found.
3. Stale reaper: release running counts / slots / build records with no live tmux session or claude process; requeue or mark their builds. Overlaps pending builds fix-stale-running-counts-per-claude-account-not-cleared and real-time-slot-tracking-stale-data-reaper: fold in what fits.
4. Notify AmberX when the self-check fixes something or finds an account it can't use.
5. Expose the self-check as a control command (API/voice) and show its last result in the orchestrator UI.
6. Tests green, report in _claude/builds/reports/, THREADS row, commit, push, PR. Keep it small; stop and report if blocked.

# Shipped Features: orchestrator manifest + API (urgent)

Brett's words: "Isn't it part of the pipeline?" ... "You put an API on it?" ... "The orchestrator should send a manifest with the information on the shipped feature. Including the prompt that created it and everything."

## Context
- Shipped Features (feature-ledger@1) only updates through the build-hook@1 events fired by builds-store writes (framework/cli/builds-store.mjs). Builds launched straight through vps.build_start tonight had no builds-store record, so nothing reached the ledger.
- `orchestrator-only-launcher` just landed on main (e15e5287681b): the orchestrator is now the only launcher (pipeline.mjs, afterTick hook). Build on that.

## Do
1. Manifest: when a build lands (or a step completes and ships), the orchestrator writes a shipped-feature manifest and sends it to the Shipped Features ledger. It holds: build id and title, Brett's verbatim prompt (the `said` field / brief origin) plus the full brief, model(s) and account(s) used, steps with estimates and actual times, branch, PR, landed commit, files/areas changed, tests run and results, UI Review item, cost and tokens, report path, and what's still open. Schema versioned (shipped-manifest@1), validated.
2. The ledger shows the manifest on each entry (prompt highlighted, collapsible sections).
3. API: Shipped Features gets full API control: list/read/search entries, add/update an entry from a manifest, link to build/PR; via MCP (axf-console tools), axHub, CLI, deep link and voice. Writes go through the builds-store so hooks stay consistent.
4. Backfill: create entries now for builds landed tonight that missed the ledger: `orchestrator-only-launcher` (e15e5287681b) and `urgent-amberx-veto-notice-alarm-too-loud-approve` (commits 864ab0549, 44862718a), using their briefs and reports in _claude/builds/reports/. Add a CLI `shipped backfill --since <date>` that finds landed builds with no ledger entry.
5. Tests for manifest schema, ledger write, API and backfill; console typecheck green. Short report, commit, stop so it can be landed with build_land.

before.title: Orchestrator checks Shipped features before splitting any job
before.detail: When the orchestrator receives a job and splits it into steps, it first checks the Shipped features ledger (which must hold every feature the orchestrator has ever built). It must: not build anything twice; not break or redo anything already done; and if a step would conflict with or change something already built, notify Brett (AmberX notification) and wait before going on. Make the Shipped features ledger complete (backfill every landed build) and keep it updated on every land. Also standing rule: ONLY the orchestrator launches builds, picks model and account, owns pending/queue and monitors status; voice/chat sessions only hand it requests.

notes.text: Conflict flow (Brett): a conflicting step is moved to a special Conflicts section and removed from the build; the other steps still build. Brett gets an AmberX notification-panel item that explains the conflict and offers suggested resolutions; he taps a suggestion or types a prompt, which goes to the orchestrator, and the orchestrator makes a new build from it. Then test it: Brett will send a 3-4 step build that deliberately overlaps existing shipped features to confirm the orchestrator catches it.
Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.

Brett (Nov 9): "needs a way to go through all the pending builds and the build queue and search for steps that are gonna break existing work or conflict with it, or it's already done, or it doesn't need it anymore." Add a Sweep: a button on the builds page (and API/voice: 'sweep the builds') plus an automatic run on every land. It checks every step of every pending and queued build against the Shipped features ledger, main's code, and the other pending/queued builds, and flags each step: Already done (shipped by build X), Conflicts (would change/break feature Y, shows the files and lines), Duplicate (same as a step in build Z), Obsolete (no longer needed: superseded or its target was removed), OK. Results: badges on each build and step, a Sweep report with a filter per flag, and one-tap fixes per flag: drop step, merge into the other build, move to Conflicts for Brett, keep. Nothing is changed without Brett's tap. Cheap first pass in plain code (ledger + file overlap); Claude only for the unclear ones.

Correction (Brett): the Sweep does NOT run automatically on every land. It runs only (1) when Brett runs it (button / API / voice), and (2) by the orchestrator on a single build at two points: when it receives the job, and again right before it dispatches it (launches the session). Flags found at dispatch hold the build for Brett instead of launching.

Merged with orchestrator-checks-each-build-against-main-righ for the 'never build twice' part: every build is now checked against main (Shipped features, its PR, its branch, the files its steps create) right before it is queued and again at dispatch; done = closed, partly done = only what is left is queued. Still open here: the check at split time, the AmberX conflict notice and the ledger backfill.

> when he get receives a job, he splits it up into steps. ## What to build
Continue build "Orchestrator checks Shipped features before splitting any job" (orchestrator-checks-shipped-features-before-spli) — Phase 1, model Opus.

Brett said:
"when he get receives a job, he splits it up into steps. And when he does that, he needs to make sure he needs to check with the shipped features... he needs to make sure he's not doing something twice or fucking up something that's already been done and if it's gonna conflict with something or change something that's already built he's gonna let me know"
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 30 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.

# Build: orchestrator-checks-shipped-features-before-spli

## Brett said (verbatim)
> when he get receives a job, he splits it up into steps. And when he does that, he needs to make sure he needs to check with the shipped features... he needs to make sure he's not doing something twice or fucking up something that's already been done and if it's gonna conflict with something or change something that's already built he's gonna let me know

## What to build
Continue build "Orchestrator checks Shipped features before splitting any job" (orchestrator-checks-shipped-features-before-spli) — Phase 1, model Opus.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said:
"when he get receives a job, he splits it up into steps. And when he does that, he needs to make sure he needs to check with the shipped features... he needs to make sure he's not doing something twice or fucking up something that's already been done and if it's gonna conflict with something or change something that's already built he's gonna let me know"
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 30 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.

[ ] s1 (~30 min) When the orchestrator receives a job and splits it into steps, it first checks the Shipped features ledger (which must hold every feature the orchestrator has ever built). It must: not build anything twice; not break or redo anything already done; and if a step would conflict with or change something already built, notify Brett (AmberX notification) and wait before going on. Make the Shipped features ledger complete (backfill every landed build) and keep it updated on every land. Also standing rule: ONLY the orchestrator launches builds, picks model and account, owns pending/queue and monitors status; voice/chat sessions only hand it requests.
[ ] s2 (~30 min) when he get receives a job, he splits it up into steps. And when he does that, he needs to make sure he needs to check with the shipped features... he needs to make sure he's not doing something twice or fucking up something that's already been done and if it's gonna conflict with something or change something that's already built he's gonna let me know
[ ] s3 (~20 min) Tests green, report _claude/builds/reports/orchestrator-checks-shipped-features-before-spli.md, THREADS row, commit, push, PR

notes.text: Conflict flow (Brett): a conflicting step is moved to a special Conflicts section and removed from the build; the other steps still build. Brett gets an AmberX notification-panel item that explains the conflict and offers suggested resolutions; he taps a suggestion or types a prompt, which goes to the orchestrator, and the orchestrator makes a new build from it. It checks every step of every pending and queued build against the Shipped features ledger, main's code, and the other pending/queued builds, and flags each step: Already done (shipped by build X), Conflicts (would change/break feature Y, shows the files and lines), Duplicate (same as a step in build Z), Obsolete (no longer needed: superseded or its target was removed), OK. Results: badges on each build and step, a Sweep report with a filter per flag, and one-tap fixes per flag: drop step, merge into the other build, move to Conflicts for Brett, keep. Nothing is changed without Brett's tap. Cheap first pass in plain code (ledger + file overlap); Claude only for the unclear ones.

Correction (Brett): the Sweep does NOT run automatically on every land. It runs only (1) when Brett runs it (button / API / voice), and (2) by the orchestrator on a single build at two points: when it receives the job, and again right before it dispatches it (launches the session). Flags found at dispatch hold the build for Brett instead of launching.

Launched directly by Brett's request (voice) because the dispatcher is stuck. Orchestrator build record id (filed separately, will be marked built after): `orchestrator-self-check-when-stuck-verify-each-a`.

## Problem
The build pipeline (build-orchestrator plugin, pipeline-status) shows every queued build waiting with "no Claude account is signed in on the VPS" and an empty accounts list, while claude-accounts/list shows mossesx-max- (Max) active and signed in, account-3 (Hulu) saved, and API workers mossesx-api and account-5. The dispatcher's account view is out of sync with claude-workers / claude-login.

## Do
1. Find why pipeline-status `accounts` is empty and why the dispatcher thinks no account is signed in (compare build-orchestrator pipeline code with deploy/claude-workers.mjs and claude-login.mjs). Fix the root cause.
2. Self-check: on console load, on every dispatcher tick where queued builds wait with no launch, and on demand, the orchestrator checks each saved account one by one (subscription logins and API keys: signed in, limited, key valid, free slots), rebuilds its account list from that, and logs what it found.
3. Stale reaper: release running counts / slots / build records with no live tmux session or claude process; requeue or mark their builds. Overlaps pending builds fix-stale-running-counts-per-claude-account-not-cleared and real-time-slot-tracking-stale-data-reaper: fold in what fits.
4. Notify AmberX when the self-check fixes something or finds an account it can't use.
5. Expose the self-check as a control command (API/voice) and show its last result in the orchestrator UI.
6. Tests green, report in _claude/builds/reports/, THREADS row, commit, push, PR. Keep it small; stop and report if blocked.

Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. notes.text: Merged from build profile "main-framework" into "all" (one profile for everything).

steps.text: Web contract: `framework/core/work.ts` = Kotlin `contract/Work.kt` (`WorkSpec`, `WorkConstraints`, policies, states, `WorkRegistry` of workers by id); fixture `spec/fixtures/work.json` (unique + KEEP/REPLACE/APPEND rules, backoff computation, constraint evaluation with explicit inputs).

Android scheduler: `axf-platform-android` `WorkManagerScheduler` mapping `WorkSpec` → WorkManager requests (constraints, backoff, unique work policy), `WorkRegistry` dispatch inside one `AxfWorker`; capability `axf.work` real; periodic + one-shot; progress through `WorkState` flow. Web scheduler: `framework/libs/work` with a `setTimeout`/visibility-aware scheduler (one-shot + periodic while the page lives, persisted queue in settings so a reload re-enqueues), constraints evaluated with `navigator.connection`/battery where available, else ignored with a terminal note.

steps.text: Plugin skeleton: copy `apps/console-web/plugins/_template` to `plugins/asset-designer` (id `ai.amberx.axf.console.asset-designer`, `uiEditor: "builder"`, lifecycle block, `install.mjs`/`uninstall.mjs`), nav → Plugins → Asset designer, Settings → Plugins sub-tab (parent `plugins`). `node framework/cli/plugin-lifecycle.mjs check asset-designer` passes; console tsc + vite build pass.

Designer shell `web/Designer.tsx`: type picker (every non-attachable type from `asset-types.json` the designer covers: nav-menu, drawer, app-menu, context-menu, toolbar, layout, style-theme, color-theme), id + label fields, Save/Cancel; `useEditorSync()` so it reloads values on focus (UI-editor rule). Saves nothing yet.

Validation gate: every save runs `validateAsset` from the baked `src/axf/core/validate.ts`; errors shown inline next to the field they name; Save disabled until clean. Server route `POST /api/plugins/asset-designer/validate` mirrors it with the CLI validator (`framework/core/project-check.mjs` pattern). Test in `test.py`.

Storage: designed assets saved as asset@1 files under `.axf-console/plugins/asset-designer/assets/<type>/<id>.json` (lifecycle dataDir), served by `GET /api/plugins/asset-designer/assets`, registered into the runtime on load like the theme-manager plugin does (`registry.register`, origin `asset-designer`). Built-in ids refused.

Menu editor (nav-menu, app-menu, context-menu): tree of items (label, icon, action, children, divider), drag to reorder, action picker from `rt.actions.list()`, live preview via `rt.swap` on a `ad-preview-<type>` id. Reuses `MenuList.tsx` for the preview.

Toolbar editor: items (icon, label, action, badge counter), `density`/`surface`/`divider`/`collapsible`, widgets start/end picker from `attachable` types (engine-rpc `app-defaults` → `widgets`), live preview through the React `Toolbar`.

`drawer` asset type: add it to `asset-types.json` (hideable chrome, `side` left/right, `width`, `items` like nav-menu, `modal`), `layout.slots` accept it in the `drawer` region, starter `framework/assets/drawer/amberx-side.json`, `framework/defaults.json` names it. Validators on all three ports accept it (Kotlin: `AssetTypeSpec` resource); fixture case in `layout-slots.json`.

Drawer rendering: React `components/Chrome.tsx` draws the drawer region; Compose `axf-ui/components/Chrome.kt` the same (swipe from the edge, scrim from `--fx-opacity-scrim`). Drawer editor in the designer (same editor as nav-menu plus side/width/modal).

Layout editor: region grid (9 regions from `layout.slots`), per-region size/visibility, `data.slots` overrides with accepted-type chips; preview through `compileLayout`. Hidden slots greyed like Appearance does.

Color-theme editor: token groups from the theme engine (`core/engines/theme.ts` token list), colour pickers, contrast warnings (reuse `theme-manager/web/rollEngine.ts` checks), light/dark pair, preview via `rt.swap`.
Style-theme editor: space, radii, borders, font sizes, opacity tokens (`opacityDisabled/Muted/Hover/Tint/Scrim/Glass`), density; preview; numbers clamped to the ranges known themes use.

Templates hook: "Start from" picker listing starters + designed assets + (later) `x.assets.templates` entries; Duplicate / Rename / Export JSON / Import JSON (validated). Export writes a file a user can drop into an app's assets folder.

Installed by default: plugin `enabled: true` in the console's plugin defaults, `framework/catalog/plugins.json` entry (planned → built resolves by itself), `node framework/cli/plugins.mjs --check`, status.json + tracker; Plugin Manager shows it.

Android face (first slice): `axf-devtools` gets an `AssetDesignerModule` placeholder route `asset-designer` listing designed assets received from the console (read-only), so the plugin-inventory shows it on both ports; full editors stay web-only for now (noted as a placeholder capability `axf.designer`).

Tests: plugin `test.py` (validate route, storage, built-in id refused, lifecycle), web unit cases for the drawer slot + layout compile, CI line; `uninstall.mjs --all` leaves nothing (`check --after-uninstall`).

Close: differences report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/asset-designer.md` (new plugin, so a build report), LOG.md line, web screenshots via `rebuild-shots.mjs`, CLAUDE.md Status, plan epic `x.assets.designer` built via `build_step`, pending item complete.

before.title: Running builds follow the active Claude account, fail over when it dies
before.detail:
## Brett said (verbatim)
Source: voice · At: 2026-11-06
> the running builds need to run on whatever account's connected. If, if the account dies, they need to switch over.
> Every time you log in with a refresh token, you need to update the refresh token.
> why doesn't it switch over? It needs to switch over on its own.

Context: claude_accounts_use to account-2 succeeded and marked it active, but the live VPS login stayed gizmox1111 (loginChanged: true) and the banner clock badge stayed gray. Reverses part of build-own-login (#357). Related: ai-keys-console-store (#358), console-account-picker. Check overlap first.

notes.text: The 'Save the rotated refresh token' steps are built by first-refresh-token-saved-every-time-it-s-used-v (PR #359): tick them once it merges, don't rebuild them.
The 'Save the rotated refresh token' steps are built by first-refresh-token-saved-every-time-it-s-used-v (PR #359): tick them once it merges, don't rebuild them.
Overlap (multi-account-headless-workers): failover is built for worker accounts. Following the active account is unchanged, and any switch must skip workers.
Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

Steps 3-5 (failover on limit/auth death, save rotated token back, banner/alert when no account is left) are built in account-failover-notify (branch claude/account-failover-notify). Steps 1-2 (switching the active account re-signs the VPS login; running builds follow the switch) remain.

Overlap: account-health-failover (PR #394) adds the shared account-status@1 store and capability axf.account-status@1 (able(name, model)): use it to pick the account to switch to instead of a new check.

Folded into account-failover-chain-subscription-next-subscri: pipeline runs now fail over subscription → next subscription → API (pipeline.mjs failover), never the console's account switch; who ran each part is recorded in pipeline.builtBy. Review what is left here once that PR lands.

Folded into account-failover-chain-subscription-next-subscri: a pipeline run whose account fails or hits its limit moves to the next subscription account, then an API account under its caps (pipeline.mjs failover); the account that ran it is recorded in pipeline.builtBy.
Moved to the Archive from pending (console).

steps.text: Switching the active account actually signs the VPS Claude login in to it (live login matches active), banner clock badge goes live
Running headless builds pick up the active account on switch
Failover: on limit/auth death, switch to the next live account by itself and resume
Save the rotated refresh token back after every login/renew
Tests + banner item when no account is left

Running headless builds pick up the active account on switch
Failover: on limit/auth death, switch to the next live account by itself and resume
Save the rotated refresh token back after every login/renew
Tests + banner item when no account is left

before.title: Approvals: no window spam on Approve; veto only for VPS writes and account switches
before.detail:
## Brett said (verbatim)
Source: voice · At: 2026-11-06
> when I click approve and the consoles pop up, I don't want it to launch a window of access. It's opening a thousand fucking windows. And also you only need to send the veto rules that ask for approval or deny if you are actually writing something to the VPS or if you are switching accounts.
> All right, go ahead, build that shit.

Notes: touches Follow Amber approval pop-up (console) and axHub tool policies (veto vs allow). Changing which calls are veto is a policy change in axHub and the shared rule 'It's a veto system'; update rules + decisions.md to match.

notes.text: Overlap with claude-settings-tabs-veto (PR 371): its Approvals & veto tab is the tool for s2 / s5-4 (default plan: hold only VPS writes and account switches). Not ticked: no live policy changed; it needs that build's Fable step s4 (axHub policy API) and Brett's Apply click. s1 pop-up windows and s3 rules are untouched.
s1 / s4-3 covered by PR 375 (claude/approvals-in-place-r2): Approve and Deny act in place, nothing opens a window. The policy and rules steps are untouched.

axHub policy: veto only for calls that write to the VPS or switch Claude accounts; console planner/orchestrator/plan writes and other non-VPS writes run as allow (audited)

# Build: claude-settings-tabs-veto

## Brett said (verbatim)
"The Claude settings interface is getting pretty big. We need to organize it. Give it multiple views, one of them being tabular. If you have it on the tab view, you can set where you want them to appear and how you want them to appear: on the left, on the right, on the top, and the bottom, whether you want the words or an icon." "The veto and the approve are gonna be their own tab in there. Break it down and put it into tabs."
Also: "You don't need to run the 90-second veto thing unless you are writing stuff to the VPS."

1. Audit Claude settings (plugin claude-settings): list every setting, group them into sensible tabs. Report the breakdown.
2. Views: classic (one page, collapsible sections) and tabbed. Tabbed uses the tab-group@1 asset: tab position left / right / top / bottom, labels as words / icons / both. Settings for the view saved per device. Claude settings stays a settings-interface asset.
3. New tab 'Approvals & veto': per axHub tool (or group) choose allow / veto / confirm, veto hold length (seconds), pass durations; reads go without a hold, only VPS writes and account switches hold by default. Writes to the axHub policy through its API (owner-only). Show the current policy table live.
4. REST/MCP/CLI for the view settings and the policy tab.
5. Tests, README, report, screenshots to UI Review, PR to the merge queue. Do NOT land directly. Overlap check with pending item approvals-no-window-spam-on-approve-veto-only-for-vps-writes-and-account-switc; tick its veto step if covered, note it.

One session, lean chain. Stay out of Gizmo, UI registry, badges/notifications code (other builds).
## Addendum 1 (Brett, voice) - where the veto/approval settings live
"Those settings should not be part of the Claude plugin. They can be accessed by any MCP server, the API or the CLI. They can be in Claude settings, they can be in framework settings."

# Build: real-time-slot-tracking-stale-data-reaper

## Brett said (verbatim)
> 

## What to build
Continue build "Real-time slot tracking + stale data reaper" (real-time-slot-tracking-stale-data-reaper) [new feature] — Phase 1, model Opus.
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 30 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. [ ] s3 (~30 min) Stale reaper: a session that misses heartbeats past timeout is killed, its slot freed, and its build set back to queued/pending (or flagged stuck) automatically
[ ] s4 (~30 min) Reconcile on startup and on a timer: build statuses that say running with no live session get fixed automatically
[ ] s5 (~30 min) One-time cleanup of current ghost 'running' builds + reaper log + end-to-end test

Screenshots that are not for approval (checking a screen, live captures, before/after): axf shot <file> --name "…" --app … --screen … --group "<build name>" (UI Review → Screenshots; ui-review-item@1), never the review queue.

This session was started by the orchestrator's dispatcher on Claude account mossesx-max- for the Opus phase. "Brett wants everything in ONE app. Molly becomes the single shell for every app and plugin: Dev Console, axHub web, AmberX, and all future apps. Patches is scrapped. before.title: Orchestrator checks Shipped features before splitting any job
before.detail: When the orchestrator receives a job and splits it into steps, it first checks the Shipped features ledger (which must hold every feature the orchestrator has ever built). It must: not build anything twice; not break or redo anything already done; and if a step would conflict with or change something already built, notify Brett (AmberX notification) and wait before going on. Make the Shipped features ledger complete (backfill every landed build) and keep it updated on every land. Also standing rule: ONLY the orchestrator launches builds, picks model and account, owns pending/queue and monitors status; voice/chat sessions only hand it requests.

notes.text: Conflict flow (Brett): a conflicting step is moved to a special Conflicts section and removed from the build; the other steps still build. Brett gets an AmberX notification-panel item that explains the conflict and offers suggested resolutions; he taps a suggestion or types a prompt, which goes to the orchestrator, and the orchestrator makes a new build from it. Results: badges on each build and step, a Sweep report with a filter per flag, and one-tap fixes per flag: drop step, merge into the other build, move to Conflicts for Brett, keep. Nothing is changed without Brett's tap. Cheap first pass in plain code (ledger + file overlap); Claude only for the unclear ones.

It runs only (1) when Brett runs it (button / API / voice), and (2) by the orchestrator on a single build at two points: when it receives the job, and again right before it dispatches it (launches the session). Flags found at dispatch hold the build for Brett instead of launching.

before.title: Skins are a complete rework: look + layout + behavior, and professional skins
before.detail: After skins-finish lands (skin@1 + skin-coverage@1 for every asset type). Today a skin covers look only; layout and behavior live in design packs. Change: a skin is the complete rework of an app. Extend skin@1 (contract, Fable) to carry everything a design pack does: look (colors, grid and hover/selection colors, typography sizes, spacing/density, radius, borders, shadows, icons, motion), layout (nav placement, app menu, toolbars, banners, panel arrangement, grid density) and behavior (how menus open/slide/collapse, context menu style, hover/press feedback, transitions, overflow rules) for every registry asset type: nav menu, app menu, context menu, grids, dialogs, windows, bars, widgets, text. Design packs fold into skins (migrate, keep a compatibility alias). Applying a skin swaps all of it at once and resets rolled assets (UI Roller rule). CI: every asset type has skin coverage for look, layout and behavior. Then design at least 5 complete professional skins (clean enterprise, dark pro, compact data, modern SaaS, plus one more), applied to the real console, AmberX and Molly; post each to UI Review with desktop and phone shots; the pick becomes the default. Full API/MCP/CLI/voice control. Tests; report.

origin.said: I want the skins to be everything. I want a skin to be a complete rework. Everything. The skins are gonna rewrite the navigation menu, the app menu, the context menu, all the colors in the grids, the hover colors, the text sizes. All the behavior, everything. I need the entire UI reworked to look professional.

steps.text: Extend the skin@1 contract so one skin carries everything a design pack does. steps.text: Make the framework behavior runtime skin-driven. Menu open/slide/collapse, context menu style, hover/press feedback, transitions and overflow rules should all come from the active skin, for every asset type in the registry.
steps.why: Changes how GUI behavior works across all apps

Update the Skins plugin UI. Show look, layout and behavior per skin, add a live preview, add apply and reset-rolled actions, and show a migrated-from-design-pack badge. Give skins full API control, the same across all four surfaces. Operations: list, get, preview, apply, reset rolled assets, set default, read coverage, and run the design-pack migration. Surfaces: REST routes on the console API, MCP tools as console actions and plugin commands, CLI subcommands, and AmberX voice intents. Add console_show / console_open targets.
Design the professional skin 'Clean Enterprise' with complete look, layout and behavior for every asset type.
Design the professional skin 'Dark Pro' with complete look, layout and behavior for every asset type.
Design the professional skin 'Compact Data': dense grids, tight spacing, data-first layout, with complete coverage for every asset type.
Design the professional skin 'Modern SaaS' with complete look, layout and behavior for every asset type.
Design the professional skin 'High Contrast Accessible' (WCAG AAA contrast, larger targets, reduced motion), with complete coverage for every asset type.
Apply all five skins to the real console, AmberX and Molly. Fix any spots that hardcode look, layout or behavior so they follow the skin instead.

Capture desktop and phone screenshots of each skin on the console, AmberX and Molly, then post each skin to UI Review. Wire it so the picked skin becomes the default. API part: make the default readable and settable through REST, MCP, CLI and voice.
Update the docs: skin@1 authoring guide (look, layout, behavior), design-pack migration and alias, and how to reach each skin feature through REST, MCP, CLI and voice.

Tests, report, THREADS row and PR. Tests cover: contract validation, migration plus alias, atomic apply plus rolled-asset reset, layout and behavior runtime, CI coverage, and API parity across REST, MCP, CLI and voice. Write _claude/builds/reports/skins-are-a-complete-rework-look-layout-behavior.md, add the THREADS row, and open the PR stating how each UI feature is reached by deep link, state read, actions and settings.

before.title: Reserve build IDs at once: add returns the ID with the veto countdown
before.detail: Today pending_change add (and control_add on planner.builds/plans) is held on the 90 s veto countdown and the orchestrator only assigns the build ID when it runs, so callers (Claude sessions) must guess the ID from the title to add notes. Fix: the orchestrator (ID registry) reserves the ID the moment the call arrives, before the hold, and returns it in the held result (e.g. reservedId). Notes, sub prompts and status calls on a reserved ID queue up and apply in order once the add runs; if Brett denies the add, the reservation and anything queued on it are dropped. IDs never collide (registry check). Same for plan_park and plan_add. Tests: add returns the id while held; a note on the reserved id lands after the add; deny drops both.

notes.text: Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.
Split by Claude into 8 steps (2 Fable).
Moved to the Archive from pending (console).

origin.said: Why do you have to guess its ID? Why can't you get it? ... Yeah, of course.

steps.text: Design the reservation model in the orchestrator's ID registry. Add a `reserved` state with reservedAt, origin call, kind (build|plan) and holdId. Add a per-ID ordered queue of pending ops (note, sub prompt, status), each with a seq and a payload. Store it in _claude/builds/store.json and add a migration that leaves existing entries untouched. Write the registry API in pipeline-core.mjs: reserveId(title, kind) checks for collisions against live builds, plans, shipped and existing reservations; commitReservation(id) turns a reservation into a real build; dropReservation(id) removes it and its queue.
steps.why: Schema and migration design for the build ID registry, which every port's contract depends on

steps.text: Change the veto-hold contract so the ID is reserved before the hold starts. Held results carry reservedId, holdId and secondsLeft. On approve or timeout, commitReservation runs and then the queued ops are replayed in seq order. On deny, dropReservation runs. Write down the contract for every caller: pending_change add, control_add on planner.builds/plans, plan_park, plan_add.
steps.why: Cross-port contract change to the held-result shape that all callers rely on

steps.text: Wire pending_change add and control_add (planner.builds and planner.plans) through reserveId so the held result returns reservedId right away. Approve and deny on the hold call commit or drop the reservation.
Wire plan_park and plan_add the same way: reserve the ID before the hold, return reservedId in the held result, and commit or drop when the hold resolves.

Queue notes, sub prompts and status calls that target a reserved ID. The note, sub prompt and status handlers check whether the ID is reserved and, if so, add the op to the queue instead of failing. The queued result says queued:true with its seq. Replay applies the ops in order after the add runs.
Show the reserved ID and the queued op count on the veto countdown card in the console Build manager. Add a 'copy ID' action. Deep link: console_show target build-orchestrator/hold/<reservedId>.

API part for the reservation and countdown UI. REST: GET /api/builds/reservations and GET /api/builds/reservations/<id> read the state (status, secondsLeft, queued ops); POST approve and POST deny act on the hold. MCP: console actions builds.reservation.get, builds.reservation.approve and builds.reservation.deny, plus control@1 for planner items. CLI: axf builds reservation get|approve|deny <id>. AmberX voice intents for the same three actions. All four surfaces call the same handlers.

Tests, report and PR. Write tests for: add returns the ID while held; a note on the reserved ID lands after the add runs; deny drops the reservation and its queued note; no ID collision when two adds with the same title arrive together; plan_park and plan_add return reservedId; REST, MCP and CLI give the same results. Write _claude/builds/reports/reserve-build-ids-at-once-add-returns-the-id-wit.md. Add the THREADS row. Open the PR, stating how the reservation and countdown are reached through the deep link, REST, MCP, CLI and voice.

before.title: Permissions control panel: every axHub tool's policy in one place
before.detail: Repo: axHub (policy store) + console/axhub-web screen. One Permissions panel listing every connected service and every tool (vps.build_start, vps.run, axf-console.*, github, hostinger, amberx...) with its policy (allow / veto countdown / confirm / deny), countdown length, who may call it (Brett's sessions, Claude sessions, headless builds, agents), and passes. Brett changes a policy with a dropdown; bulk change per service or by filter (destructive, writes, reads). Tree grouped by service > category, search, filters, live type-ahead. Every change logged with history and undo. Claude sessions and builds can read policies but never change them (owner-only, enforced on the hub, not just the UI). First change: set vps.build_start to deny so only the orchestrator launches builds. Full API (read for all, write owner-only), voice for Brett. 3 layout options to UI Review.

notes.text: Brett: "Can I make it so that employees like Molly or Amber or Moses can use it, and then I assign one of the employees to the orchestrator so the orchestrator can say run it, change it?" Permissions are granted per employee (agent from the one roster: Molly, Amber, Moses, Brownie, etc.), not just per session type. Brett assigns an employee to the orchestrator; the orchestrator acts with that employee's permissions. Brett can grant an employee permission to change policies, but only within a ceiling Brett sets: an employee can never raise its own or another's permissions above the ceiling, never touch owner-only settings or the ceiling itself, every change it makes is logged with the employee's name and sends Brett a notification, and Brett can revoke instantly. Panel shows per-employee view and per-tool view.
Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.
Split by Claude into 15 steps (2 Fable).
Moved to the Archive from pending (console).

origin.said: I need a control panel for all those settings, those permission settings.

steps.text: Design the axHub policy store schema and migration. One record per tool (service, tool id, category tags destructive/writes/reads, mode allow|veto|confirm|deny, countdown seconds, allowed callers brett-session|claude-session|headless-build|agent, passes). Add an append-only change-history table with actor, before/after and undo link. Write a migration that imports today's scattered veto/confirm/pass settings into the store without changing any effective policy.
steps.why: Schema plus migration design for the hub's central policy store

steps.text: Define the cross-port policy contract axhub-policy@1. It covers REST shapes (tree, search, filter, get, set, bulk set, history, undo), MCP tool names, control@1 ops, the CLI verbs, the live change event stream, and owner-only write semantics with error codes. Every surface (console API, MCP, CLI, AmberX voice) maps 1:1 to it.
steps.why: Cross-port contract shared by hub, console, MCP, CLI and voice

steps.text: Build the tool registry inventory. Enumerate every connected service and tool (vps.build_start, vps.run, axf-console.*, github, hostinger, amberx, ...) from the hub's connection manifests. Classify each tool into a category and destructive/writes/reads, and seed missing tools with a safe default (confirm). Re-sync when a service connects or disconnects.

Enforce policies on the hub, not in the UI. The tool-call gate resolves caller identity (Brett session, Claude session, headless build, agent) and applies allow/veto countdown/confirm/deny plus the caller list and passes. Policy writes are owner-only: any non-owner caller gets 403 with a clear message. Reads stay open to all authenticated callers.

Add the history and undo service. Every single or bulk change is written as one history entry, with a bulk change grouped under one id. Undo restores the before-state, is itself logged, and is also owner-only. Each change emits a live event for the panel.

Add the REST routes: GET /policies (tree grouped by service > category, with q= type-ahead search and filters by mode/category/caller), GET /policies/:tool, PUT /policies/:tool, POST /policies/bulk (by service or by filter), GET /policies/history, POST /policies/history/:id/undo. Write routes go through owner-only enforcement. Proxy the routes through the console API.

Expose the same operations through MCP and the CLI. Add MCP console actions (policy.list/get/set/bulk/history/undo), control@1 ops for policy items, and CLI `axf policy list|get|set|bulk|history|undo` with the same filters. Writes from Claude sessions and builds are rejected by the hub.

Add AmberX voice intents for Brett. Read intents: 'what's the policy for vps.run', 'which tools are deny'. Write intents: 'set github writes to confirm', 'undo last permission change', 'open permissions'. Writes need the owner voice session and are spoken back before they apply.

Build the shared Permissions panel core in console/axhub-web. It includes the data hook on GET /policies with live events, the policy dropdown per tool, countdown and caller editors, pass list, bulk change bar (per service or current filter), live type-ahead search, filter chips (destructive/writes/reads, mode, caller), and a history drawer with undo. Register deep link console_show/console_open target 'permissions' (with optional tool= / service= / filter=). Make the panel state readable via the console state API.

Build layout option A: a collapsible tree (service > category > tool) with an inline dropdown per row and a sticky bulk bar. It reuses the core and adds no new actions. The deep link 'permissions?layout=a' and the state read come from the core.

Build layout option B (dense filterable table with column sort and multi-select) and layout option C (service cards with a per-service default and expandable tool lists). Both reuse the core. Add deep links 'permissions?layout=b|c'.
Submit the 3 layouts to UI Review with screenshots and deep links. Add a setting for the chosen layout, readable and settable through REST, MCP, CLI (`axf policy layout`) and voice.

Make the first change as owner through the API: set vps.build_start to deny for every caller except the orchestrator's build-launch identity (via a pass). Check that a Claude session and a headless build are refused and that the orchestrator still launches builds. Record the change in policy history.

Write tests covering: migration keeps effective policies unchanged; enforcement for every mode and caller; owner-only writes rejected for Claude sessions, builds and agents on REST, MCP, CLI and voice; bulk by service and by filter; history and undo; registry sync; type-ahead search and filters; deep link and state read for each layout.

Run the full test suites and fix any failures. Write the report _claude/builds/reports/permissions-control-panel-every-axhub-tool-s-pol.md (what was built, the vps.build_start change, how each UI part is reached via deep link, state read, REST, MCP, CLI and voice). Add the THREADS row and open the PR, with the same API access table in the PR description.

before.title: Session transcripts API: search what was said, find which session
before.detail: Builds on ui-review-notify-session-audio (landed Nov 7): sessions are recorded by AmberX's Audio Output Recorder (output-recorder plugin) and transcribed by the faster-whisper worker, transcripts saved on the hub, readable in the recorder page. Today output-recorder's plugin.json declares no transcript commands, so nothing outside the page can read them. Add full API (plugin-commands@1, so MCP/axHub, REST, CLI, voice come for free): list sessions with transcripts (date, length, linked Claude session, title); read one transcript (whole or a time range, with timestamps); search across all transcripts (words or phrase, date range, fuzzy), returning the matching session, timestamp, a few lines of context, and a deep link that opens the recorder page at that moment (and plays the audio there). Also a 'find the session where we talked about X' command that ranks sessions by match. Reachable from Claude chat/voice sessions through axHub so Claude or Gizmo can answer 'which session did we talk about this'. Read-only; respects the recorder's settings. Tests; report.

notes.text: Brett: "I can find that internally without AI, right?" Yes: all search is plain code with zero tokens (full-text index over the transcripts, phrase + fuzzy + date filters). Add a search box with live type-ahead results on the recorder page and in the console's Search everything, so Brett can find a session himself without any AI. Claude/Gizmo only call the same plain search through the API.
Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.

Brett: results pop up in a scrolling window. As Brett types in Search everything (or the recorder page), matching transcript snippets pop up live in a scrolling results window: each hit shows the session (date, title), timestamp and a few lines around the match with the words highlighted; infinite scroll, grouped by session, newest first with a sort switch. Tapping a hit opens the recorder at that moment and plays the audio. Plain search also drops filler phrases like 'find the session where', 'when we talked about' so a whole sentence still works, zero tokens.

Brett: "With the keywords in focus." In the scrolling results window each snippet is centered on the matched keywords, highlighted. Opening a hit scrolls the transcript so the keyword is centered on screen, highlighted and focused, with next/previous match buttons inside that session.

Brett: "there's a column on the left with all the hits. All the sessions that match: the session name and the type of thing we were talking about." Results window layout: left column lists every session with hits (session name, date, hit count, and a topic tag for what it was about, e.g. builds, skins, approvals, AmberX); tapping one shows its hits on the right, keywords centered and highlighted. Topic tags: from the linked Claude session's title and the builds it touched (plain code, zero tokens); optionally a cheap one-time tag per session after transcription, off by default.

Brett: "I want a RAG database made of all the transcripts." Build a RAG store over every transcript: chunk each transcript (with session, date, timestamps, speaker, topic tags), embed the chunks with a local embedding model on the VPS (no Claude tokens), store them in Postgres with pgvector (reuse the postgres-console container plan if it exists, else its own table), and index every new transcript automatically after transcription. Two ways in: 1) semantic search (meaning, not just exact words) in the same results window, mixed with the keyword hits; 2) 'Ask' (API/MCP/voice): Claude or Gizmo retrieve the top chunks and answer with the sessions and timestamps as sources, each linking to that moment. Share the store with the Agent Manager's RAG knowledge (agent-profile build) so employees can use it. Settings: on/off, re-index, what gets indexed. Tests: retrieval returns the right session for a paraphrased question.
Split by rules (Claude: claude not available: spawnSync claude ETIMEDOUT): one step per line of the request, review the steps.
Split by Claude into 11 steps (1 Fable).
Moved to the Archive from pending (console).

origin.said: I want the API to be able to access the transcript so I can tell you or I can tell Gizmo, you know, what session was it that we talked about this or that.

steps.text: Design the transcript index: a schema for per-session metadata (id, date, length, title, linked Claude session id) and timestamped segments that the hub transcripts map onto, plus a migration that backfills the index from transcripts already saved on the hub. Document the contract that the API commands return (session, segment, match with context and deep link).
steps.why: Schema + migration design and a cross-port contract that MCP, REST, CLI and voice all share

steps.text: Build a read-only transcript reader over the hub store. It lists sessions that have transcripts (date, length, linked Claude session, title) with paging and date filters, and reads one transcript either whole or for a start/end time range, with a timestamp on every segment.

Build search across all transcripts. It supports words, exact phrase, date range and fuzzy matching (typo-tolerant), and returns the matching session, timestamp, a few lines of context and a deep link. Add the find-session ranking, which scores each session by its matches (count, phrase proximity, recency) for 'the session where we talked about X'.

Enforce the recorder's settings in the reader and search: recording or transcription off, retention window, sessions excluded or marked private, and the hub read scope. Every path stays read-only with no writes or deletes, and blocked results are returned as clear errors.

Declare the transcript commands in output-recorder plugin.json under plugin-commands@1: transcripts.list, transcripts.read, transcripts.search, transcripts.find_session and recorder.page_state. Each gets a parameter schema and is wired to its handler, so axHub MCP, console REST, CLI and voice pick them up.

Recorder page deep link (UI change, with its API part in this same step). The page opens at ?session=<id>&t=<sec>&play=1, scrolls the transcript to that moment, seeks the audio and plays it. Register it as a console_show/console_open target. The page state (open session, position, playing) is readable through recorder.page_state, and the open, seek and play actions are callable without the UI over REST, MCP, CLI and voice.

Make sure the commands are exposed the same way on REST (console API routes) and the CLI (transcripts list/read/search/find-session with --from/--to/--fuzzy/--json). Help text and output include the deep link.

Expose the commands through axHub MCP for Claude chat and voice sessions and Gizmo. Add voice intents for 'which session did we talk about X', 'read what was said at …' and 'open that session'. The spoken answer gives the session title, date and timestamp, and offers to open the deep link.

Unit tests: reader time ranges and timestamps, phrase, word and fuzzy search, date filter, context lines, find_session ranking order, policy enforcement (disabled, retention, private, read-only), and the index backfill migration.

Parity and integration tests: the same query through REST, MCP, CLI and voice gives the same result. The deep link opens the recorder page at the timestamp and plays the audio, and recorder.page_state reflects it.

Run the full test suite and fix any failures. Write the report, add the THREADS row and open the PR. The PR describes how each feature is reached: deep link, state read, actions and settings via REST, MCP, CLI and voice.

before.detail: Seen Nov 9: claude_accounts shows Hulu 1/3, Moses X 4/3, account-1 4/3 running while the VPS has 0 tmux axf-* sessions and 0 claude -p processes. Rule (Brett): every time the console loads, and on the watchdog tick, the orchestrator checks for stale runs and releases any slot or running entry with no live process (agent-slots, claude-workers.mjs counts, orchestrator.json statuses). Find why the existing check didn't run or didn't clear these; fix; add a test with fake stale entries; log each release.

notes.text: ROOT CAUSE (found live): deploy/claude-workers.mjs liveSessions() runs `tmux ls`; when NO tmux sessions exist, tmux exits non-zero ('no server running'), so it returns null = 'can't ask tmux'. Then ledger() counts every open session as running and liveClaims keeps claims for 12 h. So the stale entries survive exactly when nothing is running. Fix: treat 'no server running' (tmux present, exit 1) as an empty Set; only return null when tmux binary is missing. Test it.

Root cause fixed in PR #406 (claude/orch-self-check-stuck): tmux 'no server running' was read as unknown, so every unclosed session in events.jsonl counted as running. Self-check on console load and stuck ticks releases dead claims, expired limits and builds with no session; tests in claude-workers.test.mjs and pipeline.test.mjs; each release logged.

Remove every other builds table and the separate Build queue screen (redirect).

Each build is one clean compact line (title, priority, status badge, steps done/total, account, model) that expands; inside the expanded row, collapsible sections/sub-grids (steps with state, runs/sessions, cost, files/PR, Brett's words, log tail). before.title: Saved Claude logins never end up on a spent refresh token
before.detail: Builds run on a per-build copy of a saved login (claude-login.mjs). Refresh tokens are single-use: when a build refreshes, the new token lands in the copy; if the copy is deleted before the rotation is written back (claude-token-save.mjs release/sweep), the saved login keeps a spent token and every later launch fails with 'OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed' (seen on account-1 and account-3, Nov 9). Fix: find every path where the rotation is lost (crash, kill, exit 1, sweep timing, two builds refreshing the same login at once), write rotations back atomically with a lock, never let two copies refresh the same login concurrently, and before launch check the saved login is alive; if dead, skip that account, alert the phone, and don't burn runs on it. Tests for each path.

You'll see an alert pop up, and then right in the group chat, John said this or Jim said that, as things go on in the demonstration. Make mock events: a mock build gets done, a mock error is reported, a mock build failed, something being added to the queue or the orchestrator. Drag slices into slots, preview the whole console live, see which slots are empty, swap or clear slots, before/after toggle. Save, apply, export or import as a file, duplicate, edit later. 5) Professional polish: snap animations, slot highlights, desktop and phone layouts. 6) Full control via REST, MCP, CLI and voice (list sections, save section, apply with includes/excludes, build skin from sections, export). Screenshots go to UI Review grouped by screen.

origin.said: When you're looking at these lists and any of the grids of these chunks, you can preview one, or open a demo of it if it can be demoed, an interactive demonstration where you can actually use it, or at the very least a preview of what the chunk looks like. An IDE-style thing with a bunch of floating tab groups with different types of assets in them, with the info on the chunk, and you can drag them to each other and build new things side by side. Chunk manifest fields: demo capability (interactive kind: behaviour, layout or component; sandbox entry; rendered-preview fallback) and a thumbnail spec. Studio layout document: tab groups (docked or floating, position and size), tabs (asset ref, type, split state), compare containers, and named saved layouts. steps.why: Schema and migration design shared by the skins, demo and studio ports

steps.text: Extend the framework IDE layout engine taken from walkthrough-player-ide-layout. Tab groups become dockable or floating. Groups hold tabs of any asset type through a tab-type registry. Tabs can be dragged between groups and between docked and floating groups. Groups can be nested into compare containers. All of this is driven by the new layout document.
steps.why: Changes how the IDE-layout GUI works for every app that uses it

steps.text: Add the split-tab primitive and the live-update channel. Any tab can split into an editor pane and a preview pane. Edits flow to the preview in real time over a debounced change stream with the same contract for every asset type. Bad edits show an error overlay in the preview and keep the last good render.
steps.why: Engine internals and a cross-port editor/preview contract

Chunks that cannot be demoed fall back to a rendered preview. The Demo action is added next to Preview in every list and grid.

Add the IDE studio as an optional view, off by default and switched on with a setting, not forced. Wire split tabs into the studio and compare views for every asset tab type. Each type gets an editor and a live preview that updates in real time over the live-preview channel, with a split toggle on every tab.

Add saving and restoring of layouts. Named studio and compare layouts can be saved, listed, restored, renamed and deleted. They are stored per profile and the last-used layout is restored automatically.

Add full API control for compare, the studio, split tabs, compose and layouts. Deep links: console_open skins/studio, skins/compare?chunks=… and skins/studio?layout=…. All of it the same through REST, MCP (console actions and plugin commands, control@1 for tokens), the CLI and voice.
Capture desktop and phone screenshots of the list previews, demo sandbox, rendered fallback, compare, studio, info panel, split tab and layouts, and send them to UI Review grouped by screen.

steps.why: Engine internals and a cross-port editor/preview contract

steps.text: Add server-side preview rendering for skin chunks and UI assets: a cached thumbnail renderer and a full-preview render endpoint. Thumbnails are invalidated when a chunk changes. Reuse the UI asset designer renderer.

Add a preview action to every list and grid that shows skin chunks or assets: the skins section-package lists, pack grids, the UI asset designer library and the demonstration designer pickers. Hovering shows a thumbnail and Preview opens a full preview pane.

Add full API control for preview. Deep link console_open target skins/preview/<chunk>. Readable preview state. Actions preview.open, preview.close and preview.thumbnail. All of it reachable the same way through REST routes, MCP console actions and plugin commands, the CLI and AmberX voice intents.

Add the interactive demo. Demo opens a live sandbox for demoable chunks (behaviour, layouts, components) by reusing the Demonstration designer sandbox, so you can actually use the chunk. Chunks that cannot be demoed fall back to a rendered preview. The Demo action is added next to Preview in every list and grid.

Add full API control for demo. Deep link console_open skins/demo/<chunk>. Readable sandbox state (running, mode interactive or rendered). Actions demo.open, demo.reset and demo.close. All of it reachable through REST, MCP, CLI and voice.

Add the compare view. Open any number of chunks side by side in containers that can be docked or floating. Containers can mix asset types, and each container is a tab group from the extended layout engine.

Add the IDE studio as an optional view, off by default and switched on with a setting, not forced. It shows floating and dockable tab groups holding any asset types, plus a chunk info panel with name, category, source skin, tags and used-by. Used-by comes from a reverse-reference index built on the server.

Add drag-to-compose in the studio. Dropping a chunk onto another chunk, or into a pack template, creates a new skin or asset draft through the UI asset designer and the skins section-package builder, then opens the draft in a new tab.

Wire split tabs into the studio and compare views for every asset tab type. Each type gets an editor and a live preview that updates in real time over the live-preview channel, with a split toggle on every tab.

Add saving and restoring of layouts. Named studio and compare layouts can be saved, listed, restored, renamed and deleted. They are stored per profile and the last-used layout is restored automatically.

Add full API control for compare, the studio, split tabs, compose and layouts. Deep links: console_open skins/studio, skins/compare?chunks=… and skins/studio?layout=…. All of it the same through REST, MCP (console actions and plugin commands, control@1 for tokens), the CLI and voice.
Capture desktop and phone screenshots of the list previews, demo sandbox, rendered fallback, compare, studio, info panel, split tab and layouts, and send them to UI Review grouped by screen.

Add tests for the schema migration, the layout engine (drag, float, dock), split live updates, the preview, demo, compose and layout routes, and REST/MCP/CLI/voice parity. Then write the report at _claude/builds/reports/skin-chunk-previews-interactive-demos-and-an-ide.md, add the THREADS row, and open the PR. The PR lists how each UI feature is reached through deep link, REST, MCP, CLI and voice.
