If no live git process holds them and they're older than 2 minutes, remove them. 2) Stray files that block landing (assets.log, build logs, _claude/builds sync files): restore tracked ones and stash or ignore untracked ones, then retry the land automatically. 3) Crashed sessions: tmux or claude processes dead with the build marked running get reset and requeued (works with the reaper). 4) Every auto-fix is logged in the fix log and Automatic fixes notes, with an AmberX FYI. 5) Same guard after any git operation fails with a lock error: clear it and retry once. 6) Tests with fake locks and crashed runs. Same bug twice gets a guard, per it-has-to-work.

before.title: One VPS plugin: everything VPS in one place (gauges, banner widget with heat-colour icons and dropdown, cleanup, settings, status)
before.detail: ONE VPS plugin (e.g. 'VPS'), reachable from Maintenance and its own nav entry. 1) CONSOLIDATE: find every VPS-related feature across the console and move it into this plugin as tabs or sections, leaving no duplicates behind. That includes the claude-badge VPS check, agent-slots resource and swap settings and warnings, the VPS settings/orchestrator-only rule plugin (from vps-orchestrator-only-rule-vps-settings-console), Docker/container views, container-access, the Coolify/Hostinger links, VPS terminal shortcuts, ai-keys VPS sync, maintenance cleanup/redundancy scans, the disk alerts, and the running-builds watchdog's resource bits. Old entry points redirect to the new plugin. 2) STATUS tab: live gauges and meters for CPU load (1/5/15 min), RAM, swap, disk per filesystem, plus Docker per-container CPU/RAM and the top processes. Several views (radial, bars, compact strip, history sparklines), switchable and remembered, with adjustable thresholds. 3) BANNER WIDGET: a snappable widget for the banner, toolbars and title bars, with modes icon only, icon plus value, or mini meters. It has its own settings (metrics, mode, thresholds, refresh). 4) ICON-ONLY HEAT COLOUR: each icon's colour follows its level on a smooth scale, white (low) to gray to black to red (high). The stops are editable and the theme can override them. 5) BANNER DROPDOWN: clicking any banner gauge opens a dropdown listing every gauge, one row each: a dot in the same heat colour as that gauge, the name (Load, RAM, Swap, Disk /), the percentage, and the actual values (e.g. 9.4 / 16 GB). Rows update live, the clicked one is highlighted, and the footer has Open VPS plugin and quick cleanup links. 6) CLEANUP tab: docker builder/image/container prune, apt/npm/pip caches, journal vacuum, old build worktrees and logs, /tmp, the Playwright cache, and stale git locks. Each has a size preview and a confirm, shows the space freed and logs to the fix log. Optional auto-cleanup over a threshold (off by default). 7) SETTINGS tab: every VPS setting in one place. Plain code, no AI. Full REST, MCP, CLI and voice control. Desktop and phone screenshots go to UI Review.

before.title: Landing tool takes long build names, and auto-fixes and retries failed lands
before.detail: vps.build_land, build_start, build_stop and build_clean reject names over 40 characters (^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,39}$), but the orchestrator makes build IDs up to about 50 characters (e.g. demo-designer-finish-phase-2-s2-s3-resuming-from, skins-restyle-everything-badges-banner-and-every-visual-element). 1) In the axHub vps service, raise the name limit to match the orchestrator's longest IDs (at least 80), keeping the same safe character set. 2) If the orchestrator ever makes an ID the tools can't take, it shortens it consistently (folder, branch, tmux) instead of failing. 3) When build_land fails for any fixable reason (stray files, stale locks, name format), it fixes it and retries automatically, logging to the fix log. Real code clashes go to a conflict-fix build automatically. 4) Tests with long names. Repos: axHub (vps service config) and AmberX-AXF (orchestrator).

notes.text: Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.
Split by Claude into 9 steps (1 Fable).
Moved to the Archive from pending (console).

origin.said: Why, when it has a problem, when it gets rejected, aren't you just fixing it right away? I keep telling you over and over.

steps.text: Define the shared build-name contract used by both repos. Allowed names match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,79}$ (80 characters). Define one deterministic shortener: trim at a hyphen boundary, then append -<6-char hash of the full ID>, so the same long ID always maps to the same short name. The folder, branch and tmux session all use the short name. The orchestrator records long→short in its build record. Write the contract doc and the reference shortener module with its constants (max length, charset, hash length).
steps.why: Cross-port contract between the axHub vps service and the AmberX-AXF orchestrator

steps.text: axHub vps service: replace the hard-coded ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,39}$ in build_land, build_start, build_stop and build_clean with one shared constant from service config allowing up to 80 characters, with the same safe character set. Error messages state the limit and the offending length.

Orchestrator: route every place that makes a build ID, worktree folder, branch name or tmux session through build-name.mjs. When an ID exceeds the tools' limit, shorten it consistently instead of failing. Store long_id and short_id in the build record and journal. Lookups accept either form.
files: AmberX-AXF: apps/orchestrator/ (ID creation, worktree, branch, tmux spawn)

steps.text: Orchestrator: build_land failure classifier. Parse build_land errors into categories: stray_files (untracked or tmp files such as *.json.tmp-*), stale_lock (index.lock or a stale land lock with a dead PID), name_format (rejected name), code_conflict (real merge conflict) and unknown. Unit-testable pure function with fixtures from real failure output.

Orchestrator: auto-fix and retry loop around build_land. For each fixable category, apply the fixer: remove or commit stray tmp files after looking at them, clear stale locks only if the owning PID is dead, re-derive the short name for format rejects. Then retry, up to 3 attempts. Each attempt, fix and outcome is appended to the fix log. Land state (attempt, last error, fix applied) is readable through the existing console build API, MCP, CLI and voice status read.
files: AmberX-AXF: apps/console-web/ build status route/MCP/CLI land-state fields

steps.text: Orchestrator: on code_conflict, or when retries are used up on an unknown error, automatically queue a conflict-fix build. The queued build links to the parent build, the conflicting files and the failed land log. The parent build is marked waiting-on-fix in place of failed. Log it to the fix log.

axHub tests: build_land, build_start, build_stop and build_clean accept the 50 to 64 character real IDs (demo-designer-finish-phase-2-s2-s3-resuming-from, skins-restyle-everything-badges-banner-and-every-visual-element) and an exactly-80-character name. They reject 81 characters, uppercase, a leading hyphen, slashes and dots.

AmberX-AXF tests: the shortener is deterministic, stays within the limit, keeps the folder, branch and tmux names identical, and has no collisions across the existing shipped build IDs. The classifier fixtures pass. The auto-fix loop recovers from stray files, stale locks and name format errors and logs to the fix log. A code conflict queues a conflict-fix build. A full long-name start, land and clean path is checked end to end against a mock vps.

Run the full test suites in both repos. Write the report: what changed, the name contract, each auto-fix category, the API reach of land state (REST, MCP, CLI, voice) and the test results with before and after. Add the THREADS row. Open PRs in axHub and AmberX-AXF, cross-linked, axHub merged first.

before.title: Auto-land every build the moment it finishes, redeploy the console on every land, and backfill the 134 unlanded
before.detail: Plain code in the orchestrator dispatcher, no AI. 1) The moment a build's session finishes with its steps ticked and tests green, the orchestrator lands it straight away: clean sync files and stray logs, clear stale locks, merge origin/main, rerun the build's own tests, push to main. No waiting on a person or a later session. 2) UPDATE THE CONSOLE ON EVERY LAND: right after each push to main, trigger the console redeploy immediately (the same path as install-console.sh's auto-update, run now, not on the 5-minute timer), and rebuild any other app the change touched (AmberX web, axHub web, Molly and so on). Wait for it to come up healthy, then refresh open consoles. If the deploy fails, roll back to the last good image and queue a fix. 3) UI Review never blocks landing: screenshots and picks can follow after landing, and changes come as follow-up builds. 4) If main moved and tests fail after the merge, or there's a code clash, the orchestrator immediately queues a conflict-fix run on the same branch (top priority, any working account) and lands when green. It retries until it's on main. 5) Land in finish order, one at a time (a merge lock), so each lands on the newest main. Batch redeploys if several land within a minute. 6) Backfill now: land every finished-but-unlanded build (about 134), oldest first, skipping ones superseded or already on main, with conflict-fix runs where needed. 7) Each land and deploy shows in the Activity Monitor and fix log, with a phone FYI only for failures that need Brett. Tests with fake clashes and a fake failed deploy. Supersedes any auto-land pieces in other builds; don't duplicate.

Step 1 must not push to main: a finished build gets its PR and joins the merge queue (push-banner land/merge-queue.mjs enlist does this every 3 min already); the queue batches the ready PRs into one build on queue/batch, runs CI once and lands it on main as one commit. Redeploy-on-land happens once per landed batch. Keep the backfill: it should open PRs into the queue, not push.

origin.said: You realize when you don't merge stuff right away you have to pull in main again, and tests are gonna fail. Why do you not just merge this as soon as it's done? ... Right, so when something lands, update the console. Period.

steps.text: Design the land pipeline contract inside the orchestrator dispatcher. Define the land-queue state machine (finished → queued → locked → cleaning → merging → testing → pushed → deploying → landed | conflict-fix | deploy-failed). Define a merge lock that lands builds one at a time in finish order. Add a land record schema to the build store (landedAt, mainSha, deployId, attempts, lastError) with a migration that also adds a 'landed' field to existing builds. Write it up in the orchestrator README.
steps.why: Engine internals plus a schema and migration that every later step and the backfill depend on

steps.text: Implement the land core as plain code with no AI. Under the merge lock: delete sync temp files (*.tmp-*) and stray logs (.axf-*.log, .axf-brief.md), clear stale locks, fetch and merge origin/main into the build branch, rerun the build's own tests from its brief/report, then push to main. Return a typed result: landed, clash or tests-failed.
steps.why: Core dispatcher engine path that every land and the backfill run through

steps.text: Wire auto-land into the session-finish handler in the dispatcher. When a build's session ends with all steps ticked and tests green, put it on the land queue straight away, in finish order. Make UI Review non-blocking: screenshots and picks get queued as follow-ups after landing, and changes become follow-up builds. Remove the gates that waited on a person or a later session.

Add conflict-fix runs. On a clash, or on tests failing after the merge, queue a conflict-fix session on the same branch at top priority on any working account, using a fixed prompt template. When it finishes green, put the build back on the land queue. Retry until it is on main, with backoff and an attempts counter in the land record.

Redeploy the console on every land. Pull the auto-update path out of install-console.sh into a callable redeploy script and run it right after each push to main, with no 5-minute timer. Batch redeploys when several lands happen within 60 s. Wait for the health check to pass, then send a refresh event to open consoles.

Rebuild the other apps a land touched. Map the changed paths to apps (AmberX web, axHub web, Molly, …) and rebuild and redeploy each one, with its own health wait. This uses the same batch window as the console redeploy.

Add deploy rollback. Keep a last-good image tag for each app. When a deploy fails or its health check times out, roll back to that tag, record deploy-failed in the land record, and queue a fix build that carries the deploy log.

Report every land and deploy. Emit Activity Monitor events and fix-log entries for queued, landed, conflict-fix, deployed, rolled back and failed. Send a phone FYI only for failures that need Brett: a rollback that also failed, or a build still not on main after N conflict-fix attempts.

Add a Land queue panel to the Activity Monitor UI. It shows the queue, the current lock holder, recent lands and deploys, and conflict-fix runs. It offers these actions: land now, retry, skip, roll back. It has these settings: auto-land on/off and the batch window in seconds.

Give the Land queue full API control, the same across all four surfaces. Deep link: console_show / console_open target 'activity-monitor/land'. State read: the queue, the lock and the land records. Actions: land now, retry, skip, roll back, start backfill. Settings: auto-land and batch window. Expose these through REST routes, MCP console actions and plugin commands, the axf CLI subcommands 'land' and 'deploy', and AmberX voice intents.

Implement the backfill command. List the finished-but-unlanded builds, oldest first. Skip any that are superseded (checked through supersedes links) or already on main (checked with git merge-base --is-ancestor or a patch-id match). Put the rest on the land queue, which uses conflict-fix runs where needed. Support a --dry-run report.

Remove the duplicate auto-land pieces. Find the auto-land and merge code in other builds and modules (including build-manager leftovers and the shipping unblock in the orchestrator) and point them at the new land pipeline. Mark the overlapping queued builds as superseded by this one.

Write tests for the land pipeline using temporary git repos. Cover: the merge lock and finish order, a fake code clash leading to a conflict-fix run, a fake test failure after the merge, redeploy batching within 60 s, a fake failed deploy leading to rollback and a fix build, backfill skipping superseded and already-on-main builds, and API parity across REST, MCP and CLI.

Start the backfill. Run it with --dry-run and save the list in the report, then start the real backfill of about 134 builds, oldest first. Watch the first lands and redeploys come up healthy in the Activity Monitor, and note what is still queued.

Final step. Run the full test suite. Write the report at _claude/builds/reports/auto-land-every-build-the-moment-it-finishes-red.md, covering the backfill status and how each feature is reached through deep link, REST, MCP, CLI and voice. Add the THREADS row, then open the PR with the API reach list.

before.title: Claude Accounts Manager plugin: one ordered list of every account (subscription + API), usage in dollars, terminal column, banner widget, floating overlay
before.detail: New console plugin. 1) ACCOUNTS LIST: reads every Claude account stored on the VPS and lists each: name/label, email, plan, subscription or API, active builder / active worker / not, out of credits, order number, usage used / total, percent left, plan size; usage converted to dollars everywhere usage is shown. 2) ONE ORDER: drag and drop to set the order; subscriptions and API keys are equal to the orchestrator, it follows the order. Right-click any account anywhere: rename, reorder, open a Claude Code session in the terminal. 4) TERMINAL COLUMN: plugin adds a collapsible column (hamburger button) to the Terminal listing all VPS Claude accounts with the same management. Uninstalling the plugin removes the column. 5) BANNER WIDGET: drop-down to pick an account; settings choose what it shows (name, number, usage left, API/subscription, email, any combination). 6) FLOATING OVERLAY WINDOW (not a toolbar): small narrow professional window with customizable buttons; editable behavior and sub-menus in plugin settings; resizable, size lock, dockable where the console allows, minimize to main screen, overlay scope (whole OS vs just the console/browser), styleable like any asset. 7) Full API control for everything.

origin.said: I need a settings on the approval page to allow all for the next hour or two hours or a custom field that I can enter, or deny all for a custom field. Until a certain time or amount of time. And where's the switch? A setting to control the time of the 90 seconds.

steps.text: Design the approval policy schema and migration: a 'window' record (mode allow|deny, starts_at, ends_at, created_by, source ui|rest|mcp|cli|voice, cancelled_at) and a 'veto_countdown_sec' setting (default 90, bounds 10–3600). Only one active window at a time; a new window replaces the old one. Write the migration so existing installs keep 90 s and have no window. Document the contract in the approvals schema doc.
steps.why: Schema + migration design for persisted approval policy shared by server, MCP, CLI and voice

steps.text: Engine: before an approval is queued, check the active window. In an allow window, auto-approve it; in a deny window, auto-deny it. Log every auto-decision with the window id. Expire windows lazily on read and with a timer so expiry clears without a restart. Replace the hard-coded 90 s veto countdown with the veto_countdown_sec setting, read when each countdown starts.

Policy service: setWindow({mode, duration|until}), cancelWindow(), getPolicy() returning the active window with remaining time, and get/set veto_countdown_sec. Validate inputs: until must be in the future, duration must be within 24 h unless forced, countdown must be within bounds. Emit change events so the UI and phone notifications update live.

REST routes: GET /api/approvals/policy, POST /api/approvals/policy/window ({mode:'allow'|'deny', minutes | until}), DELETE /api/approvals/policy/window, GET/PUT /api/approvals/policy/veto-countdown. Use the existing console auth and audit logging.

Approval page UI, settings section: 'Allow all for' with 1 h and 2 h presets, a custom duration field and an until-time picker; 'Deny all for' with a custom duration and an until-time picker; a 'Veto countdown' number field (seconds, defaults to 90) with a save button. Use the plugin framework components and call the REST routes from the previous step.

Approval page UI, active-window banner: show the mode (allow or deny), a live countdown to the end time and the end time itself, plus a 'Cancel now' button. Show the same badge in the axHub header while a window is active. Update live from the policy change events.

API part for the UI (deep links and state): register console_show / console_open targets approvals/settings, approvals/settings#window and approvals/settings#veto-countdown. Expose the policy state through console state read. Add MCP console actions approvals.policy.get, approvals.window.set, approvals.window.cancel, approvals.vetoCountdown.get and approvals.vetoCountdown.set, all backed by the same policy service.

CLI and voice: add `axf approvals allow --for 2h|--until 18:30`, `axf approvals deny --for 30m|--until …`, `axf approvals window cancel`, `axf approvals status` and `axf approvals veto-countdown [<sec>]`. Add AmberX voice intents with the same meanings, for example 'allow all approvals for two hours', 'deny all until 6 pm', 'cancel the approval window', 'set veto countdown to 60 seconds' and 'what's the approval window', each confirmed by voice. Both go through the REST API.

Tests: policy service (set, replace, expire and cancel a window; validation), engine auto-approve/deny inside a window and normal flow outside it, configurable countdown, REST routes, MCP actions, CLI parsing of durations and until times, and the voice intent parse. Add a UI test for the settings form and the banner cancel button.

Final: run the full test suite. Write the report _claude/builds/reports/approval-page-allow-all-deny-all-for-a-set-time.md, including an API table showing how each feature is reached through the deep link, state read, REST, MCP, CLI and voice. origin.said: I don't want to archive. I want to move to another, you know how we set it up from multiple projects. Each one has its own builds, its own notes, all that. Make a new project, remove those from this project and move them to the new project.

steps.text: Design the project contract. Write the project manifest schema covering id, name, created, and the builds, notes and data roots. Define move-build semantics: a build's store entry, journal lines, notes, steps, branches, PR links, reports, shipped records and change entries all move together and keep their ids. Specify the order of operations so a move is atomic (write the target with tmp files, then remove from the source, roll back on failure) and how id collisions are handled. Confirm that a project switch already switches all build data, and write the contract to a doc.
steps.why: Cross-project data contract and schema design that every later step and app depends on

steps.text: Build the createProject core library. Validate the manifest against the schema, scaffold the project's own builds, notes and data folders, register it in the projects registry and the /projects hub sync, and refuse duplicate ids. It is a pure function with no AI. Add unit tests.

Build the moveBuilds core library, following the contract from step 1. Move the selected builds between projects: store entries, journal entries, notes, steps, reports, shipped records and change-entry refs. Git branches and PRs are left untouched, but their references are kept. Writes are atomic with rollback, and a dry-run returns the planned list. Nothing is deleted or archived; the source only loses the moved entries. Add unit tests, including a failure halfway through a move.

Add REST routes for the console API. POST /api/projects creates a project. GET /api/projects and GET /api/projects/:id read state. POST /api/projects/:id/move-builds takes {buildIds|filter:{state,createdBefore}, dryRun} and moves builds. GET /api/projects/:id/builds lists a project's builds. Add route tests.

Expose the same actions through the other three channels, all calling the same library functions with the same arguments. MCP: console actions project.create, project.list, project.get and project.moveBuilds. CLI: axf project create|list|show|move-builds with --dry-run, --state and --created-before. Voice: AmberX intents for 'create project X' and 'move builds to project X'.

Add the UI. A New project dialog in the project picker. In the Build manager, multi-select with a 'Move to project…' action that shows a dry-run preview and asks for confirmation. Add the deep links console_show/console_open targets projects/new, projects/<id> and builds/move?ids=…, register them, and make dialog state readable through the API from step 4.

Run end-to-end tests of create and move on a scratch fixture through REST, MCP and CLI. Check that the results match across channels, that history and notes are intact after a move, that switching to the target project shows the moved builds, and that the source no longer lists them.

Do a dry run against the real data. Using the API, list every build in the current project (amberx-axf) whose state is Pending and that was created before 2026-11-08T00:00. Save the list with ids, titles, created dates and branches. Confirm that builds from 2026-11-08 onward are excluded.

Do the real move. Create the new project through the API (id amberx-axf-backlog unless one is already defined, and record the chosen name). Move the dry-run list into it. Verify the counts before and after, check that every moved build's notes, steps, journal and branch refs are present in the target, and confirm nothing was deleted or archived. Commit the data changes.

Finish the build. Run the full test suite. Write the report to _claude/builds/reports/projects-create-a-new-project-and-move-builds-be.md, including the moved-builds list and how each feature is reached by deep link, REST, MCP, CLI and voice. Add the THREADS row. Open the PR, with the API access paths listed in its description.

before.detail: In the AmberX Android app the rendered page sits too high: the top banner/row is hidden behind the phone's status bar (call notifications) and the camera cutout. Fix edge-to-edge handling: apply system bar and display-cutout insets (WindowInsets / safe-area-inset-top for the web view), so the top row is fully visible. Test on the paired phone, portrait and landscape.

origin.said: Fix the top bar of the AmberX app because it's behind my top banner where my call notifications are. It renders the web page too high up for the screen. The top row is hidden. The banner's behind stuff like my camera.

steps.text: Locate the AmberX Android WebView host (activity/fragment, theme, manifest) and the web shell's top-banner CSS; note current edge-to-edge setup (enableEdgeToEdge / setDecorFitsSystemWindows, windowLayoutInDisplayCutoutMode, viewport meta) and record findings in the build notes.

Native fix: in the WebView host, apply ViewCompat.setOnApplyWindowInsetsListener combining WindowInsetsCompat.Type.systemBars() | displayCutout(); pad the WebView container top/left/right/bottom by those insets (portrait and landscape), set layoutInDisplayCutoutMode to shortEdges, and keep status bar icons readable over the banner colour.

Web side: add viewport-fit=cover to the viewport meta and make the top banner/row use padding-top: env(safe-area-inset-top) (plus left/right for landscape cutouts), with a JS bridge fallback that sets --sat/--sal/--sar/--sab CSS variables from the native insets for WebView versions where env() reports 0; ensure no double padding with the native fix.

API part: expose the applied insets and edge-to-edge mode as readable state (top/left/right/bottom px, cutout present, orientation) via the console API REST route, an MCP console action, the CLI (`axf amberx insets`) and an AmberX voice query, all returning the same payload; reuse the existing console_show/console_open deep link for the AmberX app view. No new settings or actions are added (layout fix only).

Build the debug APK, install on the paired phone via adb, verify portrait and landscape (with an active call notification) that the top row is fully visible and not under the status bar or camera cutout; capture adb screenshots plus the insets state read output as evidence.

Run the full test suites, write the report (_claude/builds/reports/amberx-android-web-view-top-banner-hidden-behind.md) with before/after screenshots and how the insets state is reached via deep link, REST, MCP, CLI and voice, add the THREADS row, and open the PR stating the same API reach.

before.title: Plugin UI inventory + per-plugin reskin: one button lists every element, behavior and token; rebuild just that plugin's look
before.detail: New plugin. 1) A button in every plugin's settings: generates a full inventory of that plugin's UI: every dialog, table, button, pane, window, tab and other element, every behavior, and every layout, style and colour token. 2) Views: grid with expandable rows, classic tree, 3D, IDE-style tab groups; selectable roots; groups of elements. 3) Reskin / rebuild just that plugin: regenerate its look, layout and behavior as a skin scoped to the one plugin (same code underneath, not rewritten from scratch), to look better, perform better, or be new. Preview before apply, one-click revert. Full API/CLI control; AI only behind its switch.

notes.text: Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.
Split by Claude into 15 steps (3 Fable).
Moved to the Archive from pending (console).

origin.said: A button in every plugin's settings. Generates a list of all the UI's dialogs, tables, buttons, panes, windows, tabs, everything, every behavior, every layout, style and color token. Multiple views, 3D, grid, expandable rows, classical trees, different roots, IDE style tabs. Rebuild, it will reskin just that plugin instead of the whole room. New look, layout and behavior, to look better, perform better, or be new.

steps.text: Design the inventory contract: a versioned JSON schema for one plugin's UI inventory (elements with kind dialog/table/button/pane/window/tab/other, parent/child ids, behaviors as event→action entries, layout/style/colour tokens with source and resolved value, groups and roots), plus the skin contract (a per-plugin skin manifest of token overrides, layout overrides and behavior toggles, keyed by plugin id and versioned so revert is exact). Write the schema files and a short contract doc.
steps.why: Cross-port contract every plugin's UI must satisfy, used by inventory, views and skins

steps.text: Framework skin scoping: add a plugin-scoped skin layer to the framework so a skin applies only inside one plugin's mount root (scoped CSS custom properties and layout overrides under the plugin's container, behavior toggles through the existing component props), with load order room theme → plugin skin and a no-op when no skin is set. Same component code underneath.
steps.why: Changes how GUIs render across all apps: a new framework layer between room theme and plugin

steps.text: Framework inventory hooks: expose a read-only introspection walk over a mounted plugin (component tree, registered dialogs/windows/tabs, bound event handlers, resolved tokens) that returns data matching the inventory schema, without changing plugin code.
steps.why: Kernel/engine internals: framework-level introspection of every plugin's component tree

steps.text: Scaffold the new ui-inventory plugin: manifest, server entry, store for inventories and skins (per plugin, with history for revert), settings (AI switch off by default), and register it with the plugin installer.

Inventory generator: build the full inventory for one plugin from the framework walk plus a static pass over the plugin's source and styles (catches dialogs and tabs not currently mounted), merge, validate against the schema and save with a timestamp.

Add the 'UI inventory' button to every plugin's settings through the shared settings frame (one injection point, not per-plugin edits); clicking it generates the inventory and opens the viewer on that plugin. API part in the same step: REST POST /api/ui-inventory/:plugin/generate and GET /api/ui-inventory/:plugin, MCP console actions ui_inventory.generate / ui_inventory.get, CLI `axf ui-inventory generate|show <plugin>`, voice intent 'list the UI of <plugin>', deep link console_open target ui-inventory?plugin=<id>.

Viewer shell with IDE-style tab groups (split, drag tabs between groups, each tab is one view on one root) and the root/group picker: choose any element as root, define and save named groups of elements.
Grid view with expandable rows (element, kind, behaviors, tokens; filter, sort, search) and classic tree view, both rooted at the selected root or group.
3D view: elements as nested layered boxes by containment depth, orbit/zoom, click to select and sync selection with the other views; falls back to tree when WebGL is missing.

API for the viewer: deep links for plugin, view, root, group and tab layout; state read (open tabs, views, root, selection, groups); actions open_view, set_root, select, create/rename/delete group, move tab, export inventory (JSON/CSV). REST + MCP + CLI + voice, all four the same.

Reskin generator without AI: from the inventory, produce a skin for the one plugin by goal (look better: spacing/contrast/type scale fixes; perform better: drop heavy effects, virtualise long tables, lazy tabs; new: preset palettes and layouts), editable token/layout/behavior overrides, validated against the skin schema.

AI reskin behind the plugin's AI switch: when on, send the inventory and goal to the configured model to propose a skin; output goes through the same validator; when off, the option is hidden and the API returns a clear 'AI is off' error.
Reskin UI: 'Rebuild this plugin' panel with goal picker, override editor, side-by-side live preview (skin applied only inside a preview mount of the plugin), Apply, one-click Revert and skin history.

API for reskin: deep link to the reskin panel for a plugin; state read (active skin, preview skin, history); actions generate, preview, apply, revert, revert_to <version>, set override, AI switch setting. REST + MCP + CLI + voice, all four the same.

Tests, report, THREADS row and PR: unit tests for schema validation, introspection walk, static scan, skin scoping (no leak outside the plugin root), apply/revert round trip and API parity across REST/MCP/CLI/voice; write _claude/builds/reports/plugin-ui-inventory-per-plugin-reskin-one-button.md; add the THREADS row; open the PR stating how each UI is reached (deep link, state, actions, settings via REST, MCP, CLI and voice).

before.title: Shared screenshot registry hooked everywhere + live edit from a screenshot + new per-screen skin asset type
before.detail: 1) Shared screenshot registry reachable from anywhere by hook (not only UI Review): Shipped Features entries, Plan Studio plans, orchestrator builds (Build Manager is being retired), errors, any mention of a build/feature/error links its screenshots. 2) Opening a screenshot of an element: side pane with every token/style/parameter for that screen; tweak live with a hot-rendered live preview of the same screen; Save. 3) New asset type: screen skin (colour, style, layout, behavior, icon themes etc.) applied to one particular UI screen only. Full API/CLI control.

origin.said: Screenshots go into a shared registry that can be accessed from anywhere. Plan Studio, features, builds, errors tie into it through a hook, not directly through UI review. View the screenshot of an element, open a pane with all the tokens, styles, parameters, tweak it live with a hot rendering preview of the same screen, save it. That creates a new asset type with the color, style, layout, behavior, icon themes that applies to just a particular UI screen.

steps.text: Design the shared screenshot registry: record schema (id, screen id, element selector, app, captured_at, file path, links[] of {kind: build|feature|plan|error, ref}), storage layout, and a migration that imports existing UI Review screenshots into it without losing their current links.
steps.why: Schema and migration design for a store shared across apps

steps.text: Define the screenshot hook contract (screenshots.attach / screenshots.forRef / screenshots.onCapture) that any plugin calls to link or list screenshots by ref, with a typed event payload. UI Review becomes one caller of the hook, not its owner.
steps.why: Cross-port contract every app and plugin builds against

steps.text: Design the screen skin asset type: schema (target screen id, colour tokens, style overrides, layout params, behavior flags, icon theme), versioning, and the migration that registers it beside the existing asset types.
steps.why: New asset schema and migration in the shared asset store

steps.text: Theming engine: resolve the token stack as global theme → app theme → screen skin for the active screen id only, plus a hot-apply path that pushes a draft skin into a render without saving it.
steps.why: Engine internals that change how GUIs are themed across apps

steps.text: Implement the screenshot registry store and REST routes (list, get, by ref, attach, detach, delete), using the step 1 schema, and run the UI Review migration.
Hook callers: Shipped Features entries, Plan Studio plans, orchestrator builds, and the errors log call screenshots.attach and forRef. Remove any Build Manager-only paths.
Mention linker: anywhere a build, feature or error id is rendered (shared ref chip component), show a screenshot count and thumbnail strip from the registry.

Registry API parity: console_show/console_open target 'screenshots' and 'screenshot/<id>' deep links, state read, MCP tools (screenshots_list/get/attach/detach), CLI 'axf screenshots …', and AmberX voice intents.
Screen skin asset store and REST routes (create, get, list by screen, update, delete, apply, unapply) on top of the step 3 schema.

Screenshot viewer side pane: when you open a screenshot of an element, list every token, style and parameter for that screen, grouped as colour, style, layout, behavior and icons, with editable fields.
Live preview: render the same screen in an iframe or sandbox, hot-apply pane edits through theme hot-apply, then Save to create or update the screen skin asset, with Revert and Discard.

Skin editor and screen skin API parity: deep links (console_open 'screenshot/<id>/edit', 'asset/screen-skin/<id>'), state read of the draft and saved skin, actions and settings (set token, preview, save, revert, apply, unapply) via REST, MCP console actions and plugin commands, CLI 'axf skins …', and voice.
Docs: registry hook usage for plugin authors, screen skin asset type, and the API reach table (deep link, state, actions, settings across REST, MCP, CLI and voice).

Tests (registry store, migration, hook callers, skin resolve order, hot-apply, REST/MCP/CLI parity), report at _claude/builds/reports/shared-screenshot-registry-hooked-everywhere-liv.md, THREADS row, and PR stating how each UI is reached through deep link, REST, MCP, CLI and voice.

before.detail: Amends per-plugin appearance saves and skins-as-packages. 1) A save captures the plugin's full state: behavior, style, layout, colour, icons and any code-level overrides, not just the changed category. 2) A skin is only a manifest of asset names per section. 3) Skins must apply consistently to every plugin screen even though plugins use different asset names than the host app: add a shared asset naming contract + alias map (plugin asset -> canonical role, e.g. toolbar, panel, primary button) so one skin resolves the same look across apps and plugins. CI check flags plugin assets with no canonical role. Rebuild existing skins to the contract.

before.title: Skin rule: overrides are local only; global changes only by applying a whole skin
before.detail: Amends the skins naming-contract build. Precedence: axHub base < skin (by canonical role) < per-screen skin < per-element override. An override changes only that element. Global changes are made ONLY by applying a whole skin; editing a button inside one plugin or app never propagates to other plugins/apps. Enforce in the inline editor (no 'apply everywhere' outside the skin editor) and document in CLAUDE.md rules.

before.title: Dispatcher: a worktree store write can erase a fresh launch record (double launch, then a stuck build)
before.detail: Seen on pass-approval-hook-deep-link-amberx-notification, Nov 10 2026 (journal _claude/builds/journal/2026-11-p4.jsonl): 18:11:16 pipeline:launch wrote status running + pipeline.session earl; 18:11:19 the worktree's orchestrator:note ('Claude account: ...', written by claude-headless.sh at start from a store copy taken before the launch) landed with status queued and no pipeline record, and the per-build newer-wins merge kept it; 18:12:11 the next tick launched the same build again (gina), both runs numbered 1. Earl's 's1 done' tick at 18:24:48 erased the second record the same way, so the live build sat in 'running' with no session: checkEnds and reapBuilds both skip a build without pipeline.session / pipeline.account, so the phase end was never handled (set to queued by hand). Fix, in this order: (1) builds-merge-core: merge the pipeline record per field, never let an incoming copy with no pipeline record replace a newer launch record on main (or have orchestrator.mjs act pull main's record before a note/tick write); (2) pipeline-core plan(): never launch a build whose status is running/waiting or that has a running or queued agent slot for its id (agent-slots status lists build per slot); (3) checkEnds/reapBuilds: a build 'running' with no pipeline record and no live slot for it ends by the phase rule (exit 0 + model switch -> queued) instead of being skipped forever; (4) claude-headless.sh: write the 'Claude account' note only after the launch record is published, or through the per-field merge. Add a check in framework/spec/check-builds-live.mjs that replays this journal sequence.

(1) The console API refuses cross-origin calls from Molly: OPTIONS https://console.amberxai.com/api/me with Origin https://molly.amberxai.com answers 401 with no CORS headers (the token check runs before FastAPI's CORSMiddleware, and allow_origins * cannot be used by the wall). Let preflights through and answer an allow-list of amberxai.com app origins with Access-Control-Allow-Headers authorization, content-type, accept. (2) The console token lives only in the console origin's storage (axf-console:token); Molly keeps its own copy (molly:console-token) that today a person must paste. Molly side is in place: apps/molly/src/molly/credentials.ts (console provider, bearer, credentials omit).

- `claude/amberx-open-url`
- `go-pass`

Rules:
- Push only to `claude/claude-sync-hold`. Never push to `main` or any other branch, never force-push, never merge the PR.
- Never print, copy or commit secrets (tokens, keys, .env files, .axf-console/).

- Record steps and the result on your change-log entry (the hooks do most of it).

# Build: pipeline-rebuild (orchestrator build ID: urgent-rebuild-pipeline-orchestrator-ids-splits-)

## Brett said (verbatim)
You need to start the pipeline over from scratch. From now on, what I say, send a build to the orchestrator. The orchestrator is going to assign an ID. A build ID. He's going to use you to break it up into steps select a model Babel or Opus Babel when it's needed and then he's going to see how many subscriptions are connected to the VPS how many accounts are available How many, what's the max parallel for each one? And uh, if it's a account that has Fable, he'll send the Fable to that. He'll send everything else to Opus. He will, no, he will check the BPS to see what accounts have what slots. Available parallel. Dish out the steps, okay? The steps are marked. We already have the rules for how the steps are marked down into a, in a progress pile and blah blah blah. Updated in real time because you have a monitor watching the progress files. And um, the orchestrator starts starts the head, headless. The orchestrator then sends it to the queue, or he sends it to pending. Yeah, he sends everything to the pending. And I have to send them from pending to queue.

## Addendum (Brett, voice)
The orchestrator doesn't start a headless session right away. If he has slots open, he grabs the next build in the queue and starts the headless session.

## Context found tonight
- The orchestrator (apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator) has NO launch code: nothing in it starts headless sessions. Only deploy/claude-headless.sh enqueues into agent-slots (framework/cli/agent-slots.mjs).
- Pending items are never auto-imported into the orchestrator; 'import' (orchestrator-core.mjs) only copies existing subPrompts, nothing splits.
- HARD RULE in force: no build starts without an orchestrator build ID (launcher enforces it).
- 'Launch builds without asking' (claude-settings) defaults off.
- Profiles were merged into 'all' on Nov 7; queue flagged needsReprocess.

## Do
1. Intake: every new pending item is auto-imported into the orchestrator with a build ID.
2. Split: the orchestrator calls Claude to split into <=30 min steps and pick Fable only where needed, Opus otherwise; write steps to the build.
3. Flow: builds sit in Pending until Brett moves them to Queue (no auto-queue).
4. Dispatcher: a loop in the orchestrator reads VPS accounts (deploy/claude-workers.mjs status, claude-login.mjs accounts): which have Fable, max parallel, free slots. When a slot is free it takes the next Queue build and starts a headless session through the existing launcher (claude-headless.sh / agent-slots), Fable steps to a Fable account, rest to Opus.
5. Progress: steps tick in the progress files per existing rules; the live monitor updates the console in real time.
6. Idle alert: AmberX phone notification when nothing is running while the Queue has work.
7. Tests, report _claude/builds/reports/pipeline-rebuild.md, THREADS, PR, steps through the store. Commits clean and professional.
## Addendum 2 (Brett, voice)
When the orchestrator splits a build and sends it to Pending, it also creates a plan in Plan Studio: a note describing the job, with a checklist of the steps, and a sub-note inside it holding Brett's prompt verbatim, with the part this build covers highlighted in a colour set in settings. Sessions are never stopped and rerun per step (saves tokens): instead, the last action of every step is to update the progress file. The orchestrator's listener watches the progress files and, on each change, ticks that step off and crosses it out in the Plan Studio checklist.

## Addendum 3 (Brett, voice)
The orchestrator writes each headless session's brief itself, with the least information possible: only the current step(s), the files it touches, and the rules it needs. No history, no full spec.

steps.text: Contract: add the `queued` status to builds@1 / orchestrator@1 / build-hook@1 (Pending → Queued → Building = running), a `pipeline` record on every build (account, session, runs, split, last run) kept across orchestrator writes, pending@1 shows queued as pending, derivedStatus keeps queued; fixtures and check-builds-store updated

pipeline-core.mjs (pure): account capabilities (which account has Fable, max parallel each, limits), the queue order, pick the account for a queued build's next phase, slot-open launch decision, session-end outcome (requeue / back to Pending / failed), idle reasons, the split prompt + step parser (≤30 min, Fable only where needed) and a rules-based fallback split

pipeline.mjs CLI (IO): status | queue | unqueue | split | intake | accounts | tick; store writes under the lock (queue/unqueue/pipeline record/steps from the split); splitter providers (claude -p on a login copy, AXF_PIPELINE_SPLITTER for tests, rules fallback); intake splits every new build with no steps

Dispatcher tick: read VPS accounts + agent slots, when a slot is free take the next Queue build, make its worktree + brief (Brett said block + phase brief), launch deploy/claude-headless.sh --account on a Fable account for Fable phases / Opus otherwise, mark running + account + session; monitor events.jsonl + slots for session end → built / requeue / Pending / failed, relaunch cap; dispatcher state file for the console; cron line in deploy/install-console.sh

Idle alert + notifications: notify.json types (pipeline.idle, pipeline.launched, pipeline.ended, pipeline.failed) raised through the console alerts API from the host (AmberX push for idle: nothing running while the Queue has work, with the reason), keyed and resolved when a build runs

Console: Pipeline tab on the Build orchestrator page (Pending / Queue / Building columns, accounts strip with Fable + parallel + running, dispatcher status, Queue / Back to Pending / Split now, live refresh while visible); server routes GET /pipeline, POST /pipeline/queue | unqueue | split; plugin commands for voice/MCP (queue a build, pipeline status); help entries; Launch builds without asking ON = new builds queue by themselves

Tests: check-pipeline.mjs end to end on a scratch store with a fake launcher, fake splitter and fake accounts (intake → Pending → Queue → launch on the right account → session end → built / requeue / failed, idle alert once, slot cap respected); python route test; CI wiring; plugin-lifecycle check; existing suites green

Close out: report _claude/builds/reports/pipeline-rebuild.md, _claude/builds/README.md Pipeline section, rules + decisions lines, THREADS row, fold the overlapping builds (idle-alert-phone-flag-when-nothing-is-building, orchestrator-start-a-build-through-the-api-mcp-and-cli) as complete with this PR, commit, push, PR, link the build

# Orchestrator self-check when stuck: verify each account one by one, clear stale jobs

Launched directly by Brett's request (voice) because the dispatcher is stuck. Orchestrator build record id (filed separately, will be marked built after): `orchestrator-self-check-when-stuck-verify-each-a`.

## Problem
The build pipeline (build-orchestrator plugin, pipeline-status) shows every queued build waiting with "no Claude account is signed in on the VPS" and an empty accounts list, while claude-accounts/list shows mossesx-max- (Max) active and signed in, account-3 (Hulu) saved, and API workers mossesx-api and account-5. The dispatcher's account view is out of sync with claude-workers / claude-login.

## Do

# Shipped Features: orchestrator manifest + API (urgent)

Brett's words: "Isn't it part of the pipeline?" ... "You put an API on it?" ... "The orchestrator should send a manifest with the information on the shipped feature. Including the prompt that created it and everything."

## Context
- Shipped Features (feature-ledger@1) only updates through the build-hook@1 events fired by builds-store writes (framework/cli/builds-store.mjs). Builds launched straight through vps.build_start tonight had no builds-store record, so nothing reached the ledger.
- `orchestrator-only-launcher` just landed on main (e15e5287681b): the orchestrator is now the only launcher (pipeline.mjs, afterTick hook). Build on that.

## Do
1. Manifest: when a build lands (or a step completes and ships), the orchestrator writes a shipped-feature manifest and sends it to the Shipped Features ledger. It holds: build id and title, Brett's verbatim prompt (the `said` field / brief origin) plus the full brief, model(s) and account(s) used, steps with estimates and actual times, branch, PR, landed commit, files/areas changed, tests run and results, UI Review item, cost and tokens, report path, and what's still open. Schema versioned (shipped-manifest@1), validated.
2. The ledger shows the manifest on each entry (prompt highlighted, collapsible sections).
3. API: Shipped Features gets full API control: list/read/search entries, add/update an entry from a manifest, link to build/PR; via MCP (axf-console tools), axHub, CLI, deep link and voice. Writes go through the builds-store so hooks stay consistent.
4. Backfill: create entries now for builds landed tonight that missed the ledger: `orchestrator-only-launcher` (e15e5287681b) and `urgent-amberx-veto-notice-alarm-too-loud-approve` (commits 864ab0549, 44862718a), using their briefs and reports in _claude/builds/reports/. Add a CLI `shipped backfill --since <date>` that finds landed builds with no ledger entry.
5. Tests for manifest schema, ledger write, API and backfill; console typecheck green. Short report, commit, stop so it can be landed with build_land.

before.title: Asset Designer plugin (no-code)
before.detail: No-code editors for nav menus, drawers, app menus, context menus, toolbars, layouts, style packs and color themes. Every asset validates against its schema before save. Adds a drawer asset type. Installed by default.

notes.text: Superseded in part by build ui-asset-designer (Current, Nov 7 2026, Fable): the menu editor (s5), toolbar editor (s6) and the generic designer shell / storage / validation gate are built from scratch there (designer@1 host + add-ons, framework/spec/DESIGNER.md). What stays here: the drawer asset type (s7, s8), layout editor (s9), colour-theme editor (s10), style-theme editor (s11); build them on the designer@1 host when picked up.
Merged from build profile "main-framework" into "all" (one profile for everything).

Audit: superseded — ui-asset-designer (built Nov 7: designer host plugin + add-ons for app menu, nav menu, toolbar, banner, embed, widgets) and context-menu-designer (complete Oct 25) cover it; the drawer type is in framework/schemas/asset-types.json
Shipped manifest sm-asset-designer rev 1 sent to Shipped features (backfill): complete 2026-11-10 (date inferred: no commit or PR recorded), 0 file(s), 0 test line(s), 16 open.

steps.text: Plugin skeleton: copy `apps/console-web/plugins/_template` to `plugins/asset-designer` (id `ai.amberx.axf.console.asset-designer`, `uiEditor: "builder"`, lifecycle block, `install.mjs`/`uninstall.mjs`), nav → Plugins → Asset designer, Settings → Plugins sub-tab (parent `plugins`). `node framework/cli/plugin-lifecycle.mjs check asset-designer` passes; console tsc + vite build pass.

Designer shell `web/Designer.tsx`: type picker (every non-attachable type from `asset-types.json` the designer covers: nav-menu, drawer, app-menu, context-menu, toolbar, layout, style-theme, color-theme), id + label fields, Save/Cancel; `useEditorSync()` so it reloads values on focus (UI-editor rule). Saves nothing yet.

Validation gate: every save runs `validateAsset` from the baked `src/axf/core/validate.ts`; errors shown inline next to the field they name; Save disabled until clean. Server route `POST /api/plugins/asset-designer/validate` mirrors it with the CLI validator (`framework/core/project-check.mjs` pattern). Test in `test.py`.

Storage: designed assets saved as asset@1 files under `.axf-console/plugins/asset-designer/assets/<type>/<id>.json` (lifecycle dataDir), served by `GET /api/plugins/asset-designer/assets`, registered into the runtime on load like the theme-manager plugin does (`registry.register`, origin `asset-designer`). Built-in ids refused.

Menu editor (nav-menu, app-menu, context-menu): tree of items (label, icon, action, children, divider), drag to reorder, action picker from `rt.actions.list()`, live preview via `rt.swap` on a `ad-preview-<type>` id. Reuses `MenuList.tsx` for the preview.

Toolbar editor: items (icon, label, action, badge counter), `density`/`surface`/`divider`/`collapsible`, widgets start/end picker from `attachable` types (engine-rpc `app-defaults` → `widgets`), live preview through the React `Toolbar`.

`drawer` asset type: add it to `asset-types.json` (hideable chrome, `side` left/right, `width`, `items` like nav-menu, `modal`), `layout.slots` accept it in the `drawer` region, starter `framework/assets/drawer/amberx-side.json`, `framework/defaults.json` names it. Validators on all three ports accept it (Kotlin: `AssetTypeSpec` resource); fixture case in `layout-slots.json`.

Drawer rendering: React `components/Chrome.tsx` draws the drawer region; Compose `axf-ui/components/Chrome.kt` the same (swipe from the edge, scrim from `--fx-opacity-scrim`). Drawer editor in the designer (same editor as nav-menu plus side/width/modal).

Layout editor: region grid (9 regions from `layout.slots`), per-region size/visibility, `data.slots` overrides with accepted-type chips; preview through `compileLayout`. Hidden slots greyed like Appearance does.

Color-theme editor: token groups from the theme engine (`core/engines/theme.ts` token list), colour pickers, contrast warnings (reuse `theme-manager/web/rollEngine.ts` checks), light/dark pair, preview via `rt.swap`.
Style-theme editor: space, radii, borders, font sizes, opacity tokens (`opacityDisabled/Muted/Hover/Tint/Scrim/Glass`), density; preview; numbers clamped to the ranges known themes use.

Templates hook: "Start from" picker listing starters + designed assets + (later) `x.assets.templates` entries; Duplicate / Rename / Export JSON / Import JSON (validated). Export writes a file a user can drop into an app's assets folder.

Installed by default: plugin `enabled: true` in the console's plugin defaults, `framework/catalog/plugins.json` entry (planned → built resolves by itself), `node framework/cli/plugins.mjs --check`, status.json + tracker; Plugin Manager shows it.

Android face (first slice): `axf-devtools` gets an `AssetDesignerModule` placeholder route `asset-designer` listing designed assets received from the console (read-only), so the plugin-inventory shows it on both ports; full editors stay web-only for now (noted as a placeholder capability `axf.designer`).

Tests: plugin `test.py` (validate route, storage, built-in id refused, lifecycle), web unit cases for the drawer slot + layout compile, CI line; `uninstall.mjs --all` leaves nothing (`check --after-uninstall`).

Close: differences report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/asset-designer.md` (new plugin, so a build report), LOG.md line, web screenshots via `rebuild-shots.mjs`, CLAUDE.md Status, plan epic `x.assets.designer` built via `build_step`, pending item complete.

before.title: Running builds follow the active Claude account, fail over when it dies
before.detail:
## Brett said (verbatim)
Source: voice · At: 2026-11-06
> the running builds need to run on whatever account's connected. If, if the account dies, they need to switch over.
> Every time you log in with a refresh token, you need to update the refresh token.
> why doesn't it switch over? It needs to switch over on its own.

Context: claude_accounts_use to account-2 succeeded and marked it active, but the live VPS login stayed gizmox1111 (loginChanged: true) and the banner clock badge stayed gray. Reverses part of build-own-login (#357). Related: ai-keys-console-store (#358), console-account-picker. Check overlap first.

notes.text: The 'Save the rotated refresh token' steps are built by first-refresh-token-saved-every-time-it-s-used-v (PR #359): tick them once it merges, don't rebuild them.
The 'Save the rotated refresh token' steps are built by first-refresh-token-saved-every-time-it-s-used-v (PR #359): tick them once it merges, don't rebuild them.

before.detail: New standalone console plugin 'Demonstration Designer' (own nav entry), replacing the disabled glossary-index one. Brett found the old one unusable, so make it simple and obvious. Pick any screen, plugin or UI element from the live registry, then build a demo: steps (open screen, highlight, click/type action, wait), narration text + voice, captions, timing. Record a demo by doing it, edit it on a timeline, preview, play it live on the console or a sandboxed preview, export as video. Demos are saved assets, reusable and chainable into longer tours. Harvest useful code from the disabled glossary-index plugin (demos.mjs, walkthrough engine) instead of starting from zero. RULE: every UI action and setting has API + voice + MCP/CLI control, and a deep link opens it. Settings in categorized collapsible sections; 3 UI options to UI Review; tests; report.

notes.text: PURPOSE (Brett): it's for PITCHING the product. Keep it dead simple. Main flow = three picks: (1) plugin or topic, (2) length in minutes, (3) narrator voice; then ONE Generate button. Generate writes a pitch script (hook up front, benefits not specs, closing call to action), picks the best screens, and plays a polished demo on real data: highlights, smooth zooms/pans, captions, background music, logo intro/outro. After: optional script tweak, preview, export video (MP4) or share link. Advanced editing (timeline, record-by-doing) stays tucked behind an Advanced section, never in the main flow.
Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.
Queued by cli.

Also a default export path that doesn't need the phone: generate the narration as real audio (a TTS voice) and mix it into the exported MP4. Full API/MCP/CLI/voice control.

before.title: Fix: stale running counts per Claude account not cleared
before.detail: Seen Nov 9: claude_accounts shows Hulu 1/3, Moses X 4/3, account-1 4/3 running while the VPS has 0 tmux axf-* sessions and 0 claude -p processes. Rule (Brett): every time the console loads, and on the watchdog tick, the orchestrator checks for stale runs and releases any slot or running entry with no live process (agent-slots, claude-workers.mjs counts, orchestrator.json statuses). Find why the existing check didn't run or didn't clear these; fix; add a test with fake stale entries; log each release.

notes.text: ROOT CAUSE (found live): deploy/claude-workers.mjs liveSessions() runs `tmux ls`; when NO tmux sessions exist, tmux exits non-zero ('no server running'), so it returns null = 'can't ask tmux'. Then ledger() counts every open session as running and liveClaims keeps claims for 12 h. So the stale entries survive exactly when nothing is running. # Build: pipeline-rebuild (orchestrator build ID: urgent-rebuild-pipeline-orchestrator-ids-splits-)

## Brett said (verbatim)
You need to start the pipeline over from scratch. From now on, what I say, send a build to the orchestrator. The orchestrator is going to assign an ID. A build ID. He's going to use you to break it up into steps select a model Babel or Opus Babel when it's needed and then he's going to see how many subscriptions are connected to the VPS how many accounts are available How many, what's the max parallel for each one? And uh, if it's a account that has Fable, he'll send the Fable to that. He'll send everything else to Opus. He will, no, he will check the BPS to see what accounts have what slots. Available parallel. Dish out the steps, okay? The steps are marked. We already have the rules for how the steps are marked down into a, in a progress pile and blah blah blah. Updated in real time because you have a monitor watching the progress files. And um, the orchestrator starts starts the head, headless. The orchestrator then sends it to the queue, or he sends it to pending. Yeah, he sends everything to the pending. And I have to send them from pending to queue.

## Addendum (Brett, voice)
The orchestrator doesn't start a headless session right away. If he has slots open, he grabs the next build in the queue and starts the headless session.

## Context found tonight
- The orchestrator (apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator) has NO launch code: nothing in it starts headless sessions. Only deploy/claude-headless.sh enqueues into agent-slots (framework/cli/agent-slots.mjs).
- Pending items are never auto-imported into the orchestrator; 'import' (orchestrator-core.mjs) only copies existing subPrompts, nothing splits.
- HARD RULE in force: no build starts without an orchestrator build ID (launcher enforces it).
- 'Launch builds without asking' (claude-settings) defaults off.
- Profiles were merged into 'all' on Nov 7; queue flagged needsReprocess.

## Do
1. Intake: every new pending item is auto-imported into the orchestrator with a build ID.
2. Split: the orchestrator calls Claude to split into <=30 min steps and pick Fable only where needed, Opus otherwise; write steps to the build.
3. Flow: builds sit in Pending until Brett moves them to Queue (no auto-queue).
4. Dispatcher: a loop in the orchestrator reads VPS accounts (deploy/claude-workers.mjs status, claude-login.mjs accounts): which have Fable, max parallel, free slots. When a slot is free it takes the next Queue build and starts a headless session through the existing launcher (claude-headless.sh / agent-slots), Fable steps to a Fable account, rest to Opus.
5. Progress: steps tick in the progress files per existing rules; the live monitor updates the console in real time.
6. Idle alert: AmberX phone notification when nothing is running while the Queue has work.
7. Tests, report _claude/builds/reports/pipeline-rebuild.md, THREADS, PR, steps through the store. Commits clean and professional.
## Addendum 2 (Brett, voice)
When the orchestrator splits a build and sends it to Pending, it also creates a plan in Plan Studio: a note describing the job, with a checklist of the steps, and a sub-note inside it holding Brett's prompt verbatim, with the part this build covers highlighted in a colour set in settings. Sessions are never stopped and rerun per step (saves tokens): instead, the last action of every step is to update the progress file. The orchestrator's listener watches the progress files and, on each change, ticks that step off and crosses it out in the Plan Studio checklist.

## Addendum 3 (Brett, voice)
The orchestrator writes each headless session's brief itself, with the least information possible: only the current step(s), the files it touches, and the rules it needs. No history, no full spec.

steps.text: Contract: add the `queued` status to builds@1 / orchestrator@1 / build-hook@1 (Pending → Queued → Building = running), a `pipeline` record on every build (account, session, runs, split, last run) kept across orchestrator writes, pending@1 shows queued as pending, derivedStatus keeps queued; fixtures and check-builds-store updated

pipeline-core.mjs (pure): account capabilities (which account has Fable, max parallel each, limits), the queue order, pick the account for a queued build's next phase, slot-open launch decision, session-end outcome (requeue / back to Pending / failed), idle reasons, the split prompt + step parser (≤30 min, Fable only where needed) and a rules-based fallback split

pipeline.mjs CLI (IO): status | queue | unqueue | split | intake | accounts | tick; store writes under the lock (queue/unqueue/pipeline record/steps from the split); splitter providers (claude -p on a login copy, AXF_PIPELINE_SPLITTER for tests, rules fallback); intake splits every new build with no steps

Dispatcher tick: read VPS accounts + agent slots, when a slot is free take the next Queue build, make its worktree + brief (Brett said block + phase brief), launch deploy/claude-headless.sh --account on a Fable account for Fable phases / Opus otherwise, mark running + account + session; monitor events.jsonl + slots for session end → built / requeue / Pending / failed, relaunch cap; dispatcher state file for the console; cron line in deploy/install-console.sh

Idle alert + notifications: notify.json types (pipeline.idle, pipeline.launched, pipeline.ended, pipeline.failed) raised through the console alerts API from the host (AmberX push for idle: nothing running while the Queue has work, with the reason), keyed and resolved when a build runs

Console: Pipeline tab on the Build orchestrator page (Pending / Queue / Building columns, accounts strip with Fable + parallel + running, dispatcher status, Queue / Back to Pending / Split now, live refresh while visible); server routes GET /pipeline, POST /pipeline/queue | unqueue | split; plugin commands for voice/MCP (queue a build, pipeline status); help entries; Launch builds without asking ON = new builds queue by themselves

Tests: check-pipeline.mjs end to end on a scratch store with a fake launcher, fake splitter and fake accounts (intake → Pending → Queue → launch on the right account → session end → built / requeue / failed, idle alert once, slot cap respected); python route test; CI wiring; plugin-lifecycle check; existing suites green

Close out: report _claude/builds/reports/pipeline-rebuild.md, _claude/builds/README.md Pipeline section, rules + decisions lines, THREADS row, fold the overlapping builds (idle-alert-phone-flag-when-nothing-is-building, orchestrator-start-a-build-through-the-api-mcp-and-cli) as complete with this PR, commit, push, PR, link the build

Addendum 1: "And the hook will reload axHub, and you can also save design back to axHub." Context: axHub defines the default look for every app; apps inherit it live; manual edits override per setting with an 'Overriding axHub' note (same rule as molly-nav-submenus Addendum 6 and gizmo-companion's appearance add-on). Agent: Ping Paulie (no Polo card). Model: Opus for every step (Claude decides); additive web-only contract, Android twin deferred in PORTING.md; Fable review recommended per the shared rule.

steps.text: s1 axHub = style source: axHub's active color-theme + style-theme is the default for every app (console, Molly, axHub web, AmberX, demo, Gizmo later, framework app template); inheriting apps follow it live

s2 Settings > Appearance in each app: Override axHub design / Override axHub colors switches, Inherited from axHub note with theme name, Overriding axHub with axHub value beside, auto-on when editing, Reset to axHub

before.title: Asset Designer plugin (no-code)
before.detail: No-code editors for nav menus, drawers, app menus, context menus, toolbars, layouts, style packs and color themes. Every asset validates against its schema before save. Adds a drawer asset type. Installed by default.

What stays here: the drawer asset type (s7, s8), layout editor (s9), colour-theme editor (s10), style-theme editor (s11); build them on the designer@1 host when picked up.
Merged from build profile "main-framework" into "all" (one profile for everything).

Audit: superseded — ui-asset-designer (built Nov 7: designer host plugin + add-ons for app menu, nav menu, toolbar, banner, embed, widgets) and context-menu-designer (complete Oct 25) cover it; the drawer type is in framework/schemas/asset-types.json
Shipped manifest sm-asset-designer rev 1 sent to Shipped features (backfill): complete 2026-11-10 (date inferred: no commit or PR recorded), 0 file(s), 0 test line(s), 16 open.

steps.text: Plugin skeleton: copy `apps/console-web/plugins/_template` to `plugins/asset-designer` (id `ai.amberx.axf.console.asset-designer`, `uiEditor: "builder"`, lifecycle block, `install.mjs`/`uninstall.mjs`), nav → Plugins → Asset designer, Settings → Plugins sub-tab (parent `plugins`). `node framework/cli/plugin-lifecycle.mjs check asset-designer` passes; console tsc + vite build pass.

Designer shell `web/Designer.tsx`: type picker (every non-attachable type from `asset-types.json` the designer covers: nav-menu, drawer, app-menu, context-menu, toolbar, layout, style-theme, color-theme), id + label fields, Save/Cancel; `useEditorSync()` so it reloads values on focus (UI-editor rule). Saves nothing yet.

Validation gate: every save runs `validateAsset` from the baked `src/axf/core/validate.ts`; errors shown inline next to the field they name; Save disabled until clean. Server route `POST /api/plugins/asset-designer/validate` mirrors it with the CLI validator (`framework/core/project-check.mjs` pattern). Test in `test.py`.

Storage: designed assets saved as asset@1 files under `.axf-console/plugins/asset-designer/assets/<type>/<id>.json` (lifecycle dataDir), served by `GET /api/plugins/asset-designer/assets`, registered into the runtime on load like the theme-manager plugin does (`registry.register`, origin `asset-designer`). Built-in ids refused.

Menu editor (nav-menu, app-menu, context-menu): tree of items (label, icon, action, children, divider), drag to reorder, action picker from `rt.actions.list()`, live preview via `rt.swap` on a `ad-preview-<type>` id. Reuses `MenuList.tsx` for the preview.

Toolbar editor: items (icon, label, action, badge counter), `density`/`surface`/`divider`/`collapsible`, widgets start/end picker from `attachable` types (engine-rpc `app-defaults` → `widgets`), live preview through the React `Toolbar`.

`drawer` asset type: add it to `asset-types.json` (hideable chrome, `side` left/right, `width`, `items` like nav-menu, `modal`), `layout.slots` accept it in the `drawer` region, starter `framework/assets/drawer/amberx-side.json`, `framework/defaults.json` names it. Validators on all three ports accept it (Kotlin: `AssetTypeSpec` resource); fixture case in `layout-slots.json`.

Drawer rendering: React `components/Chrome.tsx` draws the drawer region; Compose `axf-ui/components/Chrome.kt` the same (swipe from the edge, scrim from `--fx-opacity-scrim`). Drawer editor in the designer (same editor as nav-menu plus side/width/modal).

Layout editor: region grid (9 regions from `layout.slots`), per-region size/visibility, `data.slots` overrides with accepted-type chips; preview through `compileLayout`. Hidden slots greyed like Appearance does.

Color-theme editor: token groups from the theme engine (`core/engines/theme.ts` token list), colour pickers, contrast warnings (reuse `theme-manager/web/rollEngine.ts` checks), light/dark pair, preview via `rt.swap`.
Style-theme editor: space, radii, borders, font sizes, opacity tokens (`opacityDisabled/Muted/Hover/Tint/Scrim/Glass`), density; preview; numbers clamped to the ranges known themes use.

Templates hook: "Start from" picker listing starters + designed assets + (later) `x.assets.templates` entries; Duplicate / Rename / Export JSON / Import JSON (validated). Export writes a file a user can drop into an app's assets folder.

Installed by default: plugin `enabled: true` in the console's plugin defaults, `framework/catalog/plugins.json` entry (planned → built resolves by itself), `node framework/cli/plugins.mjs --check`, status.json + tracker; Plugin Manager shows it.

Android face (first slice): `axf-devtools` gets an `AssetDesignerModule` placeholder route `asset-designer` listing designed assets received from the console (read-only), so the plugin-inventory shows it on both ports; full editors stay web-only for now (noted as a placeholder capability `axf.designer`).

Tests: plugin `test.py` (validate route, storage, built-in id refused, lifecycle), web unit cases for the drawer slot + layout compile, CI line; `uninstall.mjs --all` leaves nothing (`check --after-uninstall`).

Close: differences report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/asset-designer.md` (new plugin, so a build report), LOG.md line, web screenshots via `rebuild-shots.mjs`, CLAUDE.md Status, plan epic `x.assets.designer` built via `build_step`, pending item complete.

# Build: md-chain-control (pending item headless-session-efficiency-shared-chain-control)

Brett: finish the optimization in Claude MD Studio. The token log, rules briefs and headless-skips-CLAUDE.md work is on branch claude/token-optimize (PR open, not merged): merge origin/claude/token-optimize into this branch first and build on it; don't redo any of it.

That item lists every step twice; do each once:
1. Fresh session per step with a short handoff note from the progress file.
2. Per-step model choice suggested by the orchestrator.
3. Steps list the exact files they need; sessions read only those.
4. Trim long tool output (configurable caps).
5. Shared registry (schema + store + read/write API with change events) used by both the Claude plugin and Claude MD Studio.

Shared controls in both plugins: CLAUDE.md chain view in load order with size and tokens; per-file include/exclude and always / on demand / never, reorder, edit, preview; per-build and per-step overrides; session mode, handoff size, model rules; output caps, file scoping, token budget per step with warn/stop; live token cost preview; presets lean/normal/full, reset, history.
7. API, CLI and MCP for the registry.
8. Verify savings with the token log on a test build.

before.detail: New standalone console plugin 'Demonstration Designer' (own nav entry), replacing the disabled glossary-index one. Brett found the old one unusable, so make it simple and obvious. Pick any screen, plugin or UI element from the live registry, then build a demo: steps (open screen, highlight, click/type action, wait), narration text + voice, captions, timing. Record a demo by doing it, edit it on a timeline, preview, play it live on the console or a sandboxed preview, export as video. Demos are saved assets, reusable and chainable into longer tours. Harvest useful code from the disabled glossary-index plugin (demos.mjs, walkthrough engine) instead of starting from zero. RULE: every UI action and setting has API + voice + MCP/CLI control, and a deep link opens it. Settings in categorized collapsible sections; 3 UI options to UI Review; tests; report.

notes.text: PURPOSE (Brett): it's for PITCHING the product. Keep it dead simple. Main flow = three picks: (1) plugin or topic, (2) length in minutes, (3) narrator voice; then ONE Generate button. Generate writes a pitch script (hook up front, benefits not specs, closing call to action), picks the best screens, and plays a polished demo on real data: highlights, smooth zooms/pans, captions, background music, logo intro/outro. After: optional script tweak, preview, export video (MP4) or share link. Advanced editing (timeline, record-by-doing) stays tucked behind an Advanced section, never in the main flow.
Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.
Queued by cli.

Brett: "Why doesn't the exported video have the narrator's voice? AmberX can screen record it." Phase 1 export uses browser speech, which Chrome doesn't route into tab capture, so videos have captions and music but no voice. Fix: add an export option 'Record on AmberX': the demo plays on Brett's phone and AmberX records it with the narration audio (reuse AmberX's Audio Output Recorder, extend it to screen + app audio), then uploads the video back to the demo asset. Also a default export path that doesn't need the phone: generate the narration as real audio (a TTS voice) and mix it into the exported MP4. Full API/MCP/CLI/voice control.

before.title: Fix: stale running counts per Claude account not cleared
before.detail: Seen Nov 9: claude_accounts shows Hulu 1/3, Moses X 4/3, account-1 4/3 running while the VPS has 0 tmux axf-* sessions and 0 claude -p processes. Rule (Brett): every time the console loads, and on the watchdog tick, the orchestrator checks for stale runs and releases any slot or running entry with no live process (agent-slots, claude-workers.mjs counts, orchestrator.json statuses). Find why the existing check didn't run or didn't clear these; fix; add a test with fake stale entries; log each release.

notes.text: ROOT CAUSE (found live): deploy/claude-workers.mjs liveSessions() runs `tmux ls`; when NO tmux sessions exist, tmux exits non-zero ('no server running'), so it returns null = 'can't ask tmux'. Then ledger() counts every open session as running and liveClaims keeps claims for 12 h. So the stale entries survive exactly when nothing is running. Fix: treat 'no server running' (tmux present, exit 1) as an empty Set; only return null when tmux binary is missing. Test it.

Root cause fixed in PR #406 (claude/orch-self-check-stuck): tmux 'no server running' was read as unknown, so every unclosed session in events.jsonl counted as running. Self-check on console load and stuck ticks releases dead claims, expired limits and builds with no session; tests in claude-workers.test.mjs and pipeline.test.mjs; each release logged.
