# Build: pipeline-rebuild (orchestrator build ID: urgent-rebuild-pipeline-orchestrator-ids-splits-)

## Brett said (verbatim)
You need to start the pipeline over from scratch. From now on, what I say, send a build to the orchestrator. The orchestrator is going to assign an ID. A build ID. He's going to use you to break it up into steps select a model Babel or Opus Babel when it's needed and then he's going to see how many subscriptions are connected to the VPS how many accounts are available How many, what's the max parallel for each one? And uh, if it's a account that has Fable, he'll send the Fable to that. He'll send everything else to Opus. He will, no, he will check the BPS to see what accounts have what slots. Available parallel. Dish out the steps, okay? The steps are marked. We already have the rules for how the steps are marked down into a, in a progress pile and blah blah blah. Updated in real time because you have a monitor watching the progress files. And um, the orchestrator starts starts the head, headless. The orchestrator then sends it to the queue, or he sends it to pending. Yeah, he sends everything to the pending. And I have to send them from pending to queue.

## Addendum (Brett, voice)
The orchestrator doesn't start a headless session right away. If he has slots open, he grabs the next build in the queue and starts the headless session.

## Context found tonight
- The orchestrator (apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator) has NO launch code: nothing in it starts headless sessions. Only deploy/claude-headless.sh enqueues into agent-slots (framework/cli/agent-slots.mjs).
- Pending items are never auto-imported into the orchestrator; 'import' (orchestrator-core.mjs) only copies existing subPrompts, nothing splits.
- HARD RULE in force: no build starts without an orchestrator build ID (launcher enforces it).
- 'Launch builds without asking' (claude-settings) defaults off.
- Profiles were merged into 'all' on Nov 7; queue flagged needsReprocess.

## Do
1. Intake: every new pending item is auto-imported into the orchestrator with a build ID.
2. Split: the orchestrator calls Claude to split into <=30 min steps and pick Fable only where needed, Opus otherwise; write steps to the build.
3. Flow: builds sit in Pending until Brett moves them to Queue (no auto-queue).
4. Dispatcher: a loop in the orchestrator reads VPS accounts (deploy/claude-workers.mjs status, claude-login.mjs accounts): which have Fable, max parallel, free slots. When a slot is free it takes the next Queue build and starts a headless session through the existing launcher (claude-headless.sh / agent-slots), Fable steps to a Fable account, rest to Opus.
5. Progress: steps tick in the progress files per existing rules; the live monitor updates the console in real time.
6. Idle alert: AmberX phone notification when nothing is running while the Queue has work.
7. Tests, report _claude/builds/reports/pipeline-rebuild.md, THREADS, PR, steps through the store. Commits clean and professional.
## Addendum 2 (Brett, voice)
When the orchestrator splits a build and sends it to Pending, it also creates a plan in Plan Studio: a note describing the job, with a checklist of the steps, and a sub-note inside it holding Brett's prompt verbatim, with the part this build covers highlighted in a colour set in settings. Sessions are never stopped and rerun per step (saves tokens): instead, the last action of every step is to update the progress file. The orchestrator's listener watches the progress files and, on each change, ticks that step off and crosses it out in the Plan Studio checklist.

## Addendum 3 (Brett, voice)
The orchestrator writes each headless session's brief itself, with the least information possible: only the current step(s), the files it touches, and the rules it needs. No history, no full spec.

steps.text: Contract: add the `queued` status to builds@1 / orchestrator@1 / build-hook@1 (Pending → Queued → Building = running), a `pipeline` record on every build (account, session, runs, split, last run) kept across orchestrator writes, pending@1 shows queued as pending, derivedStatus keeps queued; fixtures and check-builds-store updated

pipeline-core.mjs (pure): account capabilities (which account has Fable, max parallel each, limits), the queue order, pick the account for a queued build's next phase, slot-open launch decision, session-end outcome (requeue / back to Pending / failed), idle reasons, the split prompt + step parser (≤30 min, Fable only where needed) and a rules-based fallback split

pipeline.mjs CLI (IO): status | queue | unqueue | split | intake | accounts | tick; store writes under the lock (queue/unqueue/pipeline record/steps from the split); splitter providers (claude -p on a login copy, AXF_PIPELINE_SPLITTER for tests, rules fallback); intake splits every new build with no steps

Dispatcher tick: read VPS accounts + agent slots, when a slot is free take the next Queue build, make its worktree + brief (Brett said block + phase brief), launch deploy/claude-headless.sh --account on a Fable account for Fable phases / Opus otherwise, mark running + account + session; monitor events.jsonl + slots for session end → built / requeue / Pending / failed, relaunch cap; dispatcher state file for the console; cron line in deploy/install-console.sh

Idle alert + notifications: notify.json types (pipeline.idle, pipeline.launched, pipeline.ended, pipeline.failed) raised through the console alerts API from the host (AmberX push for idle: nothing running while the Queue has work, with the reason), keyed and resolved when a build runs

Console: Pipeline tab on the Build orchestrator page (Pending / Queue / Building columns, accounts strip with Fable + parallel + running, dispatcher status, Queue / Back to Pending / Split now, live refresh while visible); server routes GET /pipeline, POST /pipeline/queue | unqueue | split; plugin commands for voice/MCP (queue a build, pipeline status); help entries; Launch builds without asking ON = new builds queue by themselves

Tests: check-pipeline.mjs end to end on a scratch store with a fake launcher, fake splitter and fake accounts (intake → Pending → Queue → launch on the right account → session end → built / requeue / failed, idle alert once, slot cap respected); python route test; CI wiring; plugin-lifecycle check; existing suites green

Close out: report _claude/builds/reports/pipeline-rebuild.md, _claude/builds/README.md Pipeline section, rules + decisions lines, THREADS row, fold the overlapping builds (idle-alert-phone-flag-when-nothing-is-building, orchestrator-start-a-build-through-the-api-mcp-and-cli) as complete with this PR, commit, push, PR, link the build

Expose via REST/MCP/CLI (build list includes behindMain). Builds with no branch show a dash.

before.title: Asset Designer plugin (no-code)
before.detail: No-code editors for nav menus, drawers, app menus, context menus, toolbars, layouts, style packs and color themes. Every asset validates against its schema before save. Adds a drawer asset type. Installed by default.

notes.text: Superseded in part by build ui-asset-designer (Current, Nov 7 2026, Fable): the menu editor (s5), toolbar editor (s6) and the generic designer shell / storage / validation gate are built from scratch there (designer@1 host + add-ons, framework/spec/DESIGNER.md). What stays here: the drawer asset type (s7, s8), layout editor (s9), colour-theme editor (s10), style-theme editor (s11); build them on the designer@1 host when picked up.
Merged from build profile "main-framework" into "all" (one profile for everything).

Audit: superseded — ui-asset-designer (built Nov 7: designer host plugin + add-ons for app menu, nav menu, toolbar, banner, embed, widgets) and context-menu-designer (complete Oct 25) cover it; the drawer type is in framework/schemas/asset-types.json
Shipped manifest sm-asset-designer rev 1 sent to Shipped features (backfill): complete 2026-11-10 (date inferred: no commit or PR recorded), 0 file(s), 0 test line(s), 16 open.

steps.text: Plugin skeleton: copy `apps/console-web/plugins/_template` to `plugins/asset-designer` (id `ai.amberx.axf.console.asset-designer`, `uiEditor: "builder"`, lifecycle block, `install.mjs`/`uninstall.mjs`), nav → Plugins → Asset designer, Settings → Plugins sub-tab (parent `plugins`). `node framework/cli/plugin-lifecycle.mjs check asset-designer` passes; console tsc + vite build pass.

Designer shell `web/Designer.tsx`: type picker (every non-attachable type from `asset-types.json` the designer covers: nav-menu, drawer, app-menu, context-menu, toolbar, layout, style-theme, color-theme), id + label fields, Save/Cancel; `useEditorSync()` so it reloads values on focus (UI-editor rule). Saves nothing yet.

Validation gate: every save runs `validateAsset` from the baked `src/axf/core/validate.ts`; errors shown inline next to the field they name; Save disabled until clean. Server route `POST /api/plugins/asset-designer/validate` mirrors it with the CLI validator (`framework/core/project-check.mjs` pattern). Test in `test.py`.

Storage: designed assets saved as asset@1 files under `.axf-console/plugins/asset-designer/assets/<type>/<id>.json` (lifecycle dataDir), served by `GET /api/plugins/asset-designer/assets`, registered into the runtime on load like the theme-manager plugin does (`registry.register`, origin `asset-designer`). Built-in ids refused.

Menu editor (nav-menu, app-menu, context-menu): tree of items (label, icon, action, children, divider), drag to reorder, action picker from `rt.actions.list()`, live preview via `rt.swap` on a `ad-preview-<type>` id. Reuses `MenuList.tsx` for the preview.

Toolbar editor: items (icon, label, action, badge counter), `density`/`surface`/`divider`/`collapsible`, widgets start/end picker from `attachable` types (engine-rpc `app-defaults` → `widgets`), live preview through the React `Toolbar`.

`drawer` asset type: add it to `asset-types.json` (hideable chrome, `side` left/right, `width`, `items` like nav-menu, `modal`), `layout.slots` accept it in the `drawer` region, starter `framework/assets/drawer/amberx-side.json`, `framework/defaults.json` names it. Validators on all three ports accept it (Kotlin: `AssetTypeSpec` resource); fixture case in `layout-slots.json`.

Drawer rendering: React `components/Chrome.tsx` draws the drawer region; Compose `axf-ui/components/Chrome.kt` the same (swipe from the edge, scrim from `--fx-opacity-scrim`). Drawer editor in the designer (same editor as nav-menu plus side/width/modal).

Layout editor: region grid (9 regions from `layout.slots`), per-region size/visibility, `data.slots` overrides with accepted-type chips; preview through `compileLayout`. Hidden slots greyed like Appearance does.

Color-theme editor: token groups from the theme engine (`core/engines/theme.ts` token list), colour pickers, contrast warnings (reuse `theme-manager/web/rollEngine.ts` checks), light/dark pair, preview via `rt.swap`.
Style-theme editor: space, radii, borders, font sizes, opacity tokens (`opacityDisabled/Muted/Hover/Tint/Scrim/Glass`), density; preview; numbers clamped to the ranges known themes use.

Templates hook: "Start from" picker listing starters + designed assets + (later) `x.assets.templates` entries; Duplicate / Rename / Export JSON / Import JSON (validated). Export writes a file a user can drop into an app's assets folder.

Installed by default: plugin `enabled: true` in the console's plugin defaults, `framework/catalog/plugins.json` entry (planned → built resolves by itself), `node framework/cli/plugins.mjs --check`, status.json + tracker; Plugin Manager shows it.

Android face (first slice): `axf-devtools` gets an `AssetDesignerModule` placeholder route `asset-designer` listing designed assets received from the console (read-only), so the plugin-inventory shows it on both ports; full editors stay web-only for now (noted as a placeholder capability `axf.designer`).

Tests: plugin `test.py` (validate route, storage, built-in id refused, lifecycle), web unit cases for the drawer slot + layout compile, CI line; `uninstall.mjs --all` leaves nothing (`check --after-uninstall`).

Close: differences report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/asset-designer.md` (new plugin, so a build report), LOG.md line, web screenshots via `rebuild-shots.mjs`, CLAUDE.md Status, plan epic `x.assets.designer` built via `build_step`, pending item complete.

Drawer rendering: React `components/Chrome.tsx` draws the drawer region; Compose `axf-ui/components/Chrome.kt` the same (swipe from the edge, scrim from `--fx-opacity-scrim`). Drawer editor in the designer (same editor as nav-menu plus side/width/modal).

Layout editor: region grid (9 regions from `layout.slots`), per-region size/visibility, `data.slots` overrides with accepted-type chips; preview through `compileLayout`. Hidden slots greyed like Appearance does.

Color-theme editor: token groups from the theme engine (`core/engines/theme.ts` token list), colour pickers, contrast warnings (reuse `theme-manager/web/rollEngine.ts` checks), light/dark pair, preview via `rt.swap`.
Style-theme editor: space, radii, borders, font sizes, opacity tokens (`opacityDisabled/Muted/Hover/Tint/Scrim/Glass`), density; preview; numbers clamped to the ranges known themes use.

Templates hook: "Start from" picker listing starters + designed assets + (later) `x.assets.templates` entries; Duplicate / Rename / Export JSON / Import JSON (validated). Export writes a file a user can drop into an app's assets folder.

Installed by default: plugin `enabled: true` in the console's plugin defaults, `framework/catalog/plugins.json` entry (planned → built resolves by itself), `node framework/cli/plugins.mjs --check`, status.json + tracker; Plugin Manager shows it.

Android face (first slice): `axf-devtools` gets an `AssetDesignerModule` placeholder route `asset-designer` listing designed assets received from the console (read-only), so the plugin-inventory shows it on both ports; full editors stay web-only for now (noted as a placeholder capability `axf.designer`).

Tests: plugin `test.py` (validate route, storage, built-in id refused, lifecycle), web unit cases for the drawer slot + layout compile, CI line; `uninstall.mjs --all` leaves nothing (`check --after-uninstall`).

Close: differences report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/asset-designer.md` (new plugin, so a build report), LOG.md line, web screenshots via `rebuild-shots.mjs`, CLAUDE.md Status, plan epic `x.assets.designer` built via `build_step`, pending item complete.

before.title: Running builds follow the active Claude account, fail over when it dies
before.detail:
## Brett said (verbatim)
Source: voice · At: 2026-11-06
> the running builds need to run on whatever account's connected. If, if the account dies, they need to switch over.
> Every time you log in with a refresh token, you need to update the refresh token.
> why doesn't it switch over? It needs to switch over on its own.

Context: claude_accounts_use to account-2 succeeded and marked it active, but the live VPS login stayed gizmox1111 (loginChanged: true) and the banner clock badge stayed gray. Reverses part of build-own-login (#357). Related: ai-keys-console-store (#358), console-account-picker. Check overlap first.

notes.text: The 'Save the rotated refresh token' steps are built by first-refresh-token-saved-every-time-it-s-used-v (PR #359): tick them once it merges, don't rebuild them.
The 'Save the rotated refresh token' steps are built by first-refresh-token-saved-every-time-it-s-used-v (PR #359): tick them once it merges, don't rebuild them.
Overlap (multi-account-headless-workers): failover is built for worker accounts. Following the active account is unchanged, and any switch must skip workers.
Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

Steps 3-5 (failover on limit/auth death, save rotated token back, banner/alert when no account is left) are built in account-failover-notify (branch claude/account-failover-notify). Steps 1-2 (switching the active account re-signs the VPS login; running builds follow the switch) remain.

Overlap: account-health-failover (PR #394) adds the shared account-status@1 store and capability axf.account-status@1 (able(name, model)): use it to pick the account to switch to instead of a new check.

Folded into account-failover-chain-subscription-next-subscri: pipeline runs now fail over subscription → next subscription → API (pipeline.mjs failover), never the console's account switch; who ran each part is recorded in pipeline.builtBy. Review what is left here once that PR lands.

Folded into account-failover-chain-subscription-next-subscri: a pipeline run whose account fails or hits its limit moves to the next subscription account, then an API account under its caps (pipeline.mjs failover); the account that ran it is recorded in pipeline.builtBy.
Moved to the Archive from pending (console).

Save the rotated refresh token back after every login/renew

before.title: Approvals: no window spam on Approve; veto only for VPS writes and account switches
before.detail:
## Brett said (verbatim)
Source: voice · At: 2026-11-06
> when I click approve and the consoles pop up, I don't want it to launch a window of access. It's opening a thousand fucking windows. And also you only need to send the veto rules that ask for approval or deny if you are actually writing something to the VPS or if you are switching accounts.
> All right, go ahead, build that shit.

Notes: touches Follow Amber approval pop-up (console) and axHub tool policies (veto vs allow). Changing which calls are veto is a policy change in axHub and the shared rule 'It's a veto system'; update rules + decisions.md to match.

notes.text: Overlap with claude-settings-tabs-veto (PR 371): its Approvals & veto tab is the tool for s2 / s5-4 (default plan: hold only VPS writes and account switches). Reconciler: paused: no live session or process runs it (worktree kept); was running

before.title: Headless session efficiency + shared chain control
before.detail: Follow-on to headless-progress-file-lean-claude-md-chain. Cut headless token spend and give Brett full, meticulous control over the CLAUDE.md chain. All settings live in a shared registry that both the Claude plugin and the Claude MD Studio plugin read and write (Brett, voice, Nov 6 2026).

notes.text: Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

origin.brief:
# Build: md-chain-control (pending item headless-session-efficiency-shared-chain-control)

Brett: finish the optimization in Claude MD Studio. The token log, rules briefs and headless-skips-CLAUDE.md work is on branch claude/token-optimize (PR open, not merged): merge origin/claude/token-optimize into this branch first and build on it; don't redo any of it.

That item lists every step twice; do each once:
1. Fresh session per step with a short handoff note from the progress file.
2. Per-step model choice suggested by the orchestrator.
3. Steps list the exact files they need; sessions read only those.
4. Trim long tool output (configurable caps).
5. Shared registry (schema + store + read/write API with change events) used by both the Claude plugin and Claude MD Studio.
6. Shared controls in both plugins: CLAUDE.md chain view in load order with size and tokens; per-file include/exclude and always / on demand / never, reorder, edit, preview; per-build and per-step overrides; session mode, handoff size, model rules; output caps, file scoping, token budget per step with warn/stop; live token cost preview; presets lean/normal/full, reset, history.
7. API, CLI and MCP for the registry.
8. Verify savings with the token log on a test build.

Stay out of apps/console-web/plugins/ai-keys and the Gizmo companion plugin (other builds). Don't load the full CLAUDE.md chain. Tick steps as they finish. PR, do not land.

Shared registry: schema + store for headless session config (chain files, load mode, session mode, model rules, output caps, file scoping)

# Build: molly-native-expenses

## Brett said (verbatim)
At: 2026-11-08T16:58:59.537Z
> Standalone apps keep working until Molly covers them; list gaps as pending builds.

## What to build
Continue build "Molly gap: Expense Tracker screens load natively in Molly (Next.js 16 / React 19 app today)" (molly-native-expenses) [Molly] — Phase 1, model Opus.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said (2026-11-08 16:58):
"Standalone apps keep working until Molly covers them; list gaps as pending builds."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 30 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. Watch live: when you start on a screen, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "…"` so the live preview follows you.

before.title: Demonstration Designer plugin (new, standalone)
before.detail: New standalone console plugin 'Demonstration Designer' (own nav entry), replacing the disabled glossary-index one. Brett found the old one unusable, so make it simple and obvious. Pick any screen, plugin or UI element from the live registry, then build a demo: steps (open screen, highlight, click/type action, wait), narration text + voice, captions, timing. Record a demo by doing it, edit it on a timeline, preview, play it live on the console or a sandboxed preview, export as video. Demos are saved assets, reusable and chainable into longer tours. Harvest useful code from the disabled glossary-index plugin (demos.mjs, walkthrough engine) instead of starting from zero. before.title: Fix: stale running counts per Claude account not cleared
before.detail: Seen Nov 9: claude_accounts shows Hulu 1/3, Moses X 4/3, account-1 4/3 running while the VPS has 0 tmux axf-* sessions and 0 claude -p processes. Rule (Brett): every time the console loads, and on the watchdog tick, the orchestrator checks for stale runs and releases any slot or running entry with no live process (agent-slots, claude-workers.mjs counts, orchestrator.json statuses). Find why the existing check didn't run or didn't clear these; fix; add a test with fake stale entries; log each release.

notes.text: ROOT CAUSE (found live): deploy/claude-workers.mjs liveSessions() runs `tmux ls`; when NO tmux sessions exist, tmux exits non-zero ('no server running'), so it returns null = 'can't ask tmux'. Then ledger() counts every open session as running and liveClaims keeps claims for 12 h. So the stale entries survive exactly when nothing is running. Fix: treat 'no server running' (tmux present, exit 1) as an empty Set; only return null when tmux binary is missing. Test it.

Root cause fixed in PR #406 (claude/orch-self-check-stuck): tmux 'no server running' was read as unknown, so every unclosed session in events.jsonl counted as running. Self-check on console load and stuck ticks releases dead claims, expired limits and builds with no session; tests in claude-workers.test.mjs and pipeline.test.mjs; each release logged.

# Build: pipeline-rebuild (orchestrator build ID: urgent-rebuild-pipeline-orchestrator-ids-splits-)

## Brett said (verbatim)
You need to start the pipeline over from scratch. From now on, what I say, send a build to the orchestrator. The orchestrator is going to assign an ID. A build ID. He's going to use you to break it up into steps select a model Babel or Opus Babel when it's needed and then he's going to see how many subscriptions are connected to the VPS how many accounts are available How many, what's the max parallel for each one? And uh, if it's a account that has Fable, he'll send the Fable to that. He'll send everything else to Opus. He will, no, he will check the BPS to see what accounts have what slots. Available parallel. Dish out the steps, okay? The steps are marked. We already have the rules for how the steps are marked down into a, in a progress pile and blah blah blah. Updated in real time because you have a monitor watching the progress files. And um, the orchestrator starts starts the head, headless. The orchestrator then sends it to the queue, or he sends it to pending. Yeah, he sends everything to the pending. And I have to send them from pending to queue.

## Addendum (Brett, voice)
The orchestrator doesn't start a headless session right away. If he has slots open, he grabs the next build in the queue and starts the headless session.

## Context found tonight
- The orchestrator (apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator) has NO launch code: nothing in it starts headless sessions. Only deploy/claude-headless.sh enqueues into agent-slots (framework/cli/agent-slots.mjs).
- Pending items are never auto-imported into the orchestrator; 'import' (orchestrator-core.mjs) only copies existing subPrompts, nothing splits.
- HARD RULE in force: no build starts without an orchestrator build ID (launcher enforces it).
- 'Launch builds without asking' (claude-settings) defaults off.
- Profiles were merged into 'all' on Nov 7; queue flagged needsReprocess.

## Do
1. Intake: every new pending item is auto-imported into the orchestrator with a build ID.
2. Split: the orchestrator calls Claude to split into <=30 min steps and pick Fable only where needed, Opus otherwise; write steps to the build.
3. Flow: builds sit in Pending until Brett moves them to Queue (no auto-queue).
4. Dispatcher: a loop in the orchestrator reads VPS accounts (deploy/claude-workers.mjs status, claude-login.mjs accounts): which have Fable, max parallel, free slots. When a slot is free it takes the next Queue build and starts a headless session through the existing launcher (claude-headless.sh / agent-slots), Fable steps to a Fable account, rest to Opus.
5. Progress: steps tick in the progress files per existing rules; the live monitor updates the console in real time.
6. Idle alert: AmberX phone notification when nothing is running while the Queue has work.
7. Tests, report _claude/builds/reports/pipeline-rebuild.md, THREADS, PR, steps through the store. Commits clean and professional.
## Addendum 2 (Brett, voice)
When the orchestrator splits a build and sends it to Pending, it also creates a plan in Plan Studio: a note describing the job, with a checklist of the steps, and a sub-note inside it holding Brett's prompt verbatim, with the part this build covers highlighted in a colour set in settings. Sessions are never stopped and rerun per step (saves tokens): instead, the last action of every step is to update the progress file. The orchestrator's listener watches the progress files and, on each change, ticks that step off and crosses it out in the Plan Studio checklist.

## Addendum 3 (Brett, voice)
The orchestrator writes each headless session's brief itself, with the least information possible: only the current step(s), the files it touches, and the rules it needs. No history, no full spec.

steps.text: Contract: add the `queued` status to builds@1 / orchestrator@1 / build-hook@1 (Pending → Queued → Building = running), a `pipeline` record on every build (account, session, runs, split, last run) kept across orchestrator writes, pending@1 shows queued as pending, derivedStatus keeps queued; fixtures and check-builds-store updated

pipeline-core.mjs (pure): account capabilities (which account has Fable, max parallel each, limits), the queue order, pick the account for a queued build's next phase, slot-open launch decision, session-end outcome (requeue / back to Pending / failed), idle reasons, the split prompt + step parser (≤30 min, Fable only where needed) and a rules-based fallback split

pipeline.mjs CLI (IO): status | queue | unqueue | split | intake | accounts | tick; store writes under the lock (queue/unqueue/pipeline record/steps from the split); splitter providers (claude -p on a login copy, AXF_PIPELINE_SPLITTER for tests, rules fallback); intake splits every new build with no steps

Dispatcher tick: read VPS accounts + agent slots, when a slot is free take the next Queue build, make its worktree + brief (Brett said block + phase brief), launch deploy/claude-headless.sh --account on a Fable account for Fable phases / Opus otherwise, mark running + account + session; monitor events.jsonl + slots for session end → built / requeue / Pending / failed, relaunch cap; dispatcher state file for the console; cron line in deploy/install-console.sh

Idle alert + notifications: notify.json types (pipeline.idle, pipeline.launched, pipeline.ended, pipeline.failed) raised through the console alerts API from the host (AmberX push for idle: nothing running while the Queue has work, with the reason), keyed and resolved when a build runs

Console: Pipeline tab on the Build orchestrator page (Pending / Queue / Building columns, accounts strip with Fable + parallel + running, dispatcher status, Queue / Back to Pending / Split now, live refresh while visible); server routes GET /pipeline, POST /pipeline/queue | unqueue | split; plugin commands for voice/MCP (queue a build, pipeline status); help entries; Launch builds without asking ON = new builds queue by themselves

Tests: check-pipeline.mjs end to end on a scratch store with a fake launcher, fake splitter and fake accounts (intake → Pending → Queue → launch on the right account → session end → built / requeue / failed, idle alert once, slot cap respected); python route test; CI wiring; plugin-lifecycle check; existing suites green

Close out: report _claude/builds/reports/pipeline-rebuild.md, _claude/builds/README.md Pipeline section, rules + decisions lines, THREADS row, fold the overlapping builds (idle-alert-phone-flag-when-nothing-is-building, orchestrator-start-a-build-through-the-api-mcp-and-cli) as complete with this PR, commit, push, PR, link the build

## Brett said (verbatim)
Source: voice · At: 2026-11-04T15:25:00Z
> Make Molly's top banner asset the same as console. And when console's open in Molly, don't display its own banner.

What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said (voice, 2026-11-04 15:25):
"Make Molly's top banner asset the same as console. And when console's open in Molly, don't display its own banner."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. steps.text: Plugin skeleton: copy `apps/console-web/plugins/_template` to `plugins/asset-designer` (id `ai.amberx.axf.console.asset-designer`, `uiEditor: "builder"`, lifecycle block, `install.mjs`/`uninstall.mjs`), nav → Plugins → Asset designer, Settings → Plugins sub-tab (parent `plugins`). `node framework/cli/plugin-lifecycle.mjs check asset-designer` passes; console tsc + vite build pass.

Designer shell `web/Designer.tsx`: type picker (every non-attachable type from `asset-types.json` the designer covers: nav-menu, drawer, app-menu, context-menu, toolbar, layout, style-theme, color-theme), id + label fields, Save/Cancel; `useEditorSync()` so it reloads values on focus (UI-editor rule). Saves nothing yet.

Validation gate: every save runs `validateAsset` from the baked `src/axf/core/validate.ts`; errors shown inline next to the field they name; Save disabled until clean. Server route `POST /api/plugins/asset-designer/validate` mirrors it with the CLI validator (`framework/core/project-check.mjs` pattern). Test in `test.py`.

Storage: designed assets saved as asset@1 files under `.axf-console/plugins/asset-designer/assets/<type>/<id>.json` (lifecycle dataDir), served by `GET /api/plugins/asset-designer/assets`, registered into the runtime on load like the theme-manager plugin does (`registry.register`, origin `asset-designer`). Built-in ids refused.

Menu editor (nav-menu, app-menu, context-menu): tree of items (label, icon, action, children, divider), drag to reorder, action picker from `rt.actions.list()`, live preview via `rt.swap` on a `ad-preview-<type>` id. Reuses `MenuList.tsx` for the preview.

Toolbar editor: items (icon, label, action, badge counter), `density`/`surface`/`divider`/`collapsible`, widgets start/end picker from `attachable` types (engine-rpc `app-defaults` → `widgets`), live preview through the React `Toolbar`.

`drawer` asset type: add it to `asset-types.json` (hideable chrome, `side` left/right, `width`, `items` like nav-menu, `modal`), `layout.slots` accept it in the `drawer` region, starter `framework/assets/drawer/amberx-side.json`, `framework/defaults.json` names it. Validators on all three ports accept it (Kotlin: `AssetTypeSpec` resource); fixture case in `layout-slots.json`.

Drawer rendering: React `components/Chrome.tsx` draws the drawer region; Compose `axf-ui/components/Chrome.kt` the same (swipe from the edge, scrim from `--fx-opacity-scrim`). Drawer editor in the designer (same editor as nav-menu plus side/width/modal).

Layout editor: region grid (9 regions from `layout.slots`), per-region size/visibility, `data.slots` overrides with accepted-type chips; preview through `compileLayout`. Hidden slots greyed like Appearance does.

Color-theme editor: token groups from the theme engine (`core/engines/theme.ts` token list), colour pickers, contrast warnings (reuse `theme-manager/web/rollEngine.ts` checks), light/dark pair, preview via `rt.swap`.
Style-theme editor: space, radii, borders, font sizes, opacity tokens (`opacityDisabled/Muted/Hover/Tint/Scrim/Glass`), density; preview; numbers clamped to the ranges known themes use.

Templates hook: "Start from" picker listing starters + designed assets + (later) `x.assets.templates` entries; Duplicate / Rename / Export JSON / Import JSON (validated). Export writes a file a user can drop into an app's assets folder.

Installed by default: plugin `enabled: true` in the console's plugin defaults, `framework/catalog/plugins.json` entry (planned → built resolves by itself), `node framework/cli/plugins.mjs --check`, status.json + tracker; Plugin Manager shows it.

Android face (first slice): `axf-devtools` gets an `AssetDesignerModule` placeholder route `asset-designer` listing designed assets received from the console (read-only), so the plugin-inventory shows it on both ports; full editors stay web-only for now (noted as a placeholder capability `axf.designer`).

Tests: plugin `test.py` (validate route, storage, built-in id refused, lifecycle), web unit cases for the drawer slot + layout compile, CI line; `uninstall.mjs --all` leaves nothing (`check --after-uninstall`).

Close: differences report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/asset-designer.md` (new plugin, so a build report), LOG.md line, web screenshots via `rebuild-shots.mjs`, CLAUDE.md Status, plan epic `x.assets.designer` built via `build_step`, pending item complete.

before.title: Running builds follow the active Claude account, fail over when it dies
before.detail:
## Brett said (verbatim)
Source: voice · At: 2026-11-06
> the running builds need to run on whatever account's connected. If, if the account dies, they need to switch over.
> Every time you log in with a refresh token, you need to update the refresh token.
> why doesn't it switch over? It needs to switch over on its own.

Context: claude_accounts_use to account-2 succeeded and marked it active, but the live VPS login stayed gizmox1111 (loginChanged: true) and the banner clock badge stayed gray. Reverses part of build-own-login (#357). Related: ai-keys-console-store (#358), console-account-picker. Check overlap first.

notes.text: The 'Save the rotated refresh token' steps are built by first-refresh-token-saved-every-time-it-s-used-v (PR #359): tick them once it merges, don't rebuild them.
The 'Save the rotated refresh token' steps are built by first-refresh-token-saved-every-time-it-s-used-v (PR #359): tick them once it merges, don't rebuild them.
Overlap (multi-account-headless-workers): failover is built for worker accounts. Following the active account is unchanged, and any switch must skip workers.
Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

before.title: Demonstration Designer plugin (new, standalone)
before.detail: New standalone console plugin 'Demonstration Designer' (own nav entry), replacing the disabled glossary-index one. Brett found the old one unusable, so make it simple and obvious. Pick any screen, plugin or UI element from the live registry, then build a demo: steps (open screen, highlight, click/type action, wait), narration text + voice, captions, timing. Record a demo by doing it, edit it on a timeline, preview, play it live on the console or a sandboxed preview, export as video. Demos are saved assets, reusable and chainable into longer tours. Harvest useful code from the disabled glossary-index plugin (demos.mjs, walkthrough engine) instead of starting from zero. RULE: every UI action and setting has API + voice + MCP/CLI control, and a deep link opens it. Settings in categorized collapsible sections; 3 UI options to UI Review; tests; report.

notes.text: PURPOSE (Brett): it's for PITCHING the product. Keep it dead simple. Main flow = three picks: (1) plugin or topic, (2) length in minutes, (3) narrator voice; then ONE Generate button. Generate writes a pitch script (hook up front, benefits not specs, closing call to action), picks the best screens, and plays a polished demo on real data: highlights, smooth zooms/pans, captions, background music, logo intro/outro. After: optional script tweak, preview, export video (MP4) or share link. Advanced editing (timeline, record-by-doing) stays tucked behind an Advanced section, never in the main flow.
Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.
Queued by cli.

Brett: "Why doesn't the exported video have the narrator's voice? AmberX can screen record it." Phase 1 export uses browser speech, which Chrome doesn't route into tab capture, so videos have captions and music but no voice. Fix: add an export option 'Record on AmberX': the demo plays on Brett's phone and AmberX records it with the narration audio (reuse AmberX's Audio Output Recorder, extend it to screen + app audio), then uploads the video back to the demo asset. Also a default export path that doesn't need the phone: generate the narration as real audio (a TTS voice) and mix it into the exported MP4. Full API/MCP/CLI/voice control.

before.title: Fix: stale running counts per Claude account not cleared
before.detail: Seen Nov 9: claude_accounts shows Hulu 1/3, Moses X 4/3, account-1 4/3 running while the VPS has 0 tmux axf-* sessions and 0 claude -p processes. Rule (Brett): every time the console loads, and on the watchdog tick, the orchestrator checks for stale runs and releases any slot or running entry with no live process (agent-slots, claude-workers.mjs counts, orchestrator.json statuses). Find why the existing check didn't run or didn't clear these; fix; add a test with fake stale entries; log each release.

notes.text: ROOT CAUSE (found live): deploy/claude-workers.mjs liveSessions() runs `tmux ls`; when NO tmux sessions exist, tmux exits non-zero ('no server running'), so it returns null = 'can't ask tmux'. Then ledger() counts every open session as running and liveClaims keeps claims for 12 h. So the stale entries survive exactly when nothing is running. Fix: treat 'no server running' (tmux present, exit 1) as an empty Set; only return null when tmux binary is missing. Test it.

Root cause fixed in PR #406 (claude/orch-self-check-stuck): tmux 'no server running' was read as unknown, so every unclosed session in events.jsonl counted as running. Self-check on console load and stuck ticks releases dead claims, expired limits and builds with no session; tests in claude-workers.test.mjs and pipeline.test.mjs; each release logged.

steps.text: Plugin skeleton: copy `apps/console-web/plugins/_template` to `plugins/asset-designer` (id `ai.amberx.axf.console.asset-designer`, `uiEditor: "builder"`, lifecycle block, `install.mjs`/`uninstall.mjs`), nav → Plugins → Asset designer, Settings → Plugins sub-tab (parent `plugins`). `node framework/cli/plugin-lifecycle.mjs check asset-designer` passes; console tsc + vite build pass.

Designer shell `web/Designer.tsx`: type picker (every non-attachable type from `asset-types.json` the designer covers: nav-menu, drawer, app-menu, context-menu, toolbar, layout, style-theme, color-theme), id + label fields, Save/Cancel; `useEditorSync()` so it reloads values on focus (UI-editor rule). Saves nothing yet.

Validation gate: every save runs `validateAsset` from the baked `src/axf/core/validate.ts`; errors shown inline next to the field they name; Save disabled until clean. Server route `POST /api/plugins/asset-designer/validate` mirrors it with the CLI validator (`framework/core/project-check.mjs` pattern). Test in `test.py`.

Storage: designed assets saved as asset@1 files under `.axf-console/plugins/asset-designer/assets/<type>/<id>.json` (lifecycle dataDir), served by `GET /api/plugins/asset-designer/assets`, registered into the runtime on load like the theme-manager plugin does (`registry.register`, origin `asset-designer`). Built-in ids refused.

Menu editor (nav-menu, app-menu, context-menu): tree of items (label, icon, action, children, divider), drag to reorder, action picker from `rt.actions.list()`, live preview via `rt.swap` on a `ad-preview-<type>` id. Reuses `MenuList.tsx` for the preview.

Toolbar editor: items (icon, label, action, badge counter), `density`/`surface`/`divider`/`collapsible`, widgets start/end picker from `attachable` types (engine-rpc `app-defaults` → `widgets`), live preview through the React `Toolbar`.

`drawer` asset type: add it to `asset-types.json` (hideable chrome, `side` left/right, `width`, `items` like nav-menu, `modal`), `layout.slots` accept it in the `drawer` region, starter `framework/assets/drawer/amberx-side.json`, `framework/defaults.json` names it. Validators on all three ports accept it (Kotlin: `AssetTypeSpec` resource); fixture case in `layout-slots.json`.

Drawer rendering: React `components/Chrome.tsx` draws the drawer region; Compose `axf-ui/components/Chrome.kt` the same (swipe from the edge, scrim from `--fx-opacity-scrim`). Drawer editor in the designer (same editor as nav-menu plus side/width/modal).

Layout editor: region grid (9 regions from `layout.slots`), per-region size/visibility, `data.slots` overrides with accepted-type chips; preview through `compileLayout`. Hidden slots greyed like Appearance does.

Color-theme editor: token groups from the theme engine (`core/engines/theme.ts` token list), colour pickers, contrast warnings (reuse `theme-manager/web/rollEngine.ts` checks), light/dark pair, preview via `rt.swap`.
Style-theme editor: space, radii, borders, font sizes, opacity tokens (`opacityDisabled/Muted/Hover/Tint/Scrim/Glass`), density; preview; numbers clamped to the ranges known themes use.

Templates hook: "Start from" picker listing starters + designed assets + (later) `x.assets.templates` entries; Duplicate / Rename / Export JSON / Import JSON (validated). Export writes a file a user can drop into an app's assets folder.

Installed by default: plugin `enabled: true` in the console's plugin defaults, `framework/catalog/plugins.json` entry (planned → built resolves by itself), `node framework/cli/plugins.mjs --check`, status.json + tracker; Plugin Manager shows it.

Android face (first slice): `axf-devtools` gets an `AssetDesignerModule` placeholder route `asset-designer` listing designed assets received from the console (read-only), so the plugin-inventory shows it on both ports; full editors stay web-only for now (noted as a placeholder capability `axf.designer`).

Tests: plugin `test.py` (validate route, storage, built-in id refused, lifecycle), web unit cases for the drawer slot + layout compile, CI line; `uninstall.mjs --all` leaves nothing (`check --after-uninstall`).

Close: differences report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/asset-designer.md` (new plugin, so a build report), LOG.md line, web screenshots via `rebuild-shots.mjs`, CLAUDE.md Status, plan epic `x.assets.designer` built via `build_step`, pending item complete.

before.title: Running builds follow the active Claude account, fail over when it dies
before.detail:
## Brett said (verbatim)
Source: voice · At: 2026-11-06
> the running builds need to run on whatever account's connected. If, if the account dies, they need to switch over.
> Every time you log in with a refresh token, you need to update the refresh token.
> why doesn't it switch over? It needs to switch over on its own.

Context: claude_accounts_use to account-2 succeeded and marked it active, but the live VPS login stayed gizmox1111 (loginChanged: true) and the banner clock badge stayed gray. Reverses part of build-own-login (#357). Related: ai-keys-console-store (#358), console-account-picker. Check overlap first.

notes.text: The 'Save the rotated refresh token' steps are built by first-refresh-token-saved-every-time-it-s-used-v (PR #359): tick them once it merges, don't rebuild them.
The 'Save the rotated refresh token' steps are built by first-refresh-token-saved-every-time-it-s-used-v (PR #359): tick them once it merges, don't rebuild them.
Overlap (multi-account-headless-workers): failover is built for worker accounts. Following the active account is unchanged, and any switch must skip workers.
Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

Steps 3-5 (failover on limit/auth death, save rotated token back, banner/alert when no account is left) are built in account-failover-notify (branch claude/account-failover-notify). Steps 1-2 (switching the active account re-signs the VPS login; running builds follow the switch) remain.

Overlap: account-health-failover (PR #394) adds the shared account-status@1 store and capability axf.account-status@1 (able(name, model)): use it to pick the account to switch to instead of a new check.

Folded into account-failover-chain-subscription-next-subscri: pipeline runs now fail over subscription → next subscription → API (pipeline.mjs failover), never the console's account switch; who ran each part is recorded in pipeline.builtBy. Review what is left here once that PR lands.

Folded into account-failover-chain-subscription-next-subscri: a pipeline run whose account fails or hits its limit moves to the next subscription account, then an API account under its caps (pipeline.mjs failover); the account that ran it is recorded in pipeline.builtBy.
Moved to the Archive from pending (console).

Save the rotated refresh token back after every login/renew

Source: voice · At: 2026-11-06

Reconciler: paused: no live session or process runs it (worktree kept); was running

before.title: Headless session efficiency + shared chain control
before.detail: Follow-on to headless-progress-file-lean-claude-md-chain. Cut headless token spend and give Brett full, meticulous control over the CLAUDE.md chain. All settings live in a shared registry that both the Claude plugin and the Claude MD Studio plugin read and write (Brett, voice, Nov 6 2026).

notes.text: Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

origin.brief:
# Build: md-chain-control (pending item headless-session-efficiency-shared-chain-control)

Brett: finish the optimization in Claude MD Studio. The token log, rules briefs and headless-skips-CLAUDE.md work is on branch claude/token-optimize (PR open, not merged): merge origin/claude/token-optimize into this branch first and build on it; don't redo any of it.

That item lists every step twice; do each once:
1. Fresh session per step with a short handoff note from the progress file.
2. Per-step model choice suggested by the orchestrator.
3. Steps list the exact files they need; sessions read only those.
4. Trim long tool output (configurable caps).
5. Shared registry (schema + store + read/write API with change events) used by both the Claude plugin and Claude MD Studio.
6. Shared controls in both plugins: CLAUDE.md chain view in load order with size and tokens; per-file include/exclude and always / on demand / never, reorder, edit, preview; per-build and per-step overrides; session mode, handoff size, model rules; output caps, file scoping, token budget per step with warn/stop; live token cost preview; presets lean/normal/full, reset, history.
7. API, CLI and MCP for the registry.
8. Verify savings with the token log on a test build.

Stay out of apps/console-web/plugins/ai-keys and the Gizmo companion plugin (other builds). Don't load the full CLAUDE.md chain. Tick steps as they finish. PR, do not land.

Per-step model choice: Haiku/Sonnet for simple steps, Opus for hard ones; orchestrator suggests a model per step
Steps list exact files they need; session reads only those instead of exploring the repo
Trim tool output: cap long logs/command output before it returns to the model (configurable limits)
Shared registry: schema + store for headless session config (chain files, load mode, session mode, model rules, output caps, file scoping)
Shared registry: read/write API used by both Claude plugin and Claude MD Studio plugin, with change events so both stay in sync
Shared control components (usable in both plugins): CLAUDE.md chain view - every file in load order with size and token count

before.detail: New standalone console plugin 'Demonstration Designer' (own nav entry), replacing the disabled glossary-index one. Brett found the old one unusable, so make it simple and obvious. Pick any screen, plugin or UI element from the live registry, then build a demo: steps (open screen, highlight, click/type action, wait), narration text + voice, captions, timing. Record a demo by doing it, edit it on a timeline, preview, play it live on the console or a sandboxed preview, export as video. Demos are saved assets, reusable and chainable into longer tours. Harvest useful code from the disabled glossary-index plugin (demos.mjs, walkthrough engine) instead of starting from zero. RULE: every UI action and setting has API + voice + MCP/CLI control, and a deep link opens it. Settings in categorized collapsible sections; 3 UI options to UI Review; tests; report.

notes.text: PURPOSE (Brett): it's for PITCHING the product. Keep it dead simple. Main flow = three picks: (1) plugin or topic, (2) length in minutes, (3) narrator voice; then ONE Generate button. Generate writes a pitch script (hook up front, benefits not specs, closing call to action), picks the best screens, and plays a polished demo on real data: highlights, smooth zooms/pans, captions, background music, logo intro/outro. After: optional script tweak, preview, export video (MP4) or share link. Advanced editing (timeline, record-by-doing) stays tucked behind an Advanced section, never in the main flow.
Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.

Also a default export path that doesn't need the phone: generate the narration as real audio (a TTS voice) and mix it into the exported MP4. Full API/MCP/CLI/voice control.

before.title: Fix: stale running counts per Claude account not cleared
before.detail: Seen Nov 9: claude_accounts shows Hulu 1/3, Moses X 4/3, account-1 4/3 running while the VPS has 0 tmux axf-* sessions and 0 claude -p processes. Rule (Brett): every time the console loads, and on the watchdog tick, the orchestrator checks for stale runs and releases any slot or running entry with no live process (agent-slots, claude-workers.mjs counts, orchestrator.json statuses). Find why the existing check didn't run or didn't clear these; fix; add a test with fake stale entries; log each release.

notes.text: ROOT CAUSE (found live): deploy/claude-workers.mjs liveSessions() runs `tmux ls`; when NO tmux sessions exist, tmux exits non-zero ('no server running'), so it returns null = 'can't ask tmux'. Then ledger() counts every open session as running and liveClaims keeps claims for 12 h. So the stale entries survive exactly when nothing is running. Fix: treat 'no server running' (tmux present, exit 1) as an empty Set; only return null when tmux binary is missing. Test it.

Root cause fixed in PR #406 (claude/orch-self-check-stuck): tmux 'no server running' was read as unknown, so every unclosed session in events.jsonl counted as running. Self-check on console load and stuck ticks releases dead claims, expired limits and builds with no session; tests in claude-workers.test.mjs and pipeline.test.mjs; each release logged.

# Build: pipeline-rebuild (orchestrator build ID: urgent-rebuild-pipeline-orchestrator-ids-splits-)

## Brett said (verbatim)
You need to start the pipeline over from scratch. From now on, what I say, send a build to the orchestrator. The orchestrator is going to assign an ID. A build ID. He's going to use you to break it up into steps select a model Babel or Opus Babel when it's needed and then he's going to see how many subscriptions are connected to the VPS how many accounts are available How many, what's the max parallel for each one? And uh, if it's a account that has Fable, he'll send the Fable to that. He'll send everything else to Opus. He will, no, he will check the BPS to see what accounts have what slots. Available parallel. Dish out the steps, okay? The steps are marked. We already have the rules for how the steps are marked down into a, in a progress pile and blah blah blah. Updated in real time because you have a monitor watching the progress files. And um, the orchestrator starts starts the head, headless. The orchestrator then sends it to the queue, or he sends it to pending. Yeah, he sends everything to the pending. And I have to send them from pending to queue.

## Addendum (Brett, voice)
The orchestrator doesn't start a headless session right away. If he has slots open, he grabs the next build in the queue and starts the headless session.

## Context found tonight
- The orchestrator (apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator) has NO launch code: nothing in it starts headless sessions. Only deploy/claude-headless.sh enqueues into agent-slots (framework/cli/agent-slots.mjs).
- Pending items are never auto-imported into the orchestrator; 'import' (orchestrator-core.mjs) only copies existing subPrompts, nothing splits.
- HARD RULE in force: no build starts without an orchestrator build ID (launcher enforces it).
- 'Launch builds without asking' (claude-settings) defaults off.
- Profiles were merged into 'all' on Nov 7; queue flagged needsReprocess.

## Do
1. Intake: every new pending item is auto-imported into the orchestrator with a build ID.
2. Split: the orchestrator calls Claude to split into <=30 min steps and pick Fable only where needed, Opus otherwise; write steps to the build.
3. Flow: builds sit in Pending until Brett moves them to Queue (no auto-queue).
4. Dispatcher: a loop in the orchestrator reads VPS accounts (deploy/claude-workers.mjs status, claude-login.mjs accounts): which have Fable, max parallel, free slots. When a slot is free it takes the next Queue build and starts a headless session through the existing launcher (claude-headless.sh / agent-slots), Fable steps to a Fable account, rest to Opus.
5. Progress: steps tick in the progress files per existing rules; the live monitor updates the console in real time.
6. Idle alert: AmberX phone notification when nothing is running while the Queue has work.
7. Tests, report _claude/builds/reports/pipeline-rebuild.md, THREADS, PR, steps through the store. Commits clean and professional.
## Addendum 2 (Brett, voice)
When the orchestrator splits a build and sends it to Pending, it also creates a plan in Plan Studio: a note describing the job, with a checklist of the steps, and a sub-note inside it holding Brett's prompt verbatim, with the part this build covers highlighted in a colour set in settings. Sessions are never stopped and rerun per step (saves tokens): instead, the last action of every step is to update the progress file. The orchestrator's listener watches the progress files and, on each change, ticks that step off and crosses it out in the Plan Studio checklist.

## Addendum 3 (Brett, voice)
The orchestrator writes each headless session's brief itself, with the least information possible: only the current step(s), the files it touches, and the rules it needs. No history, no full spec.

steps.text: Contract: add the `queued` status to builds@1 / orchestrator@1 / build-hook@1 (Pending → Queued → Building = running), a `pipeline` record on every build (account, session, runs, split, last run) kept across orchestrator writes, pending@1 shows queued as pending, derivedStatus keeps queued; fixtures and check-builds-store updated

pipeline-core.mjs (pure): account capabilities (which account has Fable, max parallel each, limits), the queue order, pick the account for a queued build's next phase, slot-open launch decision, session-end outcome (requeue / back to Pending / failed), idle reasons, the split prompt + step parser (≤30 min, Fable only where needed) and a rules-based fallback split

pipeline.mjs CLI (IO): status | queue | unqueue | split | intake | accounts | tick; store writes under the lock (queue/unqueue/pipeline record/steps from the split); splitter providers (claude -p on a login copy, AXF_PIPELINE_SPLITTER for tests, rules fallback); intake splits every new build with no steps

Dispatcher tick: read VPS accounts + agent slots, when a slot is free take the next Queue build, make its worktree + brief (Brett said block + phase brief), launch deploy/claude-headless.sh --account on a Fable account for Fable phases / Opus otherwise, mark running + account + session; monitor events.jsonl + slots for session end → built / requeue / Pending / failed, relaunch cap; dispatcher state file for the console; cron line in deploy/install-console.sh

Idle alert + notifications: notify.json types (pipeline.idle, pipeline.launched, pipeline.ended, pipeline.failed) raised through the console alerts API from the host (AmberX push for idle: nothing running while the Queue has work, with the reason), keyed and resolved when a build runs

Console: Pipeline tab on the Build orchestrator page (Pending / Queue / Building columns, accounts strip with Fable + parallel + running, dispatcher status, Queue / Back to Pending / Split now, live refresh while visible); server routes GET /pipeline, POST /pipeline/queue | unqueue | split; plugin commands for voice/MCP (queue a build, pipeline status); help entries; Launch builds without asking ON = new builds queue by themselves

Tests: check-pipeline.mjs end to end on a scratch store with a fake launcher, fake splitter and fake accounts (intake → Pending → Queue → launch on the right account → session end → built / requeue / failed, idle alert once, slot cap respected); python route test; CI wiring; plugin-lifecycle check; existing suites green

Close out: report _claude/builds/reports/pipeline-rebuild.md, _claude/builds/README.md Pipeline section, rules + decisions lines, THREADS row, fold the overlapping builds (idle-alert-phone-flag-when-nothing-is-building, orchestrator-start-a-build-through-the-api-mcp-and-cli) as complete with this PR, commit, push, PR, link the build
